excels in almost every aspect of the kart racing genre. The drifting feels natural, the tracks are varied, the weapons are interesting and fair, and the boosting mechanics are great fun to exploit. Where it suffers somewhat is in the character selection - Sonic and company are great, but the rest of the roster is padded with significantly less recognizable entries. Overall a well polished kart racer.
The games’ mechanics are well thought-out. Everything works well together:
* Boosts can be gained from drifting, boost pads, and doing tricks while in mid air. You are rewarded for chaining different types of boosts together, which makes you always on the lookout for trick/drift opportunities.
* Weapons are powerful, but they always leave the targeted player with some recourse to deal with them. All automatically tracking weapons can be boosted away from if timed correctly, and nearly all other weapons can be dodged in some way.
* Tracks are dynamic and sometimes will change from lap to lap. Tracks generally will have different paths to choose from, each offering either extra boosts, extra trick jumps/drifts, or extra weapon pickups.
Kart racing games are often a party game, and this is where Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed might fall short for you. The fact is most people are familiar with Mario Kart. Plumbers, princesses and shells are recognizable to the casual gamer and that familiarity can make a game much easier to get in to. Sonic Racing's monkeys, fireworks and pufferfish aren't as familiar to people, and until a player gets a feel for how the world and the weapons work the well-crafted mechanics will be lost on them.
Still, the bottom line is that it feels good to drive your boat/plane/car around; flipping, drifting, boosting and shooting your way to victory. Recommended.

Put in over a 100 hours in both the original and in Escalation which is a lot for me so I certainly consider this to be a decent game.
For SP there are many maps and skirmish setup options as well as just over 30 SP missions across several campaigns, with further scenario stand-alone missions on top of those. I've not actually completed the campaigns (yet) as most of my time has been spent in MP which has been a lot of fun. There is 1v1 ranked, 1v1 non-ranked and custom games. I have had the most fun in the custom games.
The game is still being actively worked on. A free campaign with some new large units was recently added and another one is on the way which should add 2 more Dreadnoughts and 2 more Juggernauts.
Navy, which I feel this game would greatly benefit from, is also coming further down the line.
Graphically speaking my experience is mixed. When you have a big battle going on and then air support whizzes over and and all sorts of stuff is shooting off it can look really good and feel pretty atmospheric. Other times it can look a bit bland. A graphics update of some sort is coming and also I think when water hits and assuming it is done well it should make the maps look better and just more interesting to look at. As is stands though it is still fine. I've seen the game played on a 4k screen too and have to say it does make quite a difference and does look really nice.
Following this game from the very beginning has sometimes been frustrating as the base game had some feature and technical deficit at release and development has not always been as fast as I would like. However since then many things have been added: more map types, larger maps with the ability to play with many more AI or people, more AI behaviour types, more skirmish options, more units, structures and orbital abilities, more missions, more control options (though not enough yet), and functions like observer mode and replays. So if you are buying the game now it is a pretty feature complete experience.
I would really like to see more control options that games like TA and Supcom have. I would like more atmospheric battlefields with varied building explosions and unit wreckage (both promised features from long ago at this point). After navy is done I hope another faction is not so far behind and with more unit locomotion variety than currently exists. I would also like it to be totally bug free at this point tbh. Better mod support for the modders also, but apparently this is happening at the moment so that is good. Steam support for map and scenario sharing is coming which is also very welcome. Vulcan on the way too which should be interesting to see, especially for Win7 users.
Anyway, this was originally going to be a one sentence review as few people read these things but there you go. It is a decent streaming economy based RTS with base building which is built to support large battles on big maps. I recommend playing with family/friends.

This is one of the best kart racers I've ever played.   I'm not a huge kart racing game fan, but I've played all the classics like Mario Kart 64, Diddy Kong Racing, and Double Dash.  This game is very much like combining all 3 of those games into one big package, while still mixing it up enough to have it's own feel.
-30+ Characters
-Performance Customization for Karts
-Several Gameplay Modes
-Online & Local Multiplayer
-Cheap DLC
-High Difficulty
-Grindy
You transform your kart on the fly during races by going through transformation parts on the track, but you can also perform tricks that will give you a speed boost during transformations and also during any air time.  Go off a ramp, do a trick, get a boost.  If you fail the trick you will slow down.
Tricks are performed simply by flicking the Right Analog stick on the controller, and depending on the direction you will do different tricks.  Doing a certain trick at a specific moment can make or break your race.  E.G. Do a right flip, to move to the right in mid air so you can avoid a wall or a fall.
There are several characters to choose from, each has their own strengths and weaknesses.  Sonic is one of the faster characters, but he has trouble turning while Amy has easy turns and acceleration but is not as fast.  You can also unlock up to 5 (6 total) mods for each character that will change up their stats.  Example, you can get a mod for Sonic that will lower his speed but increase his acceleration and turning.  This way you can play your favorite character on any track as long as you have the mod required for that character best suited for said track.
Mods are unlocked simply by playing your characters and leveling them up.  They earn experience for every race played, including in online matches.  There are lots of characters and this can actually feel like a grind but if you only play 1 or 2 characters it's fairly easy to max their level.  I haven't played very long but I have Sonic and Shadow both at max level.  The DLC characters automatically come at max level with all mods unlocked.
There are several tracks to choose from, but most need to be unlocked in the campaign mode.  The campaign mode is a simple follow the path to unlock the next track.  You earn stars for each race you complete, and higher ranking races earn you more stars.  I recommend simply playing the highest rank at all times mostly because those stars are needed to progress.  You need to spend stars to unlock new characters, tracks, and certain mods.
All in all, this game is great and if you are a Kart Racing fan you will definately want to pick this one up.  Don't bother getting the console version either since they are no longer supported by the devs.  PC version has more characters, tracks, and extra DLC.

Sonic And Sega All Stars Racing Transformed is a great game for not only Sega fans, but for racing game fans as a whole. It improves on the mechanics of the previous title in this series (Sonic And Sega All Stars Racing) while also adding all new, very unique mechanics that have been well polished and certainly well implemented.
-Graphics-
This game looks absolutely beqautiful! Transitions between the different vehicle forms are smooth (at least for the original characters like Sonic) and the forms themselves also look very good. There are a few draw distance issues with shadows and such, and character models aren't the best; but overall it is a very good looking game.
On top of that, it runs very smoothly (on medium to high settings) on my $600 laptop (very good considering).
-Gameplay-
This game is very fun in that it has a large variety of vehicles (characters) and tracks as well as game modes. Plus some fun power-ups at your desposal.
Vehicles (characters): The vehicles all have there own play style. Some more focused on speed or boost, others on handling or acceleration. And you can change this up even further with vehicle mods that you are rewarded through leveling up or through finding them in the single player campain. Plus, those play styles are changed beyond that in the different vehicle forms (bat, plane, and car). Planes are the fastest overall, cars are the middle ground in speed but (at least from personal experience) have the best handling and drift, and boats are the slowest and the hardest to handle (especially when getting tossed around by large waves). You can also get free boosts by taking advantage of the game's simple trick system.
Tracks: In total this game contains 20 different tracks (each with multiple froms for different modes). One special thing about them is that (unlike in most other racing games) these tracks change as the race progresses, adding more obstacles or even forcing you to go a lap in a different vehicle mode all together. They are very exciting to play around in and can offer quite a challenge to master.
Game Modes: This game has a total of 6 different game modes. You have a single player campain, grand prix, single race, time trials for lap times, split-screen multiplayer, and online multiplyer. This makes sure that the game has plenty of replayablity, as with so many different game modes and all the things each of them offer, you'll be finding yourself unable to stop playing for quite some time.
Power-ups: These are the big equaliser. They aren't very powerful (exect for the very rare All Star move) and are very limited in duration (again, exept All Stars). But there are planty of them and when used correctly can give you a major upper hand, however it can also backfire as all of them are fairly easy to dodge or outrun (even the homing type attacks). If you rely souly on them, you are going to have a very hard time doing good at this game as simply using power-ups is only enough to get you a small amount of time to overtake racers, you must also master the tracks as well as the different mechanics in order to do good.
-Is it worth it?-
In my opinion, yes.
It is fun in every aspect it sets out to be; it has tons of replayability (he large variety of vehicles (characters), tracks, power-ups, and game modes is a big factor to that.), the focus on skill rather than luck, the beautiful graphics; all of this ties into one of the best mascot racing games (or maybe even one of the best racing games in general) of the previous generation and I highly suggest you pick it up if you haven't already.

Aaah, bliss! This brings back the good ol memories!!
I remember Wolf 3D was one of the first games I ever played. Those days, the graphics were as good as it could ever be (pretty much rivaled Doom & Quake).
Many years later, out came Return to Castle Wolfenstein. Upgraded graphics, more weapons, cooler weapons, insane enemies and the (ahem) Elite Guards made the game extremely interesting and eye catching. Heck, my dad & I kept fighting over who would play the game. (We finally compromised and used different save files).
In 2009, the revamped Wolfenstein was released. As a revamp of the original Wolf (albeit a few modifications like the Thule Medallion, the Black Sun groups, etc.), the game was rivetting with very well designed levels, enemies and weapons. I figured Wolf could not be improved upon for a long, long time. To my surprise, yes, it could be, and it was sooner than I ever expected.
Wolfenstein: The New Order dishes out the fun like there's no tomorrow. Insanely cool weapons, amazing enemy AI (though the only thing I can't figure out is why some of the enemies spot you, make a noise, but remain in the same place until they keep staring at you (perv much?) for a few seconds. The game caters to 2 timelines, based on who you decide to sacrifice for the greater good. Each timeline is almost the same, except for a few power-ups, scenes and designs.
What captured my fancy was that you are not limited to 1 - 3 weapons like most games allow you too. Oh, Hell NO! You get to use almost every damn weapon in the game, saving it in your inventory for you to raise Hell later. And the icing on the cake: Dual wield. The toppings: Almost all the weapons have a secondary mode (rockets, silencers, laser cutter / energy pulse, etc.)
The levels are amazingly designed, the cut-scenes are excellent & the acting is perfect! Heck, I'm on my third tour of the game and it still is a bucketload of fun.
My biggest regret is waiting for ages to get this
. If I could go back in time, I would definitely buy this game regardless of the cost, just because it's just that good.

Summary:
Pros:
Amazing graphics
Team based formula
Amazing when things work
Cons:
Clunky controls
Exaggerated recoil
Terrible faction balancing
Only fun when things work (which rarely happens)
In the games current state it basically becomes what I like to call, "camp bush simulator."  Meaning if you really want to be successful just find the nearest bush on the frontlines and never ever move.  On top of that, the asymetrical gameplay makes some factions extremely overpowered compared to others *cough* *cough* Americans *cough* *cough*.  Because this is an early access game the controls are extremely clunky which is forgiveable except for the ridiculous overly exaggerated recoil.
The maps look gorgeous and are actually quite huge with is a definite positive.  However, due to the objective placement on these maps you will most likely never see the entire thing.  You will also mostly spend your time getting shot at too which disrupts the idea of just taking in your surroundings.  As intricat as you may find the maps, you will also find them extremely annoying when you spend 5-10 minutes of just continous walking from objective to objective where you will most likely get shot on the way there by some vehicle sitting on a distant hill that can't be hit because RPGs and AT-4s are very inaccurate and have extremely exaggerated projectile drop.  In short, the maps favor vehicle gameplay over infantry gameplay.  If you are playing infantry (which is 90% of this game) you are going to have a bad time.
However, I do have to praise this game as being on of the only PvP games I have ever played that actually gets the teambased mechanic correctly.  This is the only game where I have seen squads and act as squads and move together and listen to their squad leader and can actually be effective doing so.  Unfortunately, if that squad leader dies it leaves the squad completely useless if people have no idea what they are doing.  This plays into the idea that this game is only fun if everything goes as inteded which RARELY happens.
I can't recommend people by this game yet.  In its current state it is a mess.  If you are looking for a MILSIM experience play Arma 3 or Insurgency.
****EDIT*****
As brought up in the comments below, Insurgency is not a milsim.  However, the core gameplay of Insurgency provides a more valuable and fun experience that has MILSIM elements that is better than Squad (in my opinion that is).

This game is a lot of fun with a little bit of not. Class-based with roguelike elements, it has a few surprises up its sleeve to keep it interesting and enjoyable. Just when I think I'm pushing water uphill, I manage to pull myself out of a tight spot. Just when I feel like I'm cruising along too easily, I get my face pounded in with something spiky and mean. I've clocked almost 10 hours in three days, and I'm showing no signs of stopping anytime soon.
I have a few problems with the game, however.
While the blood of a roguelike is pumping fast through the heart of this game, it isn't passing through the brain as much as I'd like. Collecting a relic grants an effect, but very rarely does the description of the relic lend to an explanation of what that effect is. A mouse-over text would do wonders for telling the player what they've just gotten themselves into.
Also...there's no nice way to say it. The voice acting is a crime against nature. Thus far I've played five of the available eight classes: Viking, Marksman, Redneck, Pirate and Samurai. Only one of these five (the Viking) hasn't made me wish I knew more about modding, and that didn't seem as though it lacked the attempt.
How is it that the Marksman is more redneck than the Redneck? The Pirate is so obsessed with treasure (and climbing, for some reason) that it actually makes other pirates look charitable - seriously, we get it, you like gold and want it in your pockets. As for the Samurai...
If you can imagine Antonio Banderas doing an impersonation of Christopher Lambert's Raiden from Mortal Kombat who is himself doing an impression of Mickey Rooney's character from Breakfast At Tiffany's, you've about got it. Seriously, Kyle Kinane's bit about Trader Joe's Asian counterpart Trader Ming was less racially insensitive, and it was mimicking a man who was doing a terrible Oriental accent. "Trader Ming demand respect from forrorers!" It's that bad.
Oh, you don't want to buy the DLC and find out? That's okay, just whisper the following phrase in a very pensive, meaningful way: "Your rack of barance was your reakness." That's an actual line from the game, in all the glory it lacks. You get me? You get me.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who has a strong love for games similar to The Binding of Isaac (same control scheme, even) but who have long patience for dying unnecessary while cringing at terrible, just terrible voice acting.
Oh, and Akrea, the Lightning boss, talks like a six year old with a speech imediment. "Awe you scawed?" L2speak, then we'll talk.
...seriously with this voice acting...

Don't get me wrong, it's a good game in the right hands but here's somewhat of a buyer's beware for anyone who's condering picking it up.
1.)It's only good with friends you know who will be level headed in terms of thinking and will give you the patience to learn. Not exactly fun going solo with pubs.
2.)The LoD and viewdistance (particularly with playermodels is waaaay too low). Even at max settings, you will get shot by enemies you can't even see (it's like playing goldeneye on the N64 again, yay!). Also if you want the best chance of seeing enemies from afar, you better set that FOV slider to the lowest.
3.)Content; or lack-therof, is far and few if you're used the the wide selection of something like ArmA. This means:
-No Invade and Annex
-No KOTH
-No editor
-No steam workshop, which follows to the next point
4.) It's PVP only, (and only in first person). Many MILSIM elitists will rejoice at this feature, but for me, ehh...
5.) Performance isn't the best. Yeah I can see the responses, "but ArmA has even worse optimization", which is debatable because in this game there are many factors that will effect you FPS. The amount of people on the server, the map, amount of vehicles spawned, ping of each player. Just like ArmA, exept ArmA has more content overall so I don't know why I'd recommend getting this game.
One thing this game does get right though, is the sound design. Probably the best I've heard in a game.

Game still needs a bit more work, but as of right now, it's a great game.
Also; I've read some other reviews, and some say it's currently a driving simulator. Well yes, however there's things called role-play, you can role play fires and stuff.
A little suggestion is to add civilian cars for now, that you can drive so there can be an actual car accident RP maybe.
Overall; This game has a good future.

Zombie Defense is a hilariously generic title for this game but beneath the surface is a fun mobile port here. Make no mistake, the UI isn't set up for desktop but I managed to enjoy my time spent playing it despite that. Also, the microtransactions aren't too in your face and you really don't need to spend to advance if you are ok with replaying levels a bit to earn more cash.
So Zombie Defense is like a cross between tactics games like xcom and tower defense games. You have a squad you recruit on each level to kill zombies and there are all types of classes. Tesla, a guy with a chainsaw, shotgunner, marine, sheriff. Lots of different units with abilities and you move them around the map to certain allowed circles. I also liked the fact that you can resume a level from the round you failed rather than having to start over again at round 1. I wish more wave based games allowed that.
Overall, for a free game, it's worth checking out if you are at all interested in the premise. I talk more about how the game works in the video below (shameless self promo).

You ever play a local game with your friends, and wonder why one or more of you is wailing on pause uncontrollably when something goes wrong? It is because of games like this.
This game will teach you when to quit. You make a perfect turn and pass 7 people? That's fine. Eat two tornadoes, a rocket, and two shards of ice spread so you'd only miss if you got hit by something else. You can take that? have a remote right at a ramp, see you next fall. I heard you like drifting... let me trap a few boost panels. The game will do this to you constantly, and you have to take it and lose, or become the most aggressive driver there is by restarting and whipping everyone into a paste for even thinking of making you their whipping boy.
Don't worry, they'll teach you thoroughly how to drive, and how to properly drift and single handedly maul  your opponents on your way through races. There are a load of trials for you to do in the single player race modes, some that are exponentially more irritating than an actual race, while others will always seem a friendly breeze. You'll know full on that your technique is not the problem provided you completed those trials fully, so it is either track memory or the fact that your rivals aren't going to let you slip away because of this...
First place. Being first place is just a little less pronounced than the alliance developed F-Zero GX. But again, being in the lead is one of the easiest things to do in this game provided you can handle making the gap bigger. Of course you can, you went through the trials right? No? DO THE TRIALS! If you played the aforementioned F-zero game. Think of the Time test on very hard mode. Think of the tight drifts and pinpoint boosts you needed as well as bouncing off of the wall to pick things you weren't supposed to, you will know how to drive way before you can handle the racers. Wow, I just finished Unepic's single player and I am blown away.  This review is just for single player.  I chose to play on hard mode to make it a little more similar to Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, one of my all time favorite games.  The difficulty progressed at a good rate and It proved to be a good challenge while not being so difficult that I lost interest.  I had to put the controller down a few times due to frustration but never more than a couple minutes and I always wanted to come back and beat that next boss or get past that next room.
The story was good and I enjoyed how the main character related to his situation.   I'm also happy to say the voice acting is well done, especially for the main characters.  They play their rolls very well and never feel like they are just reading off a script.  Wow, the end is really cool!  It had me worried for a second but overall came back with some laughs and I felt good with it.
The music was exceptional to me.  It looped very well and never got annoying while I was running around dissecting everything in my path, which also sounded great.  It felt completely in place for each area of the castle and was one of the main things that made this game bring back the nostalgia I have for Castlevania: SOTN on the PS1.  Other things like items falling on the ground, lighting torches, squishy enemies, and shooting waves of fire in front of you all sounded great.  I did encounter one bug where sometimes the background music would start playing more than once, creating kind of an echo.  This went away after getting in combat (because combat music took over) or going to a different area with different, or no, music and wasn't a huge issue.
I'm a sucker for the 2D/3D style that Castlevania: SOTN is known for.  While I don't believe Unepic makes use of any 3D the shadows and lighting are excellent and do an amazing job at bringing depth to the game.  I like the style of the characters/enemies and the castle is a treat to wander through.  Everything is well animated and beautiful to look at if you enjoy this old school style.   One thing I really enjoyed was having to light the torches in every area.  It's a great touch that adds to the wonder and curiosity of exploring the castle while giving you that great accomplished feeling when the ringing sound plays from lighting the last torch in a section.
I choose to play with my Xbox 360 controller which it detected and is set up perfectly for.  The game gives you 12 hotkeys for a controller setup which was enough although a couple times I wish I had one or two more.  Controls felt tight and responsive and I had no problem quickly navigating around the dungeon.  Targeting can be a little tough if there are a lot of enemies but I never felt like I couldn't get past an area because of it.
There are only 2 "bad" things I feel I need to mention.  First, there is a (4 screens) long room with glowing white orbs you have to avoid.  I found that the orbs will often hit you when they shouldn't as if the hit-box was ahead or behind the visual representation of the orb.  It was one of the most frustrating moments for me as I kept getting "hit" when I was more than an inch away from the orb which would take me back to my last save which meant in the middle of the castle because I was playing on hard and a bit of a run to get back there. Second I had originally planned to be a mostly melee character but I found by the end of the game I found I was using my bow almost exclusively.  The endgame feels like its designed only with long range attacks in mind so make sure you have something long range or its going to be very tough.
Overall I would give this game a 9 out of 10.  Despite a few minor irritations the quality of the characters, graphics, gameplay, story, music and sounds is way above average and well worth the asking price.  I have a ton of great memories from playing through just the single player and it's one I will come back to every few years to play again and again just for that feeling of nostalgia.
If you're a fan of Castlevania style games then do yourself a favor and pick Unepic up.  If its on sale for less than 5 dollars, even if you're not sure about it, I'd strongly recommend giving it a go.  I think most people will thoroughly enjoy Unepic and what it offers and even if you don't it's only the cost of a coffee.

[Note: I'll have an actual, short review at the bottom; I figured, however, that I'd write up the story I went through in my most successful game since starting a few days ago. So, without further ado: the three colonists.]
Day 1:
We woke up and ship was in flames; we ran and jumped into our escape pods. There's me, the big, burly, strong, rougish, wondrously handsome older gent [55-ish], a younger man in his mid-30's (who I've named "Kid"), and his ex-wife in her mid-20's. Thankfully, none of us were too badly injured by our fall; I managed to scavenge a rifle and I went hunting while the other two gathered some wood and took stock of our supplies. We started making a small shelter, but wound up passing out on the cold ground for the night. Despite the crash, things seem to be doing better than we could've hoped...
Day 7:
We've got a small barracks set up, and we've even managed to dig out a small cave that we've slapped some electronic coolers into, making a walk-in freezer. We have a chance, it seems, to survive. The Kid's been planting crops all week, hoping it'd give us something to live on in the next few months; he and his ex seem to like each other fine enough, but they occasionally argue with one another. Maybe that's why she seems to have no interest in me. Oh well, I'll keep trying, and I'll keep surviving.
Day 13:
Someone ran to our small fortress today, after we'd finished setting up sandbags all around; a young woman, who, while extroardinarily beautiful, seemed to be a smart-mouth and far smarter than anyone would've ever believed. She was, of course, pursued by an evil trafficker, but one quick shot between the eyes stopped him in his tracks. She knows her stuff, and she had us start researching technologies as fast as we could.
Day 27:
Well, our young researcher and I are now an item. Who'd have thought a grizzled old soldier and a young pretty thing like her would ever get together? Ah well, no use complainin', I'm pretty happy with all things considered. Another young woman ran to us over the passing week, and her husband ran to us as well, several days later. I never need to see another fat guy running naked in my life, again, thanks. But they seem happy.
Day 35:
The Kid's ex is dead. It was a freak accident, where some crazy, big animal started mauling random people. She shot at it a few times, and.. well.. the Kid's pretty shaken up, all things considered. She saved his life and mine, too. Poor guy. Even if they weren't on great terms, they still cared about each other at one time. Very little else happened, aside from us harvesting and freezing our crops.
Day 41:
Another survivor! She crashed. Down from the atmosphere. She was bleeding out, and my fiancee helped patch her up. I've seen the kid making goo-goo eyes at her, though; she's a pretty thing, I can't blame him for it. He did just lose someone important, after all.
Day 70:
The Kid and our most recent addition, Penny, are going to get married! Glad to see that the kid is doing so much better, now, and Penny is just a great person to be around. Other than that, winter is nearly here and we're rushing to make some heaters. We've built a few turrets around our perimeter along with a small generator, powered by.. I dunno, natural geysers or summin? I got no idea. The Kid's been hard at work, though, using a small sewing machine that we made and making parkas for everyone. He's a good kid, overall, and we're all glad he's so passionate about working.
Day 102:
Everyone's dead, except me and the woman who ran to us. Let me backtrack a few days: we got a signal about someone fleeing a band of pirates, and we offered them refuge, quickly dispatching the pirate. This person was hurt and my fiancee nursed her back to health. Things went well for about a week, until she got bored of doing absolutely nothing and started lighting everything on fire. Our homes, our labs, our resources--everything burned up, aside from a small stash of food we'd prepared, just in case. Everyone else burned up fighting the fire, I only survived because my bed was destroyed the day before and I was sleeping in a nearby cave. My fiancee, the Kid, Penny, her husband.. and the idiot who started the fire, burning herself alive in the process.. we can't stay here. We've decided to gather what resources we can, and then move out in the next day. All of our pack animals are gone, but this place was nearly tapped out, anyway. Hopefully we can make it before this blizzard starts....
Day 105:
No food left. The blizzard claimed her, last night, after she was sleeping off a bad scratch wound from a local rat. No food, no shelter, and I'm all alone, now. There's only one thing left for me to do.. thank God I brought a gun with me....
[End of the story of "Grim" the Space Marine]

I've only played the Escalation version of Ashes when it was released but even after just 1-2 patches the game has gotten significantly better. It's gotten more stable, units feel more balanced and useful, abilities and resource management has been streamlined or improved.
What's unique about this game is that you lack direct control of your units. While you can order specific targeting in an army how your individual units behave is left to the army composition and units themselves. While this can be challenging at times since they don't always respond the way you want, if you can make a few armies and compensate based off of terrain and unit types you'll have much better time when getting into battles. You will lose units so keeping them alive is difficult but not impossible. And you're supposed to be making and losing armies as part of the game.
What most impressed was the feeling of large armies crossing the map. It wasn't you need to counter these units but actually zooming out, planning the best sectors of the map to attack and what unit composition. This is a slower pace game but it allows you to make these decisions and focus on more strategy. Line of sight is hugely important, terrain is a big factor, what units you bring is factor, how you mange your economy is factor to how well you'll do in the game.
If you like having the feeling of commanding huge armies across a battlefield much like Supreme Commander did, you'll enjoy this.

What a disappointment, this game is a complete miss and I have no idea how it has so positive rating. I played the original game, and I played and loved Return to Casle Wolfenstein back when it came out. But this game is a mockery to both its prequels.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a story driven adventure/fps. It plays like a mix of Bioshock Infinite, Duke Nukem Forever and Call of Duty 1, with absolutely everything that this would imply:
-The gameplay is extremely fragmented, heavily depending on scripts, full of some stupid minigames and passages where you do absolutely nothing but walk on highlighted path, push an action key or just give a hand to someone. Levels are often visually grand but you cannot go anywhere except the one small path you have to take.
-This is 100% story driven game, full of long cutscenes. The problem is, the story is absolutely terrible nonsense, seriously. I was glad at first they decided to go with "alternative history", since that is way better imo than to molest actual history. But the storyline is completely idiotic on all levels: It fails as a sci-fi as it makes no sense whatsoever and ignores completely both history and the laws of physics (without any exaggeration, even Bioshock Infinite has a much more inteligent and believeable story...Yea, crazy, I know!), it fails also as a story as the characters are flat, stupid, and all talk like in a Disney fairy tale. There are even (wishfully) romantic scenes in the story...HAHAHA!  I wont go into any details on the story to avoid spoilers, but I guarantee you, you will be laughing your back off at moments which the developers tried hard to be brutal or hearthbreaking.
Again,

- there are many stealth parts in this game, but they are a complete joke (just imagine Mafia 3 stealth play)
- you lose all your stuff between almost every mission, and have to start with a knife almost every mission. Not terrible on it's own, but it makes searching for ammo and weapons a waste of time in this game.
I honestly cannot think of one strong upside of this game, only things that are not horrible. The weapons feel phony and I found most of them boring. Most of the enemies look, move and die the same so the gun side of this game feels very repetetive. I like the checkpoints system (no quick save). The visuals are pretty good, some of the levels are nicely detailed. I liked the perks and also hunting for hidden collectibles. The nostalgic levels from first Wolfenstein were a nice touch too.
I recommend not buying this game, certainly not for more than 10 usd, it is not worth more. If you are looking for a decent adventure/fps story driven game with romantic elements, get Bioshock Infinite. Also, I just read that they are planning a sequel to this game, pretty much in the same spirit as this pathetic mess. So rip Wolfenstein series, we will never forget (*your first 2 games!)...

The Silent Age follows the character Joe as he finds out in 1972 that his company is doing something that might mean a little more than he though... but, god! I really thought this story was going to be so good! And all the questions I had had  really simple answers. What kills everyone in 2012? The flu. Who are those guys in the chambers? Other time travellers (not even clones!)? Who is Frank? A Soviet... secret agent... Right.
See the story is what I had my biggest problems with, if you couldn't tell. I thought it would be so complex and there'd be a massive plot twist at the end, but this particular time travel story is played very safe. Pretty much every convention you know from your traditional time travel stories is in here. Dystopian future, limited time to save the world, yada yada yada. But I wouldn't have as many problems if the story itself wasn't so dull. Joe has no personality. The doctor is a unique character, but he's given such little time that we don't know who he is. And the big twist with Frank is kind of out of nowhere, since we met him 5 mintues before he revealed himself (Oh, and the post-it note at the beginning. Forgot about that.).
The world itself is also very boring. Don't get me wrong, the graphics are GORGEOUS in this game. Silent Age has a very unique look that really stands out when compared to other video games' artistic styles. And I really like how this game looks. But the world itself is just... boring. Archon is a serious business with a boss who doesn't care about his employees that has some dark secrets. Yawn. And outside of that, there's very little to the actual world. Just a bunch of linked events to lead you to the climax.
However, there are a few things I REALLY liked in this game. For one, the music and ambience is top notch. It really establishes a sense of tension, and the things going on inside the levels you traverse feel like real locations. I'd say the worst sound aspect is the voice acting. It's all over the place. You've got some good lines here and there, but there are some really awkwardly written and delivered lines where all you can do is raise an eyebrow and ask, "The hell...?"
On top of that, I enjoyed the time travel mechanics used in puzzle-solving. It's very unique to see a homeless man playing guitar in 1970, and later see his charred corpse on the ground in 2012. Plus, using this mechanic makes puzzles a lot more unique. Some doors might be locked in 1970 that are unlocked in 2012. There might be a wrench in 2012 that'll screw the bolts of a hatch in 1970. And the puzzles are decently laid out, so you can intuitively solve them by yourself. It's a point-and-click puzzle that isn't too complex or too simple. It's just right.
Unfortunately, this is dragged down by some of the dull elements in the actual story. I don't care about Joe. The world he lives in is just... uninteresting. And the story encompassing everything going on is surprisngly bland. I was hoping it'd lead to so much more (the tension really made me think there'd be a twist where Joe's past clones of himself were all trying to solve the same problem and kept getting stuck where he did towards the end. Now THAT would be cool! Or maybe he finds out that Archon was actually trying to solve the problem that he was unknowingly creating over and over again. Now, wouldn't that be a neat twist? But, if you like a well-done point-and-click with amazing graphics and sound design, but an unfortunately forgettable story... hey! This game's alright.

Go To Bed: Survive The Night is a very cool looking game and has a neat idea, but the execution is really really bad.
Go To Bed: Survive The Night places you in the shoes of a little child who goes to bed, but the forces of darkness are attacking him and you must defend him until the sunrise.
But you might ask how do you protect the child ? Well you click the monsters away. Yes you have to click these monsters away, but there are some other stuff too. After every level you go to a shop where you can buy stuff like a teddy bear which takes a hit, a dream catcher which collects light balls which either activates a lamp which freezes everything on the screen and also a clock which clears everything on the screen, you can also buy a toybox which after being broken clears everything on the screen as well.
You buy stuff with spiders you crush in every level, but if you die your spider counter is reset to zero, which means in later levels it gets harder to buy stuff.
Art Style to this game is probably the best thing, but in general it's mostly too dark to see everything and this is where we go into the incredibly bad things about the game.
First of all the game has an insane difficulty spike in the penultimate level of the game. It's okay if the game get's progressively harder as the game goes on, but that's not the case. The entire game is easy and simple, but as stated the penultimate level throws too much stuff on the screen you will get cramps from playing the game. I literally had to take a break after my first attempt on the level, because my hand started hurting badly.
The main story of the game doesn't take that long to complete. It took me an hour to finish the story, but there are some other things like an endless mode and a gauntlet mode which gives the game more play value.
The game overall isn't really good and there's no point in playing it as all this game does is just frustrate you. It's not rewarding and sadly it feels like a mobile game.
Final Rating:
4/10
Pros:
+ Great art style
Cons:
- Difficulty spikes
- Boring

The Silent Age  is a point and click with a quite rare central mechanic - in the majority of the game it's possible to timetravel - changing past affects the future, and you can take items with you.
The game was originally a mobile game, which got revamped, and it's mobile past shows - there is no item combination, has 10 shorter chapters to support shorter sessions, no pixelhunting and all items are used only once - these add up to a casual, easy, but well-made point and click game with really nice voice acting quality.
The developers recently added several (six!) new supported languages, and the patch broke the achievements -  after we mentioned it on the forums, in two days they patched it, they work fine. To be honest I don't understand why they didn't reply to us, or featured it as news, even though their patch caused the whole issue, they fixed it nicely really fast - good support is a valuable thing.
Things that may deter you from purchasing, depending on your preferations:
- Game has 10 chapters, each around half an hour if you play for the first time, maybe somewhat more. This is considered to be a short point and click, and it's easy as well - if you want a more challenging, or longer game, you should stay away.
- The game features time travel, so it does what every story, movie, book every that features timetravel heavily: messes it up.  Any change you make in the past is really focused on the future, always calculable - the hole won't get fixed, buried, covered etc, and never will have extra consequences. So if you're going for a very logical, almost realistic story, this game isn't really your thing.
If you're okay with these, feel free to get the game! Not the longest, not the most realistic/serious ones, but it's quite likeable, perfect for players who want a point and click with more emphasis on story, and won't get you stuck for hours with a puzzle - the protagonist isn't the sharpest tool in the shed and pretty clueless in some situations, so prepare for some funny descriptions about items or actions!
Surprisingly effectively threatening.  The mechanics and "story" are very simple, but it's a good way to drive a little time spent playing a game.

The King of Shadows wants to get you and is sending his minions as soon as your mother sends you to bed: to survive the night you'll have to touch (click) the shadowy horrors coming your way before they grab you.
Go To Bed: Survive The Night is a short clicker/ reflex game where you face the aforementioned shadow monsters in three different areas as the clock slowly counts towards sunrise: as a whole it's a decent but basic experience that fans of the genre might enjoy.
-has a quite nice art style
-simple but effective soundtrack, the narrator does a decent job
-the different monsters/ areas give some variety
-the gameplay is obviously basic
-while it can get hectic at times I don't feel the game is particularly challenging, I've completed it without upgrades and never died despite a few close calls
-I found the extra modes pretty dull
-extremely short, story mode'll take 30 mins if you don't die
-at least one achievement (beating story mode without getting hit) is broken and the game throws an error, while still working into windowed mode, at the ending cutscene
-no way to pause a stage while you're playing
-you need to finish story mode in one sitting as, afaik, the checkpoints will be erased if you quit before finishing the story
The game was decent but short-lived fun for me, of course you're basically just clicking things as fast as possible but at least there's a bit of variety to it such as lights that needs to be kept on, a couple helpful objects to buy from a store, enemies that need more than one click and a stage where branches will obscure your vision. It's very short but I feel this works to its advantage as it ensures the game doesn't overstay its welcome before the simple gameplay gets boring and your hand gets too sore.
I personally wasn't too impressed by the extra modes as Mom Rush is an endless mode that's only fun for a couple tries before you realize it's pretty pointless with no scores/ leaderboards while the Nightmare Gauntlet changes things a bit through a few gameplay changes but is too reliant on grinding levels until you unlock the next stage.
All things considered Survive The Night is a decent, if short, proposition if you like the genre but I don't feel it does enough to warrant its price so I'd get it on a bundle or on a big sale.

I bought this game on its idea alone -- a fast-paced boss rush where one hit kills. Who wouldn't think that sounds intriguing? I was really excited, and I like hard games a lot. When I started playing the game, I think it's one of the worst designed games I've played in years, and I had to put it down pretty quickly. It's presumptuous that the developers seem to think this will be a popular game for speedrunning, because the game needs tons of improvements before it would even be fun.
The biggest thing that I hated was your weapon. You have only a bow, and press X to charge a shot. Not only does the camera move confusingly when you do this (making it difficult to aim precisely), but you actually have to continue holding X for your arrow to *return* to you. This completely and utterly breaks the flow of the boss fights, as you constantly have to find small windows of "doing nothing" so that you can retrieve your arrow. I feel like this mechanic was put in solely for the uniqueness factor, and nobody seemed to think about whether this actually made the player feel "cool" when fighting all these bosses. Shadow of the Colossus made me feel *awesome* -- I was climbing these huge, hairy beasts, hanging on for dear life. In this game, 3/4 of my time was spent scurrying around and retrieving my arrows. Not exactly the same feeling.
Absolutely everything about the game has these tiny, aggravating design problems. Death animations are long, and elevator animations are longer. Respawn points aren't right by the boss you were just trying, so it takes a minute or more to just get back to the boss you were fighting (even after dying in as little as 2 seconds). The arrow moves so fast that you can't even see it fly through the air, just where it lands. Bosses also have one health, so when you beat them it feels more like dumb luck than you actually having mastered their mechanics. The overworld is huge and has no map, and it's way too difficult to just find bosses to fight. You can't charge a bow shot while moving. You can't dash unless you roll first. Rolling has a short cooldown that doesn't match up with the animation and isn't indicated in any way. You can't roll up stairs, and it halts your movement if you even try. Basically, each and every one of these little things decreased my enjoyment of the game, and one of them was the straw that broke my tolerance.
All of this adds up to a game that *seems* like it should be absolutely stellar, but I beat about eight of the bosses and couldn't stomach having to sit through one more death animation or one more cycle of missing an arrow, then waiting helplessly until I could find a window just so I could retrieve it and attack him again.
Please do not buy this game. The saddest thing in the world to me is an amazing idea with awful execution.

Classic SF, with the main themes being the end of mankind and civilization, and time travel - all seen through the eyes of one of the most iconic (and seldomly used) protagonists of the genre, the janitor. Enjoyable and certainly something a little different from what's usually on the menu of games, and adventures in particular - alternating between the 70s and the ruined remains of society in the present.
A nice humorous undertone lightens up the narration considerably, so the apocalyptic setting never feels overwhelming, ominous or menacing in any way. Not especially long, it betrays its episodic lineage by having chapters, that are effectively different areas, entirely sealed off one from another, so puzzles can never span across them, and the items leading to the solutions must always be found in relative vicinity, making the process easier than most adventure games and more puzzle-y.
The game's not fully voiced, but when it is, the voicework's quality is excellent, with several familiar voices from Telltale games, including Adam "Bigby" Harrington.

[Note: I'll have an actual, short review at the bottom; I figured, however, that I'd write up the story I went through in my most successful game since starting a few days ago. So, without further ado: the three colonists.]
Day 1:
We woke up and ship was in flames; we ran and jumped into our escape pods. There's me, the big, burly, strong, rougish, wondrously handsome older gent [55-ish], a younger man in his mid-30's (who I've named "Kid"), and his ex-wife in her mid-20's. Thankfully, none of us were too badly injured by our fall; I managed to scavenge a rifle and I went hunting while the other two gathered some wood and took stock of our supplies. We started making a small shelter, but wound up passing out on the cold ground for the night. Despite the crash, things seem to be doing better than we could've hoped...
Day 7:
We've got a small barracks set up, and we've even managed to dig out a small cave that we've slapped some electronic coolers into, making a walk-in freezer. We have a chance, it seems, to survive. The Kid's been planting crops all week, hoping it'd give us something to live on in the next few months; he and his ex seem to like each other fine enough, but they occasionally argue with one another. Maybe that's why she seems to have no interest in me. Oh well, I'll keep trying, and I'll keep surviving.
Day 13:
Someone ran to our small fortress today, after we'd finished setting up sandbags all around; a young woman, who, while extroardinarily beautiful, seemed to be a smart-mouth and far smarter than anyone would've ever believed. She was, of course, pursued by an evil trafficker, but one quick shot between the eyes stopped him in his tracks. She knows her stuff, and she had us start researching technologies as fast as we could.
Day 27:
Well, our young researcher and I are now an item. Who'd have thought a grizzled old soldier and a young pretty thing like her would ever get together? Ah well, no use complainin', I'm pretty happy with all things considered. Another young woman ran to us over the passing week, and her husband ran to us as well, several days later. I never need to see another fat guy running naked in my life, again, thanks. But they seem happy.
Day 35:
The Kid's ex is dead. It was a freak accident, where some crazy, big animal started mauling random people. She shot at it a few times, and.. well.. the Kid's pretty shaken up, all things considered. She saved his life and mine, too. Poor guy. Even if they weren't on great terms, they still cared about each other at one time. Very little else happened, aside from us harvesting and freezing our crops.
Day 41:
Another survivor! She crashed. Down from the atmosphere. She was bleeding out, and my fiancee helped patch her up. I've seen the kid making goo-goo eyes at her, though; she's a pretty thing, I can't blame him for it. He did just lose someone important, after all.
Day 70:
The Kid and our most recent addition, Penny, are going to get married! Glad to see that the kid is doing so much better, now, and Penny is just a great person to be around. Other than that, winter is nearly here and we're rushing to make some heaters. We've built a few turrets around our perimeter along with a small generator, powered by.. I dunno, natural geysers or summin? I got no idea. The Kid's been hard at work, though, using a small sewing machine that we made and making parkas for everyone. He's a good kid, overall, and we're all glad he's so passionate about working.
Day 102:
Everyone's dead, except me and the woman who ran to us. Let me backtrack a few days: we got a signal about someone fleeing a band of pirates, and we offered them refuge, quickly dispatching the pirate. This person was hurt and my fiancee nursed her back to health. Things went well for about a week, until she got bored of doing absolutely nothing and started lighting everything on fire. Our homes, our labs, our resources--everything burned up, aside from a small stash of food we'd prepared, just in case. Everyone else burned up fighting the fire, I only survived because my bed was destroyed the day before and I was sleeping in a nearby cave. My fiancee, the Kid, Penny, her husband.. and the idiot who started the fire, burning herself alive in the process.. we can't stay here. We've decided to gather what resources we can, and then move out in the next day. All of our pack animals are gone, but this place was nearly tapped out, anyway. Hopefully we can make it before this blizzard starts....
Day 105:
No food left. The blizzard claimed her, last night, after she was sleeping off a bad scratch wound from a local rat. No food, no shelter, and I'm all alone, now. There's only one thing left for me to do.. thank God I brought a gun with me....
[End of the story of "Grim" the Space Marine]
Here's the actual review:
I love this game. Hands-down, this is one of my favorite games on Steam. It's got so much of a simulation aspect to it that, while YES it can be gamed a little bit, it has so much depth that just lets you paint a picture over it with your imagination while you play. None of that story above happened in that exact way in the story, I interpreted it that way, and decided to go with the perspective of the longest-lasting survivor.
My final verdict for this game is simple: if you love games like Dwarf Fortress or simulation games in general, you'll probably like this. ESPECIALLY if you're a giant sci-fi nerd like me. I do think the asking price is still a bit steep, but I am glad that I paid it. (Note: A friend bought it for me and I paid him back. Worth it.)

I want to like this game, I really really do. But it just lacks finesse- it isn't polished enough. I love how your choices matter, like how for example a woman wants a gun and if you give it to her she'll shoot her ex husband. Sure, you spent a lot of money to buy that gun but the fact that she does that is still great, it really shows how not all quests have a good ending. However, money is impossible to get in this game. For example, your daugther will get sick really early on. She needs 20.000 for surgery and I heard some people say that she needs another 15.000 after that. How do I not know this for myself? Because getting 20.000 within the 80-hour timeframe you're given is ridiculous and impossible.
Your son needs another 15.000 a day after your daugther gets ill to continue his studies. The time you need to do this? 48 hours. Even though you desperately need money to keep your daughter alive, you also need a lot of money to help with your son's future. And the worst part is? If you don't talk to them, the quest won't start. If you don't talk to them, your daughter doesn't become ill and your son does not need money for his studies. It is as simple as that.
What's worse? Your wife wants money too. She needs 500 for groceries and 700 for utility bills. How often? Like once every day- maybe every two days. Not just that, in the middle of your daughter being ill and your son needing to study my wife also give me a quest to buy her a radio within the next 24 hours. Because a radio - that she later puts in YOUR office, even though you'll never use it - is clearly the highest priority, way more important than the lives of your family.
Allthough the art style is beautiful and really represents the dystopian future setting, together with the nice and atmospheric music, this game's writing is shallow. Every once in a while you get an article and it does not feel like an actual realistic article made by well respected journalists but instead it feels like something put together by some guy who still lives in his mom's basement. Articles in this game always come together with another article made by revolutionists that tell the so called 'truth'. These articles are even worse and truly don't sound realistic at all and completely ruin the mood.
The same goes for the character dialogue. You'll find people saying things such as 'cool' and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ that, once more, do not properly represent the ideas of something like say Orwell's '1984', that this game is obviously based on. Dialogue is boring and onesided. You know what would make this great? If you could ask your tenants how their day was, and every day it'd be something else. Heck, it wouldn't even have to be every day, as long as you could talk to them about something other than that quest you did for them days earlier.
I want to compare this game to 'Papers, Please', a game that is beautiful and brilliant and near perfection, set in a Communist republic with brilliant story writing. You know what that game did well that this game didn't do? Of course I understand that they're completely seperate types of games, though the feeling and atmosphere is definitely similair. Or at least, it is supposed to be similair but it fails massively. What Papers, Please' did well is that it didn't let the protagonist talk much. What the protagonist said were always short, snappy lines that made sense- okay, maybe you wouldn't always agree with it, but usually they said something sensible along the lines of 'get out of my booth!'
What this game does instead is give the protagonist full sentences. And the things he says are usually not very good. He means good for his family, I am sure, but whenever he talks to his wife he is mean to her. Heck, the choices are bad too. You can either choose between 'make my wife mad' and 'make my wife mad'. This makes it really difficult for me to actually feel bad for the guy when you eventually fail- and trust me, you will fail.
Why? I wouldn't know. One time I was arrested for 'embezzlement'. What did I steal? I wouldn't have a clue. I don't recall stealing anything but I was arrested nonetheless.
I could continue about what makes this game rather unenjoyable. For example, the gameplay is repetitive. There are supposed to be different options for each quest, but I find that untrue. Sure, some quests do have that, but with say your daughter you need to pay either 20.000 or 30.000- there's no better option there. And you can't do anything to help your son in any other way other than paying the required amount of 15.000.
This game is not very good. Does it have potential? Definitely. But in its current state I do not believe it is worth your time or money.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a sterling example of a game that kowtows to expectations of what people think a modern shooter to be and suffers immensely for it. The core gameplay is fine, the guns look nice, they sound nice, they have recoil that makes them seem powerful without being too annoying to aim, the enemies react well to being shot and have acceptible AI keeping them moving around and flanking, whenever you're just in a room shooting soldiers the game is enjoyable. Everything around that core experience of shooting guys is awful though and detracts from the experience in the most egregious ways.
There is no automatic item pickup so after every fight you're going to have a couple minutes of just walking around staring at the ground picking up ammo, health and armor. This is maybe understandable for health and armor since you might not want to accidentally waste some when you don't need it but there's no reason for this to apply to ammo which you're almost never going to be maxed out on to waste. Every time you transition levels you lose all of your weapons and ammo as well and have to collect all the exact same stuff again, I probably spent about as much time staring at the ground looking for♥♥♥♥♥♥as I did actually fighting anything. Every couple of minutes the game completely wrests control away from you for cutscenes. In between every action level there is an actionless level in which you just walk around and talk to NPCs who are almost completely lacking characterization, I didn't care about a single one of them at any point throughout the game. Every level is padded out in size to fit hidden collectibles which do absolutely nothing, yet somehow also feels far too short (probably because so little of each one involves actual combat). The game has a perk system that adds absolutely nothing to the gameplay, it's all boring passive perks like extra ammo capacity or extra magazine sizes, and since you just get the benefits of every one you unlock and don't have to switch them or interact with them in any way there's no reason to even open the menu to look at them.
All of this stuff feels like it's just what people expect an FPS to be nowadays. They expect collectibles, they expect some kind of incremental upgrade system, they expect lots of cutscenes and story, they expect levels where you just walk and talk instead of shooting anything, but those things have come to be expected because they've been done in ways that have made games more engaging or immersive. Half-Life used walk and talk segments to completely remove cutscenes entirely, Modern Warfare used them as a way to blindside players with events that would lose impact with the abstraction of a cutscene, and there's probably even better examples I'm not remembering right now. Wolfenstein uses them to bore you out of your skull and waste your time doing busy work like trying to find someones missing folder or a lost piece of welding equipment. Dishonored used collectibles as a way to upgrade your equipment and open up different gameplay options, Wolfenstein just has them sitting around doing nothing. RPGs use what's functionally similar to a perk system to make different playthroughs feel really different by having you pick and choose what you want your character to be able to do, Wolfenstein just lets you unlock a bunch of +3 bullets in the magazine ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t that doesn't affect how you play at all.
The game has a bunch of other issues too, like bland level design that really squanders the premises the story sets up. The vast majority of the levels are grey hallways even when they have amazing excuses to make them something more interesting. You break into a huge tower, the decadent symbol of the Nazi's control over England, and the entire level is cramped grey hallways. There's a level aboard a submarine, apparently the largest and most powerful one in existence, and all you see of that sub is a handful of cramped grey hallways, an engine room, and a control room. There's a level on the damn moon and you get ONE short segment of low gravity where you fight exactly two small drones, both killed in one or two shots, and the whole rest of the level is cramped grey hallways.
I've played a whole lot of different shooters and I can't think of a single one that I wouldn't prefer playing over Wolfenstein. Hell I even enjoyed the little joke minigame of the original Wolfenstein level you can access in the base more than most of the real levels in the game, at least that one had bright blue doors breaking up the grey hallways and it didn't interrupt the flow every minute with a cutscene.

I don't think it's a bold statement if I say that EVERYONE has had fun time with Mario Kart. At least, I know no person who has had no fun with Mario Kart. I had fun, my lil sis had fun, my parents had fun, my grandparents had fun, all my friends had fun. Mario Kart is FUN. And so is... ahem: "Sonic and Sega All Star Racing TRANSFORMED", what's in the name ;)
Why the comparisson? Well just look at it, it's a race game featuring game characters from other games (sega and valve) you may or may not know and you have powerups and weapons to pick up and use. Is it a bad thing? Not according to me, this is a good game.
It's gameplay gimmick is the Transformed part. Most courses are part driven in a car, part in a boat and part flown in an aircraft! This changes the dynamics quite a bit as you have to manouvre in 3d when you fly, boats respond differently, etc. It works really well and the tracks are well designed.
It's just a fun arcade racing game with powerups, boosts, skill and cartoony weapons, nothing more to it. It's fun singleplayer, it's fun but tough online, and even more fun when playing with family and friends in split-screen.
The characters you can race with may not be known to some players nowadays. I played both Nintendo SNES and Sega Genesis back in the days. I liked mario, off course, but I like Sonic too. I never was part of any camp. Now Sega has come to my beloved PC and I was happy to see that speeding blue hedgehog and his friends again, even though they haven't had a good game since Sonic-CD besides these racing games. Titan Souls is a top down non-linear puzzle game, similar to the idea of Shadow of the Colossus.  While not on the same level with the comparisons between the two, the one thing that both games have going for it is the boss mechanics.  Titan Souls takes that idea and turns it into a mechanic that the bosses die in one hit, you die in one hit, and you only have one arrow.  A puzzle like mechanic that is lacking the usage of equipment and abilities.  Instead, it's based on reaction time and awareness.  If you miss your shot, you'll probably die.  If you never learn the boss's mechanics, you'll die.  You can argue that a game based on trial and error is not a good game, but trial and error is a concept in every game.  The fact that the Souls titles (which need to stop being compared to Titan Souls) are very succesful because of the trial and error.
Now to play this game, you will need a controller.  The PC controls are not fantastic in the least and there are no key rebindings (although there are only two real actions in the game).  If you don't have a controller, you'd either go and get one or just skip it.  The difficulty is an opinion.  I say that because people who can solve puzzles or learn mechanics quickly, will have no problem.  If you can't, you're going to get stuck.  The art style is fantastic with a portrayal of some Fez like animations and the camera being drawn back reminds me so much of what Below on the Xbox One is doing, giving you a sense of how large this world is.
The music is simply beautiful in every aspect, to the point that it's a damn shame they don't have it on sell anywhere.  From soft and somber music to some straight heavy guitar riffs, the range of sounds are absolutely outstanding.  As far as sound design, every sound is impactful (I.E. a yeti rolling into a wall, a blob hitting the ground, being sucked in by a gust of wind, etc).
The story itself is probably the weakest.  It heavily focuses on narrative and doesn't give you much of the history of the world, bosses, and protagonist.  That is up to you to decide whether your character is there for the right reasons or the wrong reasons.  Why is he here?  What kind of person is he?  Why do the titans not attack you instantly?  What's the "truth"?  All questions you ask yourself throughout the game, only for you to come up with the answers.
I feel the price range of $15 is fair because I love simple yet challenging games like this.  It's not everyone's cup of tea, but if you dig like Shadow of the Colossus and are heavily supportive of the rise of indie devs, I totally suggest picking this title up.

I was tempted to say that this game is far more enjoyable than it has any right to be, but ♥♥♥♥ it:  It's actually quite genuinely CLEVER, so any kudos I'm inclined to give it is fully deserved.  Simple, yes...deceptively so...but definitely clever.  How, you ask?  Well, in...SIMPLE ways, really!  Such as the fact that your visibility declines as the game progresses, meaning that the formerly easy task of clicking on all encroaching beasties becomes significantly harder, especially if you have to keep frantically turning on lights just to keep said visibility up!  So, yes, it's basically a "time management" game with a very simple interface, and in that sense may well appeal to the Five Nights at Freddy's crowd (without being a completely blatant rip-off of said franchise, such as, hmmm, let's see...123 Slaughter Me Street, anyone?)!  Add to all this an extremely charming art style, fabulously spooky sound and - what's this - highly competent voice acting?  In an indie "horror" game?!  TELL ME IT AIN'T SO!!
And okay, so the main story mode doesn't appear to be that long - though I for one am yet to beat it - but there's a couple of mini-modes on the side to give it all a bit of longevity.  So on sale, at least, it's certainly a bit hard to argue with the more-than-adequate bang-for-your-buck...unless you're one of those tiresome ♥♥♥♥s who complains about spending a measly few bucks on a game to find it doesn't last for twenty-seven-plus hours.  (Seriously, you people really are tiresome, and should find something more worthwhile to concern yourselves with...maybe turn on the TV news for five minutes some time...THAT oughtta scare the living♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you!  I know it gives ME ♥♥♥♥in' nightmares...)
Oh, and for all you "clicker game" people:  This is a bit like that, only it requires some degree of thought and skill. It's quite good, in terms of quality. I really enjoyed the boss fights as bite-sized challenges, like a sudden-death Zelda boss rush. The art is simple, but very effective and consistent, and everything runs well and plays smoothly and responsively, as expected. I give it a "wait for a sale," though, since there are two major problems I have with the game that make it not worth buying right now:
1) There are 18 titans in the game (thanks Hazmatt) and if you beat them all before finishing the game you get one more secret fight. YMMV but for me that translated to less than two hours total (final time was 1 hour 54 minutes), at least half of which was walking around the surprisingly large, totally empty landscape. Also, unless you want to try challenges like a no-death run or a no-roll run, there's very little replay value, which is to be expected, but which would have been helped if the actual content was more robust. And no, unlike SotC, you can't replay fights from dead bosses for a time trial or just for fun. In addition, there's very little story, and what is there is highly abstract and vague, which is intriguing, but at the same time again diminishes its content. When all's said and done, for $15 it's just not enough value. For $10, maybe, but even that's stretching it.
2) The interface is minimalist, which is nice, but it also removes crucial information in a game like this. Namely, when your roll delay is up. If you roll, you can't roll again for a period of time, but in order to know that period of time, you just need to memorize and get used to it. In a tense fight, it can frequently feel like you got cheated into a death because your roll wouldn't respond. An audio cue or something would have eliminated that issue.

The game feels like a blend between the Binding of Isaac, Diablo 2, and Killing Floor, but without many of the perks of each. The random levels do make the game feel new and refreshing each time I had to grind through a level. The problem with the random levels, is the unbalanced random enemies. One of the other complaints I had about the game was the voice acting. Half the time, it's difficult to understand what the characters are saying because they sound more like they are muttering than speaking. Occasionally some of the things they say are somewhat funny, but the acting itself seems a bit off. Also, the shop keeper is incredibly annoying because his voice doesn't seem to respect your sound levels.
Also on the difficulty, it took me 5-7 runs with one character to even be able to beat the first level. The final bosses for each area always seem to have the same hp/attack strength no matter what level your character is, or what level you encounter them on. Supposedly I unlocked Nightmare mode, but I couldn't play it when I went back to the character screen.
The graphics are really pretty, but with a lot going on, it's difficult to keep track of enemy projectiles.
Play this game if you enjoy killing random hordes of enemies and finding random items to use.
Don't play it if you're looking for a well polished, and balanced game.

Despite the many many flaws, I totally love this game!
This is not the kind of title you can pick up casually hoping to have some immediate fun: it requires love and passion for a couple of hours, in order for you to pick up how to pilot the ship AND the mech appropriately but, when you do... oh boy!
It's a pity that the game has so many shortcoming preventing it from becoming a masterpiece, but thanks to the great game mechanics, it can still hold its own.
Here is what I didn't like:
- repetitive missions.
Here and there by reviewers you will be told that the missions are generated randomly, but this is half true. While the layout of each mission is scrambled (as well as the topology of the "hulks" to explore), the randomness is quite low, so it doesn't take much before everything gives a deja vu feeling
- rigid game structure
the game is subdivided in seasons and, while it is a nice touch that fits into the general concept, it comes a time when you just want to either pick a random mission and get wild, or replay one of the missions you already did.
Sure, there is "The Void": a streak of unlimited random generated missions, but they are differently structured and are not as satisfying as the original game [EDIT: the void is totally cool. At some point you build some tolerance for the spinning ;-) ]
- sluggish transitions
between pretty much everything there is a anime intermission with the pilot winking, the ship starting, ecc ecc. Now this is great when it's done to hide some loading time, but the developers really overdid it. Guys, can I just shot some fu...rs, please??? :)
That said, the game is so damn good, you can forgive it pretty much everything, as long as you give yourself the time to get a bit good with it: the dogfights are a chaotic mix of physics and environmental based combat where you dance and slide with your vehicle while transforming from fighter launching missiles barrages, and mech pulling and throwing stuff around.
The graphics is stunning and the audio does its job remarkably, with touches of styles like the pilots intercoms during the fight (a nod to the anime material the whole game is inspired from), and the game is sparkled with humor and references (one of the enemy pilots is dressed like the protagonist of Guacameleee :DDD).
Regardless...
You get to pilot a space ship that transforms into a mech, and feel like a total badass in the process. What the f#%$ do you want more than this?? =)
Highly recommended!

It's not a bad game, but it's just too much grinding and too unbalanced.
You can enter a dungeon in the first level and encounter enemies with 10k+ health while you deal around 50 damage per hit. While you don't have to enter dungeons it's the best chance of finding artifacts other than defeating the boss enemies every 5-6 waves. So it's a real gamble if you will be able to survive the dungeon or just end your run that way. I choose the viking as my first character and got an archer skeleton as my minion. The minion AI is horrible or better almost non existent. He doesn't follow you, but instead wanders around aimlessly. Yet he does 4-5 times as much damage as I do. So I lure the enemies to him and hide behind him while he shoots the enemies (and bosses). I pretty much just gather coins and revive him if he dies.
When you level up you get 2 stat points which can increase your attack-per-second speed in the 0.01-0.02 range each point, your damage around 1 point, your armor percentage rating around 0.1% or your health for around 30-40 points. Investing in health seems to be the only viable option. It's a lot of grinding to gain a level and you only get a very minimal increase in you stats for that. You can find potions that increase your stats for this run, but they are randomized each run so you never know what a potion does until you try it for the first time. Of course there are a lot of potions with negative effects too so again it's just gambling.
The presentation is nice yet simple. The different level have their unique setting and there's a good amount of different enemies. Some of the bosses are much harder to defeat than others and again it's completely random which one you'll encounter. Only the amount of hit points changes depending in which level you face them.
Overall it's not a bad game, but it just doesn't feel balanced enough to be engaging. You can hit a lucky streak and get quite far or you'll just hit a brick wall in the first level. It's not skill, but pure luck.
