This is simply the best telltale game. It follows the same gameplay pattern first seen on The Walking Dead game with over the top presentation and a very well written and very funny story. It has plenty of QTEs, almost no items to grab and no open world exploration besides the rails of the scene being played.
. Graphics 8.5/10 - The graphics in this game are very close to the style used on The Walking Dead, therefore it is good, not great. I give this game one extra point due to its great over the top presentation.
. Audio 10/10 - The audio is simply great. The music clearly matches the scenes in play and what a great soundtrack this game has. The voice-over work is algo very good.
. Gameplay 8/10 - The usual telltale gameplay. Expect next to zero inventory items and puzzles, little exploration and lots of QTE. Do not get me wrong, I like this type of gameplay for a change. This game gets an extra point due to its "death" scenes. Truly funny.
. Story 10/10 - Intriguing well crafted story. This is usually where the greatest telltale strength lies. This game is no exception. Lots of misteries, chases, funny heroes and NPCs. I really laugh out loud from time to time playing this game.
. Overall 9/10 - I believe this game to be the best game from telltale. If you like the games they make, this one is no-brainer. If you are in doubt, give it a try. Do not expect a classic point and click/puzzle game.

Wolfenstein:  The New Order is the best of everything.
1.  It's a great shooter.  It varies between corridor-shooter and arena-shooter.  There are a wide variety of enemies who use a lot of different weapons and have different strengths, and who require different tactics to defeat them.
2.  There's a lot of variety of location:  insane asylum, prison, government building, military base, submarine, and even a moon base before reaching the final fortress.
3.  It has one of the best and most moving stories in gaming history.  The story has a beginning, middle and end.  It introduces the main villain in the first part of the game, and sets the final objective from the very beginning:  take down the villain.
There are two main paths depending on a choice you make early in the game, and it ultimately changes some of the characters you meet.
This is revenge story bound up with a very well-done love story.  There's a lot of tenderness in this story.
This game also has some very memorable characters.  Even minor characters are memorable.  As well, there are some very memorable set pieces in the plot.
The only negatives I can think of are:
1.  I felt that the choice in the beginning needed more of a difference between the two paths.  In one, you gain a hacking skill, and in the other, a lockpick skill.  This was badly under-utilized.  As well, there's an awkward moment in BOTH timelines facing anger from a comrade over the choice that was made.  It would have been nice if they hadn't reacted the same.
Other than that, the game is flawless.  It's fun, it's moving, it's memorable, and I've replayed this game at least four times since I bought it.  It's well-worth the money.

Was founder for original game at $50
A few months later it is on steam early release for $35. OK fine.
Game releases for $40.  Fine; founders paid for early access I guess
Then they decide to create a new stand alone game Escalation.  Only $20 more for founders.  No thanks to $70 total
Then steam sale for $30 for those late adopters.  (Founders $15 but I still said NOPE)
Now they gave it free.  Great I suppose unless you paid the $70 stupidly which I did not.
So now the game:
Campaign is a tutorial.  If you want Sup Commander campaign, this is not it.  Seroiusly, one of them is "more your unit across the map".
Game play.  They give you huge maps but super slow and expensive units and slow resources collection.  If you are attacked on the flank, forget getting there.  Expensive units and low resource collection means maintaining multiple fronts is very hard.  End result is a "blob".  Hopefully your blob meets the enemy blob otherwise you will never make it back to your base.
Also, this whole "stand alone" game thing is a joke.  Extra zoom and "upgradable" turrets is not a new game.
I should have known better after SINS (which was great game), the rebellion "stand alone game" was a $2 DLC that added 4 units.  They did the same thing here.
As an aside, I almost bought Gal Civ on steam sale but then saw 10 DLC for over $70.  I bet half are useless and rest are what should have been put into game to start with.
Never back another Stardock game again.  Just wait for reviews and steam sale.  Sadly, the blend of SupComm and SINS does not come together well in Escalation.

I generally do not Leave reviews for a game. Least of all for one in Early Access.
First and biggest issue and perhaps the only gripe that I have with this game is the instability of your saves between builds.
PRO TIP: If you are planning to have a modded playthrough(and you should ; totally revamps the gameplay) make a vanilla Save prior to adding any mods
Now for the actual review of this game.
I have spent a total of 128 hours in this game. making it my 4th most played game ever and that time is split between two playthroughs (the first one I had to end because of the aformentioned reason).
I generally do not admit to save-scumming,  but in this game, I did so shamelessly. Not because I was afraid of losing valuable members of my Tribe, but because I couldn't bear to continue without them. Spend enough time in this game and their patterns become yours. The "One more Day" rule applies here way more than your would first believe and soon  enough, the Sun in rising and even the Real World clock that you can enable in the HUD does little to nothing to stop this complusion to continue.
Now for the reason to Buy:
This game is Hard and random and gets harder and randommer the more you play. every decision you make creates a snowball and before you know it you have created this monster of a settlement cleared out one small tile at a time.
Reason Not to buy:
The level of involvement you get out of the game is based on the amount of time you invest in it. Seeing as the game is in early access, any update to the core Build or any mods that you might add could end up wasting hours of progress. Making that save unplayable (as in the save will not load). I went 3 months without playing pricesely for this very reason.
Final note.
Make sure you are willing to live with the decisions that you make in this game. The Following is the Story that unfolded in my Tribe that led me to get to the end game.
I was happy to keep on playing the game with no real end, even though I had my spaceship built. But my hand was forced.
I had 3 married couples in my tribe. One guy( I had named him The Miner as he was good at mining) started an affair with another female in the tribe ( causing destress to him and his wife and the female he was having an affair with). A few days past and the Miner's Wife started an affair with another Male member for the tribe. A few Bedroom Re-assignement later> The wife and husband are sleeping in different rooms with their lovers.
But the writing is on the wall. This can't continue and soon enough the relationships will keep on getting too complicated to the point where it would be just utter chaos.
So I load everyone except the Miner's Mistress into the pods and then right before lift off, I extract the guy Who was having the affair with The Miner's wife. I Didn't want for all of this effort to go to waste and thought it would be a good ending in paper atleast.
The last two members of the tribe, deciding to stay behind, with bountiful food and farmland and animals to take care off.
I though I would Imagine them living in this Rimworld, Providing sanctuary to those that need it most.
Only the game does not end with the launch.
The credits roll begining with list of people who made it out in the ship and who were left behind.
The usual thanks and what not continue.
The music keeps playing.
Then you are taken back to your settlement.
The game keeps on going.
And you are faced with your decision.
The stupidity of mine did not occur until I saw the two go into seperate rooms.
In my haste to get my first launch going, I left the two halfs of a Broken marraige that had nothing to do with each other.
They had little to no relationship with each other.
I check their social and see the name of their respective lover with (Dead) next to their name.
The realization dawn on me. For the ones who were left behind, the ones who left might as well be dead.
I quit the game. I need a Break from this. Don't even bother saving it.

It's not only my game of the year, it's one of the best games I have played. Mind you, I'm speaking in terms of the three main aspects that, for me, constitute a great game:
(1) Randomisation
(2) Challenge
(3) Mechanics
Galak-Z excels in each of these categories. Once you become accustomed to the control system, just flying the craft and navigating the enivornments alone is a sheer thrill. But it's more than that. It's about skillfully using the meticulously crafted control system to overcome a very steep challenge, and the satisfaction derived therein. It's about exulting in a stylish, efficient dogfight, and swallowing your own mistakes and learning from them. It's about perfecting your skills as a pilot, learning to pick your fights, and always coming back for more, because it's just that good.
If pressed, I'd call it a tough, arcade-space-shooter rogue-lite. If this genre appeals to you, you need Galak-Z in your life. I honestly can't see myself playing much else for the forseeable future. Highly, highly recommended for those who appreciate the genre.

You can easily tell that the development team are really passionate about this game, the communication back and forth with gamers in the Steam forum, the constant updates all comes together to show commitment. Sure everyone makes a miss step here and there and for Stardock their misstep was the first version of the game, nothing wrong with it, but 'Escalation' took the game to a whole new level making the first game almost obsolete.  It seemed to me the team was at odds with itself pushing and pulling and stumbling until they came up with the right choice and risky as it may be fearing a massive backlash from the PC community they decided to discontinue the first game and concentrate on 'Escalation'.
People who bought the first game and 'Escalation' are now treated to the season pass free to alleviate some of the negative feelings amongst the gaming community. But from what I have seen for this game the PC community is very forgiving, in fact I have seen nothing like it before, it's as if for this one game everyone agrees the foundation for greatness is there and together we can all take it to the next level.
Please do not get me wrong, the game looks amazing, it is very well optimised for a DX12 multi GPU config, but I have to be honest, if you are coming from C&C and wanting a meaty fun campaign you wont find it here at the moment, I say at the moment because the game is evolving even as I type this report. The meat of the game is in it's Skirmish and MP, although I am not confident enough to play it in MP yet I do enjoy the skirmish missions.
Bases for example could look better, could be larger, I mean there is much fun to be had destroying an enemy base but bases are lacking here, sure there are various builds, but they do not look meaty enough. Units look very similar to each other but they do look great, building a shield wall would be a welcome addition as you fend off against an attack force and that shield begins to fluctuate, now that would be awesome. I also miss ground units, grunts, sniper missions, if only the game had these elements
They are now opening the doors to modders, this should increase the lifespan of the game and I for one am looking forward to seeing what the amazingly talented modding community comes up with, especially from those modders coming from Supreme Commander.... ;)
If you love RTS games then this is a definite yes, the maps are baron and although they look great they lack detail, but it's one big playground of destruction and boy it has never looked as good as this. I also believe if you like RTS and see this game as a strong foundation to the next level then support this game so Stardock can continue to develop it...
Give the game a try, if you are an RTS fan the game deserves that much and I am sure once that Skirmish draws you in you will be hooked....

Galak-Z is an endearing game which pros easily outweigh its cons.
TL/DR-9/10
Pros:
1. Gameplay is incredibly fun and responsive, (I used 360 controller, I've read many enjoy the keyboard/mouse controls as well)
2. Rogue-like elements add a balanced difficulty which is "hard but fair"
3. Two difficulty options: arcade and rogue, only difference being when death occurs how far the player is set back (replay mission or have to restart entire mission set aka seasons) This feature adds extra incentive to play the game again, given its brevity this is a great feature.
4. Impressive AI, this certainly adds to the difficulty and thanks to the procedural nature of the game each replay has a different vibe altogether.
5. Variety, goes with point #4 store upgrades/loot are random, if playing rogue gamemode these can really change the dynamic of the game.
6. Beat the game your own way! The complexities of the combat are hard to see until you play for a while (need to get past first season) Combat or lack of combat is your choice, types of combat vary greatly from player to player eg sniping/melee etc. After you get used to your ship/mech you really start to feel like the anime pilots of old which can be a great feeling of nostalgia.
7. You get a Gundam!
===================
Bugs/Glitches
So far I've only noticed two bugs worth noting.
1. Occasionally a small lag spike occurs usually in combat (this could be my setup however others have reported this stutter) EDIT this bug hasn't happend to me in several hours, this issues was a big one on PS4 but the PC version seems to have fixed this /EDIT
2. In arcade mode Season 2 episode 5- if failed would, upon restarting, get stuck on the loading screen. Exiting game and reloading allowed mission to be played again; however in my experience if failed again the same issue occurred. ****Mine was fixed by verifying the cache.*** EDIT Has been fixed in second Patch /EDIT
***Edit*** 3. "Missiles, Who Needs 'Em?" achievement bugged. Dev replied and will have this fixed by the next patch. This isn't the first achievement for this game to have issues, hopefully they will be ironed out in the second patch. Thankfully achievements don't effect gameplay so I wouldn't let this sway your purchase. 11/3-These have now been fixed.
===================
Cons
1. Level design is pretty but the environments get reused quite often. Usually an industrial asteroid, "bio-asteroid", and their respective debris fields are your main areas.
2. Missions, dialogue, "plot" also get repetitive. Each season has 5 episodes, usually episode 1 and 5 have a set plot whereas 2,3,4 are random insert basic mission here situations. The dialogue is well done, however the combat dialogue gets really repetitive. You will hear some lines ten times per episode easily.
3. Brevity of the game, it's not the longest game but as previously stated there is some replay value here, at the very least i'd recommend doing a play-through of each game mode. Depending on the player and circumstance this can easily put you over 10 hours.
4. *This one isn't much of a con for me but it's worth mentioning/also highly subjective to each person* Story/animation is kind of hit and miss for me. The game doesn't take itself seriously and some of the campy dialogue is pretty funny. However as many have said it feels a bit more western than its anime intent. Personally I'm not a big fan, it looks and feels like a very cheap poorly drawn comic book. Thankfully this is one of those games where you don't play it for the story, on the other hand the addition of the Admiral was a welcome one.
5. Season 5 has yet to be released (will be free and hopefully by the end of the year) so its a bit of "hurry up and wait" if you are really having a good time.
=================
Some things I'd like to see in no specific order
-Remappable controller inputs (not a large issue as an emulator can be used if needed)
-Ability to sell upgrades at reduced rate for extra scrap.
-Endless or "binge mode", currently after you complete seasons 95% of what you have accumulated disappears, carryover of upgrades/scrap between seasons would be an interesting addition. (a limitation on scrap accumulation would be required as the difficulty would quickly become trivial otherwise) It would also give you yet another reason to do a play-through.
-Extreme hardcore mode, this game certainly is difficult but an even scarier difficulty would add some extra incentive to keep playing a great game. After 20 hours in game the fourth season's difficulty is still very challenging, but the first three seasons don't benefit from this extra difficulty.
-Some kind of leaderboard/multiplayer nod would be interesting. When I think of old school arcade games I always remember seeing the old leaderboards with the initials I'm somewhat surprised that is missing. I always love coop in games however I don't know how much that would contribute to this game as well as greatly increase difficulty of production. That being said I think it would be great fun to play with friends like Raiden Trad back in the old days.
-A stats and general info page, including best run for each season, kills of each faction/specific enemy. Preferred killing method etc etc. Also a more indepth information page on enemy ships and mechs.
-Greater player customization to effect ship/mech aesthetic. Currently if you change the ship's blaster it adds effects like fire/ice/scatter shot etc out of necessity. Mech upgrades/passives changing the appearance would be pretty cool; different colored sword, different boosters, and unlockable mech/ship skins things like that.
================
Summary
I've been excited to get my hands on Galak-Z since I heard about it coming to PS4 and it has certainly been worth the wait. It really brings me back to my youth with an old meets new school approach to gameplay as well as characters, units, and abilities that remind me of 80's anime like Macross/Robotech and especially Mobile Suit Gundam. The gameplay is very well done so much so that it really overshadows almost all of the game's faults. The plot, animation, and in game dialogue are subjective weak points for me, but very easy to overlook as the gameplay is just so exceptional. Finally this game brings me back to a time where I didn't need a competitive multiplayer in every game, nor did I need an open world story that had to last me sixty hours. This game would be a great pickup at any price but if its sub $15 you really owe it to yourself to give this game a shot. Thank you for reading my book, I hope you enjoy the game.

The premise is pretty simple, and as far as plot goes, pretty bare.
TL;DR You are the last surviving starfighter of an earth fleet. While you managed to make off with a prototype fighter, everyone else wasn't so lucky. You link up with the last functioning cap ship and her captain in and effort to make it back to earth. There are some plot things in between, but that's the gist.
Galax-Z Is very roguelike. During seasons (5 missions each) The damage your fighter takes is permanent and must be repaired. YOu can spend money on upgrades as well as extra missiles, but salvage is scarce and leads to situations on whether its safe to jump an Imperial patrol or opt to try sneaking past them and risking taking extra damage you'll have to spend resources fixing. There are two difficulty settings, the more masochistic one has you going through all 5 episdoes of the seasons without any deaths. In the case that you do die, you are forced to start over from the beginning. Ther is also a more arcade-y variant, where you can just restart after each stage you died on.
I think the game does a good job of easing you into things, (except the upgrade you get start of season 2) and its incredibly satisfying to cream enemies who would previously kill you endlessly as you improve. The creative enemy AI can lead to some really cool game moments, like Luring one group of enemies into another opposing faction, sparking a three-way slugfest, or using your enviroment against the enemy. All in all I would say it's a definate purchase worth having if you enjoy SHMUPS or Roguelikes. If you happen to be a fan of Stuff like macross, robotech, or gundam, this would be up your alley as well - it has many throwbacks to that genre, in more ways than one.

In its hey day this game was probably lined up and armed to become one of the most "fun" competitive creative based "building" game... with everything from OP one shot set ups (with proper counters) to straight up BOSS BATTLES where you and 10-20 people whent up against someone of a higher lvl's mega ship.... it was EPIC and fun for both sides... then... they changed the game... and it got worse with each update...
i dont know what order the horrific changes that murderd the enjoyability of this game were as i left it for a bit due to... internet issues... but im going to list the changes that KILLED this game for me..
before i start i just want to say balancing in my eyes is ONLY good for a game when there is ZERO counter and everyone is using the same strat... because broken wackey tactics that are op.... not only add fun but make being creative (which is what this game seems to stress) actualy rewarding... now onward to the list
1. making everyone have the same CPU cap... if you dont know this is the limit to the size of your robot... before it was based on your level... with a very high level cap you could get some pretty monsterously sized robots... with crazy strats.. and build options... this also allowed you to be very creative with what you robot actualy looked like.. in one boss battle i remember seeing what looked like an old iron clad battle ship it was devestatingly awsome...
2. making weapons fire seperatly / acting as a single weapon... so basicly how weapons used to work is that when you put guns on your robot you added their damage their firerate and so on... now if you put more then one of a single type of weapon you are simply adding increased fire rate.. Thats it... for instance you used to be able to cram a bunch of plasma cannons on your robot and fire them all at once doing devastating damage hard to aim due to the weapon drop and often unreliable because they take time to fire again but still its far better then just having it up the fire rate... it rewards players finding how how to cram the most weapons onto their robot without killing its mobility
3. the energy system... im ok with this change but it still massivly limits you as EVERYONE has the same energy limits the massive guns (which are WAY too big since you can only get a cpu of 2k ie.. the look super derpy unless you use them in a perticuler manner) but you can only sustain their fire for a short time then thats it your done you either have to run for your life or hope they dont shoot them off before you get enouph energy to do another volley which mind you takes time... this creates a meta that i have noticed... its ether you go big weapons and burst (which mind you NEVER kills someone making KSing WAY too easy).. or you try and make the fastest robot you can and run circles around them blasting with small cheap weapons (which takes forever... often times they can just run back to their base and regen)
their used to be a game i played called final fantasy tactics war of the lions... this was a single player game.. but non the less a BRILLIANT game.. it was both balanced and broken... it rewarded players on using clever combos and strategys that could DECAMATE the enemy... when balancing is taken too far its like going to your childs baseball game and watching him get a trophy for losing... fair is not fun... when people get their asses handed to them they dont give up they change thier tactics...

. Gameplay 8/10 - The usual telltale gameplay. Expect next to zero inventory items and puzzles, little exploration and lots of QTE. Do not get me wrong, I like this type of gameplay for a change. This game gets an extra point due to its "death" scenes. Truly funny.
. Story 10/10 - Intriguing well crafted story. This is usually where the greatest telltale strength lies. This game is no exception. Lots of misteries, chases, funny heroes and NPCs. I really laugh out loud from time to time playing this game.
. Overall 9/10 - I believe this game to be the best game from telltale. If you like the games they make, this one is no-brainer. If you are in doubt, give it a try. Do not expect a classic point and click/puzzle game.

To start, if you are looking to get a Borderlands game, this is not what you want. Borderlands 2 GOTY is the same price, with far more content, better graphics, better story, gameplay improvements, and closer to true Steam integration. This game is older, and really shows the age. Securom and Gamespy features were only removed in 2014. B-lands 2 is just better.
I like the idea of an FPS-RPG. The execution here is mediocre, with weak weapons and bullet-sponge enemies. Normal RPGs raise stats with levels, so your character strengthens independent of loot. Here, RPG elements are just 1 active ability and a pitiful tree of uninteresting passives. Your health pool does increase with levels, but shields make health pointless. The main damage scaling not based on random drops is the weapon-type level. However, this system just pushes you to use 1 type of weapon entirely, or lose damage by switching to a new type. This makes the Eridian class of weapons feel weak, as they will be level 1 in the last third of the game. In dozens of hours, at character level 47, I still haven't maxed out the shotgun type despite using shotguns most of the game.
Shooter fans will likely be underwhelmed here, as the combat is unsatisfying with RPG variables. One-hit kills are rare, and bosses have no unique skills to challenge players. My RPG side is also bored, as the progression system is meaningless. I've only had a few pieces of high-level loot to look forward to equipping. Everything is guns, shields, and class mods, so it's easy to establish a full build that will last for days as you wrap up the game.
As for wrapping the game up, it seems the developers didn't want you to finish it anytime soon. Many of the DLC quest lines involve grinding up hundreds to thousands of random drops, or fighting the same bosses again and again, or grinding reused enemies for 6 hours straight in the Arena. The game's visual style is unique, but becomes bland after seeing the same areas and reused assets and repeated enemies. Add onto that the same repeating jokes from said repeating enemies, and I hope you didn't want anything new in the last dozen hours of gameplay.
The ideas may have been unique in 2008, but the game failed to take real chances even on release. Destiny seems to suffer some of the same design issues, turning gameplay into a grind. If you want a co-op shooter, I'd really recommend Payday 2. If you HAVE to jump on a loot treadmill of junk weapons, see Borderlands 2. If you can live without FPS, go for a real MMORPG. This game, however, is still overpriced and the sequel is a better game.

A match three game. Beating it on normal took about five hours.
The goal of the game is to construct wonders. That takes resources which you get by matching gems. You can only get a limited amount of resources per level so you have to play about seven levels to complete a wonder. That is if you manage to get the maximum amount of resources every level. If not, you have to complete more levels. Each wonder also requires you to complete two minigames. The minigames have to be unlocked by collecting keys while playing the levels.
To complete a level, you have to break background tiles by matching gems on top of them. After the tiles are all broken, a special gem appears that you have to get all the way to the bottom by matching the gems underneath it. Once the special gem reaches the bottom, the level is complete. You also have a time limit, but I do not know what happens if you run out of time since it never happened to me.
The levels vary in shape and the amount of background tiles that need to be broken increases as you go along. The background tiles also become more durable, requiring multiple matches to break. There are also special abilities you can use that recharge when you match gems. Matching four or more gems spawns special gems that can clear whole rows at a time.
To put it all together, you start playing a level. You match gems until you have collected the minigame keys and maxed your resources. Then you break all the background tiles. Then you lower the special gem to the bottom of the screen, completing the level. Now you can spend your resources on building the wonder. Then rinse and repeat until the wonder is complete. Then you start a new wonder. It's a simple diversion that kept my attention for the scant few hours I played it.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fun, albeit mixed bag:
Pros:
+fairly good graphics
+hits 60FPS mostly at 1080p max settings on a GTX 1060 6GB (more on that in cons)
+weapon handling is good
+animations are smooth
+good menus/customisation
+characters with some depth
+good sound design
+several difficulty levels
+interesting story (subjective, I guess)
+you get to kill Nazi's, robot Nazis, Nazi dogs, and robot Nazi dogs
Neutral:
•FOV adjustable in menus in intervals of 10 degrees; from 80 to 100. Neutral because lower-end PC's would benefit from something like 65 FOV for more frames and people with higer end machines/people that get motion sickness from low FOV would benefit from 120+ FOV, but I find anything between 90 FOV and 120 FOV is perfect
•Due to idTech 5 engine, VSync must be enabled to avoid horrendous screen tearing on the bottom half of the screen during any type of camera movement, and VSync introduces noticeable input lag on menus, but I don't really feel it ingame which is why it's neutral
•Accuracy with some guns feels off, especially when ADS. Shots seem to land an inch above where I'm aiming, even when tap or burst firing. Neutral because hipfiring doesn't seem to have the issue, and it's a viable choice to go through the game without aiming
•Minibosses that can instant kill. I believe the only thing that should be able to instant kill you is an environmental hazard i.e cliff, pool of lava, etc, but I guess it might add a sense of challenge for some people.
Cons:
-idTech 5 engine,
-Due to idTech 5, texture streaming is poor; if you look left and right too fast you'l see pop-in from low LOD to high LOD models and textures
-AI isn't as smart as desired
-Hotwiring is somewhat annoying on low DPI/sensitivity
-No Anti-aliasing options in the menus; you'll have to force it in drivers.
-Film grain on with no toggle or slider in the menus
-Game struggles to keep to a locked 60FPS on a GTX 1060 6GB at 1080p when Vsynced, and does jump around a fair bit in intense fight scenes.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a good game, albeit with flaws inherent in the engine and a few things that I personally don't like that others might enjoy. I give it a 7.5/10 and would recommend to anyone that likes or wants to get into a classic FPS like Doom 1/2, Quake or Wolfenstein 3D but doesn't want to try something with dated graphics. Hell, I'd recommend it to anyone who likes FPS games full stop. Bought it during the Steam Summer Sale 2017 for $10, and I'm more than likely going to get more than 10 hours out of it.

Out of all the Farm Frenzy games, Farm Frenzy 3 is the one to get. It is, by far, the most comprehensive Farm Frenzy games of the series.

It's a mini-game fueled "farm tycoon" game with none of the meta-game, and Popcap-style arcade play.
Farm Frenzy 3 trasnports us to various locations around the globe, managing different farms in different regions. Each location is slightly different, but the mechanics remain the same. There is a light narrative going on top of the game where your character, Scarlett is the girl in charge.
I was a little disappointed that Scarlett represents a white colonialist business model, engaging in questionably clandestine practices in economically less-developed regions, but this game is for 6 year olds.

7 Wonders: Magical Mystery Tour is one of many tile matching games in the 7 Wonders series. There are seven levels in total with each level having several sub levels. In each level there are also two mini games which you can finish to get gold and statues with which to decorate the wonder you're building. To build them, you must match tiles in lines of three or more. A match larger than three tiles rewards you with special tiles. Clearing the tiles also rewards you by powering up special powers.

: In this game, you've been hired by the gods to build various buildings/cities of myth and legend.

: The art assets are pretty good, though the multiple colours of the tiles in later levels can be a bit overwhelming due to there being so many on the board at once.

: The music and sound fx are simple, but pleasing to listen to. They do get a bit samey towards the end, but they're also easy to tune out.

:  It took me about 5 hours to complete the game. For the price, this isn't too bad.

: There isn't much in the way of replayability in this game. Once you've completed all the levels and          beat the two mini games in each level, that's pretty much all there is.
This game is simple and casual in nature. If you like matching games, I recommend it. Due to it not having much, if any, replayability however, only get it when it's on sale.

This is probably one of the best Arcade Kart Racers of all time, and my second favorite behind Crash Team Racing (for nostalgia's sake)
This game feels like a cross between Mario Kart and Jak-X with a bit of Star Fox 64 thrown in for good measure, the controls are incredibly snappy and drifting is smoother than a cashmere codpiece. I was worried that much like mario kart, the challenge of the game would dissapate once you have gotten quite proficient at it, but I was pleasently surprised to find that a fourth difficulty is introduced once you get far enough into the game.
The Transforming feature of this game I initially assumed to be a gimmick, but in actuality It forms an integral part of what makes this game great; the speedboat style parts have realistic water physics (not to mention that the water looks great too), the flight sections of tracks are well designed so that you dont get lost and the flight physics do not take days to figure out (in fact I picked them up almost instantly [after a little oh the vertical is reversed moment]) unlike some games such as battlefield.
The Variety of different game types is pleasant; race, battle race, battle arena, etc. however the time trial style mini games in the world tour such as drift challange and traffic attack (which are good fun) cannot be played on all of the tracks.
Four of the 21 tracks in the game are direct ports from the previous game, they are fairly good tracks so I can overlook this, one of these is a paid DLC that comes with metal sonic. Honestly I feel this DLC should have been free, but compared to the other DLCs which are literally just extra characters it makes some sense. So completionists beware, if you really want to get every unlock in the game you will need to spend just under $5.00 extra to get those karts.
The Graphics in this game; while its not a super duper high-end eye-gasm inducing system-melting dx11 masterpiece, the visuals are very pleasing, it is seamless and themed well, at times you may see a couple of low-res textures or low-polycount models in the backround, reminding you that this is a console port but nothing that takes away from the playing experience.
Oh, Yeah thats right, this is a console port! and before you turn tail and run sceaming to your copy of Crisis 3 and proceeding to clutch it while shivering in the corner; It is a wonderfully optimised port, solid 60fps and absolutley no stuttering, input lag or any other issues often asscosiated with console ports (cough.. cough... Trials Fusion).
SEGA have been doing a lot of great ports of late, good job you show 'em how its done!
I did own the previous game; Sonic & Sega All Stars Racing on Wii briefly, it was laggy, difficult to control and not at all fun to play, but I suppose thats just down to motion control and >30fps that you get with a wii, but Mario Kart Wii played much better than that, so Idk. The point i'm trying to make is that before purchasing All-Stars Transformed I was highly skeptical of it being any good, and well I guess I couldn't have been more wrong.

I've put in at least 11 hours with this game, so I'm still pretty new and that should say a lot to those looking to buy it.
For starters, Squad is extremely immersive and you should be prepared...no...you should definitely take your time fiddling with your bindings for intense gunfights and spend a good amount of time getting a feel for each weapon at the training map.
Next, be prepared to learn if you jump in actual game; the squad-leaders that you have (if they're good) typically do not have time to explain every facet of the game to you, so take the time to check out the youtube videos posted for a simulated boot-camp experience (hopefully they add an actual in-game bootcamp to get everyone up to speed).
Finally, keep your head on a swivel. Communicate. And be prepared to get lit up - verbally and in-game ammo-ily(sp?). It's a hard game.
For the most part, I'd give the game - at it's current stage - a 7/10.
Pros:
-Realistic and immersive.
-Great graphics, gun play, and sounds
-Addicting and relentless for hardcore game lovers
-Load of fun if you can actually find a server with enough people to make it competitive and satisfying when you finally take out an BTR/Sniper/Squad.
Cons:
-On the fly learning, no formal teaching or tutorial of the game within the game (aside from signs posted in the training map)
-No option to kick squad leaders who just don't live up to the role.
-Toxicity is pretty common if you end up skipping tutorials and your gameplay shows it
-Servers are far and few in-between. Every good server is full, every empty server stays empty, and hardly any U.S. supported servers so you end up having to take a ping hit and end up getting wiped by a Russian or Korean.
Conclusion:
Buy this game if you enjoy hardcore realistic gameplay and can handle waiting in queues for a good server for at least 8 minutes. The wait is worth it if you have a great squad leader and squad, but it also gets frustrating not having server support for US players, no bootcamp to teach new players, and the lack of overall game knowledge present by devs - in game. Also, buy this if you're okay with all of that and the fact that it's still practically in beta.
Don't buy this game if you think that you won't have the time to put into learning the intricacies of gameplay, don't like spending money on an unfinished game, or do not like waiting for server spots to open up just to play.

In my first play through during a cold snap a Muffalo self tamed itself then walked across the map, walked into my base and curled up beside the heater. "Screw this - way too cold out here... I'm going to be your pet now and sleep in the warmth". Great game!
6 Months later I came back to the game. I did a full playthrough taking my colony from start to building a ship and leaving. It took me about 60 hours. This is truly a masterpiece of a game and it's still only in Early Access.
Worth every penny of the price - there's a lot of depth to the characters, game and story than you might think. Especailly when you include friends and family members as part of your colony. The story of course is made up from the events that happen and your own creation of the story in a sense.
During my 60 hour playthrough there were times of joy, excitement, fear, sadness and more. A few of the story highlights that I recall during that:
- The many times my wife the pyro would go off and start setting parts of the base on fire when she was upset. One time she even lit me on fire while I was sleeping in our bed. After the skin graft I always slept with one eye open.
- The "beautiful" 76 year old female, gay, pop star that ran from pirates and sought shelter with us. She refused to do anything but be social and artisitic so we had no choice but to stick her in a small room and craft sculptures day in and day out that we could sell to traders. She was fine with it even up to her nearly fatal heart attack when she turned 80 while hauling some limestone blocks to her workbench.
- My father who had always had heart issues finally had a major heart attack which my wife treated and during the treatment he felt it was a fitting time to try asking her on a date. (thanks dad, that's not creepy at all)
- My buddy who was born a builder was forced into the medical profession out of necessity. And over time gained some decent skills in it. After my father had a heart attack he took it upon himself to build a replacement heart for him. The first time he tried to do the surgery to replace his heart the knife must have slipped so the oppertion failed and put my father out of commision for days to heal. (Perhaps it had to do with him missing a few fingers). But refusing to accept failure he crafted another heart and tried again ...which also failed. At that point he gave up the medical profession and went back to work banging boards together for the rest of his days.
- My dad used to be a fine hunter despite always getting gravely wounded by his prey, it was his sole prefession up until he lost both his arms. I then devoted my time to discovering how to make prosthetics for him meanwhile he spent weeks moping around the base as the designated switch flicker (I assume he used his nose) since he literally couldn't do anything else. Once we stuck a couple broom sticks into his arm sockets to act as arms we made him the dedicated cook.
- It took nearly a year to build the ship for them to escape and right before it was completed was the biggest siege they had ever experianced. Everyone fought hard knowing that winning this fight meant their freedom. Many were wounded, some on the brink of death. Med beds had to be made in the field to treat the wounded but they fought off the attack. As the wounded recovered the ship was completed and everyone was told to get in. We had to leave now as the enemy attacks were only getting stronger. If we waited we may not survive another attack. Everyone loaded up, my character kissed his wife one last time on the planet and said they would see each other again when the ship landed which would only feel like a moment but could be thousands of years. Once everyone was in the ship took off and not a moment too soon. Credits rolled then was put back in the game to watch what would become of the once thriving base that was home to my colonists for many years.
- Two months after the colony left the base sat partially ruined and deserted, gradually things starting to break down. Until a lone person came running up away from a band of a dozen pirates. He saw the base from the distance and it must have looked like a safe haven, standing walls, a few turrets - surely here he could find salvation and some friends. He quickly ran inside and saw no one. The first order of business was to nab a pair of shoddy pants that were on the floor to cover his naked butt. With the pirates baring down there wasn't a moment to waste, he grabbed the first gun he saw and ran out to man the mortar station. He had never fired a fun before and was a horrible shot but still had to try. BLAM BLAM... a couple lucky hits took a few out but the rest were busting down the last of the turrets and the door. He continued to fire even directly into the base (he could always rebuild) fires started. Once inside the pirates were more interested in slaughtering the pig pets that remained after the colony left and trashing the place. The battle lasted a full day until one found their way out to the mortar station where the lone survivor was, ready for a shootout. Back and forth the shots fired trading hit for hit, no one of his pirate friends knew he had found this survivior. Just at that moment the pirate leader shouted out "ok guys let's get outta here there's not left for us" and as that happened the pirate in the shootout took one final shot that sadly was a headshot and gravely downed the last survivor who then bled out as the rest of the base was consumed by fire. Fortunately he didn't suffer it didn't take long for the flames to reach the pille of mortar shells which exploded and vaporized him instantly.
- After that, and when the base was reduced to rubble, raiders came numerous times, but finding nothing they would merely trash anything not already burned or broken and left. Their numbers got less and less each time. Perhaps word was traveling that there was nothing here...
- Nearly a year after the last survivor died another came, this one was only being chased by a single raider carrying a club (which was odd since they had 0 skill with melee). The survivor again thinking the base would be salvation came rushing in... they saw all the corpses and burned remnants - shocked and disappointed there wasn't time to waste. A glint in the distance caught their eye - a single machine gun somehow miraculously had survived the fallout. He ran and grabbed the gun with the pirate just on his heels. He had the upper hand now being a skilled marksman. Freedom was almost assured. But then a pack of manhunting raccoons appeared and started to attack. Perhaps running on pure addrenaline he managed to kill them all with his newly acquired gun as they bit off popular parts of his anatomy. Bloodied and shaking from the shock the pirate then burst it. The survivor starting shooting but was missing like crazy, perhaps from the blood loss and shock from the raccoon attack. The pirate managed to close the gap only taking a few glancing bullets that just grazed the skin. Fortunately his inexperiance with the club would be his down fall. He got a couple good hits in but mostly his swings were easily dodged as shots from the gun were returned. And finally a decisive shot to the lung was all it took. The pirate was down. Fortunately he was carrying  a med kit because if he hadn't been the survivior would have surely died from blood loss in a matter of hours.
- After the battle the survivor was in shock and didn't know what to do first so he grabbed a broom and started to sweep up all the debris. After a couple hours he came to his senses and started to secure things that were needed to survive, shelter, bed, food... A couple days passed and another female colonist joined - now it was all to easy, they just had to clean up, rebuild and get the hell off this rock.
Of course there was a lot more to this story but you might as well get the game and live out your own story!

I purchased Season of 12 Colors back in March on a whim, primarily owing to the beautiful art. I knew basically nothing about the story or premise, other than that there was secondary content that was vital to the full enjoyment of the game. Being an impulse buy it has sat in my library for several months, and it wasn't until today that I finally sat down to play it.
Season of 12 Colors is a short, (almost) linear Chinese visual novel. A complete playthrough of the game would take around 90 minutes, maybe slightly longer depending on your reading speed. The style of the story is sort of a cross between Narcissu and Shan Gui, and thematically it has some similarity with
. If you are familiar with either Narcissu or
, you may realize these are not stories which are known for being particularly cheerful.
The story starts out innocently and pleasantly enough, but by the time you have finished the main story things have taken on a somewhat more depressing or sombre tone. If you complete all the auxiliary content (and make one choice which may require the assistance of a guide), the story does end on a happier note, but I still couldn't call this game lighthearted.
In the beginning I thought I knew what the plot twist was going to be, but boy was I wrong. Season of 12 Colors kept me guessing throughout, and most importantly kept me engaged; I wanted to understand the backstory, and I wanted to see how it ended. The writing is extremely solid and well paced. The translation is very well done. There are some minor grammatical oddities , but nothing that takes away from the experience. In just an hour and a half Season of 12 Colors manages to develop its cast of characters better than most visual novels many times its length.
The character art and backgrounds are a delight to look at, and the music - while somewhat limited - is very poignant and fits the story well. The voice acting also deserves praise. Not all dialogue is voiced, in particular the main character is not voice acted, but I did not feel this was detrimental to the game.
It's difficult to explain why I recommend Season of 12 Colors without spoiling the experience. It's a beautifully crafted, sometimes bittersweet story that I think most people will be very satisfied with. I also think the less you know about the game going in, the better, with perhaps the exception being that you should make sure to read all of the secondary content which unlocks upon completing the main story.

This review's for the Dwarf Fortress fans out there.  RimWorld's definitely inspired by that classic game.
Micromanaging colonists with something like the Dwarf Therapist tool?  Check!
Colonists form relationships with one another?  Check!
Unhappiness and bad moods if something happens to a friend or lover?  Check!
Tantrum spirals?  Check and check!
Colonists have varying preferences?  More for broad categories than something specific, but yes!
Art that reflects events in the colony?  Check!
Devs release a fully playable game but still only consider it an "alpha"?  Check!  (Latest, as of March 2017, is Alpha 16)
Instead of DF's Tolkein-esque world, RimWorld is set in a far future where humanity has reached the stars and civilizations have risen and fallen on a planet.
You get three scenarios, plus a scenario editor to make your own or tweak the originals.  I've onlly tried the first one so far.
The first is the "classic" RimWorld scenario, three crashed survivors of a blown-up passenger liner.  Very random choices of personalities and strengths, but you're not locked out of any task category at the start.  (Some colonists are incapable of doing intellectual or "dumb" work, or a specific task category.)
The second is one insane but very rich explorer.  They get lots of gold for trading, which includes slavers to help populate the colony, and advanced defensive tech.
The third is a breakaway faction from one of the other established factions.  This is the closest to DF's own classic starting scenario.
You then can choose from one of three "storyteller" AIs, which characterize how the difficulty ramps up.  Cassandra Classic is a classic linear progression.  Phoebe Chillax is easier on you at the start, but eventually catches up to Cassie.  Randy Random, is, well, random, hitting you with either extreme.
Then there are sub-settings for relative intensity, ranging from easy to extreme.  The easiest setting leaves only moods, including berserk killing sprees, and animals going simlarly mad.  And, of course, death by starvation, illness, and bloodloss.  Basebuilder adds in raids from pirate factions and the more minor dangers of Normal level.
You do get to choose your landing site.  For that Dwarf Fortress cliff fort experience, choose a Mountainous site.  One side of the map is always going to be a cliff to dig into.
The latest alpha, 16, cast the site choice map as half a planet.  Latitudes function here.  You can choose a temperate forest zone and still be subjected to hot summers or very chilly winters.
DF's dwarves run on beer.  You get beer here, but also other drugs, ranging from recreational to ones that boost performance but are super addictive.  Colonists might already be addicted, and others are teetotalers.  You can set drug policies, and, of course, just not make the stuff.  But the drug trade is very profitable . . .
You can have advanced tech, as implied by the whole spacefaring thing.  Your crashed passengers land with guns for hunting and defense.  Electricity is in this game, too, from woodburning generators to solar panels to geothermal generators that harness the steam geysers on every map.  One endgame is to get off the planet, which includes being able to build your own spaceship.
To that end, you get a research table and tech tree.  I have yet to survive long enough to begin that process.  (Too busy trying to make and store enough food to last the winter and setting up other parts of the base.)  Even the breakaway faction, which starts out as tribal, can research up to spacefaring.
Also, advanced technological dangers lurk in many maps, sealed away in collapsed ruins.
And, unfortunately, no Z-levels, just the surface map.
My biggest complaint is that it is difficult to grow the colony's population.  No mass groups of migrants appearing here.   One of the main ways offered is to capture travelers passing through and then recruit them.  Another common way is that someone is fleeing another faction and if you agree to give them safety, you need to fight off the raiders following them.  I did also the occasional wanderer.
The other complaint is that, with just three people to start, you really need to keep juggling the work priorities and micromanage them to get much done quickly or precisely where you want.
Oh, and don't bother waiting for a discount.  Over a dozen games on my wishlist waiting for Christmas gift cards, and RimWorld was the only one without any discount at all.  Not even 10% !

So i got this game on a whim, because one of the tags is Rouge-Like and the user reviews i read were overall pretty positive and made it sound really good.
+The gameplay is good and it works well with my controller.
+Each character feels somewhat different, although they all play the same hit and run style with most enemies.
+The levels are well designed, most levels have loops, hidden areas are fairly easy to notice. There are some fall into acid/lava levels but its fine because you have double jump.
+Dropped items like bombs, hearts, mana orbs and keys are not thrown at you endlessly, but you can end up with a big disparity of items gained depending on your luck.
+The music is really good.
+The art style works well with the game.
-Characters feel a bit slippery because of high movement speeds that you can get.
-The levels although well designed get stale with nothing really changing, just the overall layout floor to floor.
-Bosses are a joke and a waste of time, the only difficult boss i encountered playing was the 2nd major boss, but once you know its moves it becomes easy like the rest.
-Lack of enemy diversity, there are only a few types of enemies, e.g. Zombie, Bats, Skulls and slugs.
-Some Special items are unclear as to what they do, there is no real way of knowing with them unless you get the requirement for them to work. But there are some pretty good ones, like the spike friend and the item that lets you see in the dark (shows whats behind doors).
-The equipment system is confusing at first. When you find a new item it is hard to tell if it is actually increasing your stats or is just a +1 attack weapon. This should be cleared up by putting its actual attack value with a + or a - depending on what you have equiped. Shields are confusing to get better ones as well, i had one shield that every other shield encountered would appear worse even when it was at 1% durability.
Overall i think its a fun game, but i don't think there is enough to keep me playing it for any period of time. Its a rouge-like/lite in terms of the map and enemies being procedurally generated but it doesn't feel like it changes all that much.

The Silent Age was not what I expected it to be.  I didn't read the page description at all (you should go do that) and rather thought it was just a game about 70s kitsch and that was that.  Instead, I was entreated to a pretty interesting sci-fi story wrapped around a pretty simplistic adventure game.
As far as the story goes, it's a typical romp through time as you guide Joe, a somewhat naive, yet genre-savvy janitor on a quest to save the world.  Nothing done here will blow your mind, but the key piece is a little hand-held time machine that goes forward and back a static amount of time.  Throughout the game, there is no formal (that I remember) statement of how much a span of time that is, but it does change from time to time as the story progresses.
With regards to the game, it's pretty simple.  On the plus side, there's very little "adventure game logic", so you won't need to spend any time attempting to combine items together or walking up to NPCs and exhausting conversation trees.  Instead, the game - a mobile port - is quite straightforward as far as its puzzles go.  They are not in any way difficult to figure out and their solutions are pretty much find an object, apply that object, then proceed.  Whether this is positive or negative is subjective, but I will say that anyone looking for challenging puzzles won't find them here.  They entire premise of the game is time travel, so expect that to play heavily into the solutions.
All that being said, I can't say that MSRP is a fair price for what amounts to approximately two hours of your time, but I suppose it's no larger than the price of admission to a movie.  However, if you do happen upon a pretty good deal, I'd say go ahead and seize it.  Again, it's not a very long game, nor is it a frusrating one.  This is more about how much you enjoy the story of the game and whether or not you are interested enough to see it through to the end.  At times it can be dark, but nothing scary or out of the ordinary occurs - the game faithfully describes its ruleset and sticks to it.  Nothing bad about that.
I will take a sidebar here and note that the vector art is wonderfully rendered and nothing will ever make you say "wha?"  The art is beautiful in its own way and is both detailed and minimal at the same time.  More importantly, it serves the story well, and the haunting tunes ensure that the atmosphere is appropriately melancholy and lonely.  And make no mistake, while there are a few NPCs peppered throughout the game's short run, this is very much a lonely adventure for our friend Joe, even right up till the very end.
Like I said, the game sets its rules and sticks to them.  I think the Silent Age plays extremely well to its themes and does not betray them.  It's hard to say more without diving into the ending, but this is a review, not an analysis.  As far as that goes, if you have the chance to get this on the cheap, a hearty recommend, my friends.

TLDR:
+ good AI
+ beautiful graphics
+ large armies
+ not as twitchy as StarCraft
+ good skirmish customization
+ viable defenses
+ good but not exceptional SP campaign
+ good amount of maps
- beefy hardware needed
- difficult to distinguish units
- UI / usability not quite where SC is (yet!)
You might like it if you:
+ like Supreme Commander
+ prefer a slower approach to RTSes
+ like comp stomping alone or with friends
+ like thousands of units on the screen at the same time.
You better skip it if you:
- like StarCraft
- don't like the SciFi setting
- buy the game for its narrative / SP campaign
- have a potato for a PC to run this on.
It has been said before, but Ashes is quite the spiritual successor to Supreme Commander. The focus is more on the strategic side, rather than the hectic button mashing that is found in StarCraft-like games. Armies move quite slowly, defenses are viable and unit abilities are "centralised" in "orbital" abilities. Although the game offers a campaign mode and various scenarios, the main focus is on skirmish maps. These skimishes offer a vast amount of options to adjust the rules to your liking (like no air units, defensive bonuses etc.). You can win games by eliminating the enemies HQ or by accumulating victory points by holding special locations. I could swear the AI was adapting its army composition to counter my armies and defenses.
The developer is known for supporting their games for a very long time and when you take a look at their design documents, you find that there is still stuff planned in the future:
- more tech tiers,
- naval units,
- overall usability improvements
and more.
On the negative side, I find the different units and buildings quite difficult to distinguish. While most of it is due to the fact, that its grounded in science fiction (its not like in Company of Heroes, where a thing that looks like an MG nest is indeed an MG nest and behaves as you think it would), its not clear what a building does just by looking at it. But as times goes by you get used to it.
Although you can queue up multiple buildings and units (even on repeatable queues), or order reinforcements directly from the selected army, the overall usability could still be improved. Its not obvious that building blueprints and waypoints can be moved for excample and the different levels of icons shown when zooming out could be better adjusted.
Its all rather nit picky though. I am sure that Stardock will keep improving the game!

Additionally at time I became very frustrated wondering why my ship was just sitting there spinning slowly around rather than attacking the ship that I had ordered it to fire at. These things gave the game a very "on rails" feeling to the game as there was near zero room to do anything other than basic stuff like "fire at that ship" or go towards that base. Be warned that the pace of play is VERY slow. While this is likely due to the fact that these are battles between slow moving heavily armored ships there was never really a sustained sense of urgency and I would be sitting around doing absolutely nothing waiting for a ship to be destroyed or disabled as my ship automatically fired at it for several minutes.  It almost feels like as if you are playng a RTS game but only controlling 3-4 ships AT MOST at a given time and very often many less than that. Perhaps I am jumping to conclusions and I cannot say that I finished the game but I really lost the interest in continuing to slave on in the hopes that it will get more interesting. maybe I am missing something that the ~85% of people who reccomended this game did to make this game fun but personally I don't get it. I was picturing visions of getting to pilot a capital ship and instead I got a basic button pressing RTS but with none of the tactical/strategic skill required from a RTS.
This game is 50% space sim and 50% strategy game but 0% exciting for me, which is sad because I enjoy both genres usually.

It's simple, yet elegantly crafted, with small details and nuances, it can make an old school gamer smile, that old.... warm smile, a bit of 'thats cool,' from the days when we used words like "rad;" for whatever reason this game nailed something nostalgic, and tapped that old school love, in these modern times.  There is a reason this game is considered one of the top 10 indie games... ever.  If there is a game worth your time, this is likely it.  Simply put, this game is 15 dollars of happiness. .   .    buy it.  I guarantee you will find yourself smiling, I'm just curious how long it will take you to realize it.

So I won't lie, I'm not a big Borderlands fan. It's a typical albeit unique FPS RPG with some of the most annoying drop mechanics in a game i've ever seen. Also DLC out the♥♥♥♥♥ That said, it has a pretty interesting world with decent characters which makes it more sad the Gearbox writers decided the best way to utilisize would be making the story age horribly by adding in every meme they could think of for no good reason.
With that in mind, while I enjoy the hell out of Telltale games I was a bit worried how this would turn out, especially with how The Walking Dead Season 2, while fantastic, lacked what made Season 1 so spectacular. After playing through episodes 1 -3 of Tales from the Borderlands I honestly think it's one of the best games Telltale has EVER released.
It doesn't play like a Borderlands game yet it still has the charm of the games. The Borderlands UI, returning characters and craziness of Pandora makes it feel like home. So what is it about?
You play Rhys, a Hyperion lackey who looked up to Handsome Jack and wishes to be as powerful and influential as him only to be let down time and time again by the company, and Fiona, a con-woman with her sister always hoping to get that big score and no longer on the run. After a big deal over a lurcious vault key goes wrong they find that there is something bigger they both must work towards, despite their distrust and dislike of each other. The story is told sometime in the future with a mysterious stranger who has unknown motives and asks both Rhys and Fiona of their sides of the story which of course, are bias in their own way and leads to pretty funny jokes and scenes. The pacing is just fantastic, voice acting is superb (seriously, the cast they got for this game is crazy; Nolan North, Troy Baker, Laura Bailey, freakin' Patrick Warburton?! As well as the original game voice actors!) and holy ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥the Intros are just amazing. Seriously, the first and second intros are hilarious and the music is incredibly fitting, better than any current Borderlands intro I've seen.
My only complaint honestly is the gameplay is lacking, it is a Telltale game after all and QTE's do get repetitive and boring but dialogue choices are pretty solid. I just wish there was a bit more freedom in certain scenes, like in the original Walking Dead where you could talk to people and find out how they feel about a situation or whatever (which to be fair, they did a good job with in Episode 3). Regardless, it's a incredible and funny as hell experience and I'm really looking forward to seeing how the rest of the game pans out. If you're a Borderlands fan, why the ♥♥♥♥ don't you have this already? If you're not as big as a fan of Borderlands then it's still awesome and is definitely worth your time.

This game is everything I wanted and more. I'd played other TTG games before, so I'm familiar with their style of choice-based story telling, and I've logged more hours in BL2 than I care to think about, so I'm similarly familar with the world of Pandora. I was expecting a lot of this game, since I had such a good time with The Wolf Among Us and BL 1&2, and I was aboslutely not disappointed.
Like the other Borderlands games before it, this game continues to strike a flawless balance between atmosphere, characters, setting, and worldbuilding. The new characters are immediately vibrant and endearing, the old characters drop in just often enough to let us see the world we'd left behind without overtaking the spotlight, and the plot aboslutely drives you forward through twists, turns, bandits, rakk hives, chase scenes, pop culture references,♥♥♥♥♥♥jokes, and surprising moments of genuine, tangible emotion. One of my favorite things about the Borderlands series has always been the balance between over-the-top, ridiculous, Mad Max-style dieselpunk flamboyance and deeper narratives centered around the characters and the world they inhabit, and Tales from the Borderlands not only continues that trend, but, in my opinion, perfects it.
Possible cons!:
No shooting :(
Short gameplay (~10 hours total, compared to BL2's 40+)
Low-to-mid replayability unless you're super into the characters.
Episodic release format is frustrating if you're hooked on the plot (which I am) and just couldn't hold off on buying the game even though it's only 3 episodes in (which I did).
Overall, this is one of the best games I've played in a long time, and is worth every single (full-price) penny I spent. Do yourself a favor and get it.

I've put in at least 11 hours with this game, so I'm still pretty new and that should say a lot to those looking to buy it.
For starters, Squad is extremely immersive and you should be prepared...no...you should definitely take your time fiddling with your bindings for intense gunfights and spend a good amount of time getting a feel for each weapon at the training map.
Next, be prepared to learn if you jump in actual game; the squad-leaders that you have (if they're good) typically do not have time to explain every facet of the game to you, so take the time to check out the youtube videos posted for a simulated boot-camp experience (hopefully they add an actual in-game bootcamp to get everyone up to speed).
Finally, keep your head on a swivel. Communicate. And be prepared to get lit up - verbally and in-game ammo-ily(sp?). It's a hard game.
For the most part, I'd give the game - at it's current stage - a 7/10.
Pros:
-Realistic and immersive.
-Great graphics, gun play, and sounds
-Addicting and relentless for hardcore game lovers
-Load of fun if you can actually find a server with enough people to make it competitive and satisfying when you finally take out an BTR/Sniper/Squad.
Cons:
-On the fly learning, no formal teaching or tutorial of the game within the game (aside from signs posted in the training map)
-No option to kick squad leaders who just don't live up to the role.
-Toxicity is pretty common if you end up skipping tutorials and your gameplay shows it
-Servers are far and few in-between. Every good server is full, every empty server stays empty, and hardly any U.S. supported servers so you end up having to take a ping hit and end up getting wiped by a Russian or Korean.
Conclusion:
Buy this game if you enjoy hardcore realistic gameplay and can handle waiting in queues for a good server for at least 8 minutes. The wait is worth it if you have a great squad leader and squad, but it also gets frustrating not having server support for US players, no bootcamp to teach new players, and the lack of overall game knowledge present by devs - in game. Also, buy this if you're okay with all of that and the fact that it's still practically in beta.
Don't buy this game if you think that you won't have the time to put into learning the intricacies of gameplay, don't like spending money on an unfinished game, or do not like waiting for server spots to open up just to play.

Simple and effective! Game offers a nod to the Diablo and Diablo II line of games and is a fun 2D slash and hack game.
Con:
1) Buggy as of this review. Crashes can happen with particular levels/characters though they do get patched very quickly.
2) NOT a game for purists. Related to one. I have had a non-hardcore character file wiped out on me. Only happened once but it was annoying. There's a pseudo work around since you can easily edit the SP files. I just leveled a new character back to my old character's level in 2 minute and gave him my old charm.
3) 2D and VERY simplistic. This may be an issue if you're looking for a bit more. Yes, there are 150+ levels and 4 difficulties, but they can get retetitive.
4) Lack of character customization/skill diversity. You have maybe 1-3 skills you'll use for each character and everyone plays the same way in the end game (when you have lots of relics/items). Namely you sit in one spot and spam normal attacks.
5) Balancing is an issue. Neither characters nor levels are balanced though the developers are constantly working on it. Based on luck, starting levels can be insanely hard while end acts can be ridiculously easy. Unexpected OHKO can happen. Your milage can vary.
6) Nothing original or innovative in this game. If you're looking for a certain WOW factor in your games, Hero Siege won't do it for you.
Pro:
1) It's Diablo-lite and 2D! Has a sort of active RPG feel. No limit on stats though character skills (called talents) are soft capped to 30 just like in Diablo II. You can boost them with a charm though. Your character will effectively be capped at level 80-100 because the exp gain is so slow at that point.
2) Actively being updated/improved as of this review. Developers do listen to input.
3) Super cheap IF you get it on sale. I picked it up for $2 including DLC.
4) Perfect for alt-tab/window screen gaming. Fun breaktime game in-between stressful studying.
5) Lots of variety in the in-game items called relics. More being added soon. They can range from hilarious/useless to game-breaking.
6) Nice mix of classes. Redneck is hilarious while marksman/pyro may be the easiest to play because of their range and them having pet/static defenses.
7) **Multiplayer** in the future. MP is in alpha currently and very, very buggy, but this mode has been promised to all holders of the base game. Maybe something to look for.
8) Achievement Hunting. Most of the 100+ achievements were removed recently, but developers said better new ones may be added in the future.

In essence The Silent Age may appear to be just another very basic 'casual' puzzler for mobile, but despite its simplicity in controls it's still well worth your time if you're into adventure games. The graphics are streamlined but atmospheric, the story engaging, and Joe the Janitor makes for a solid protagonist as he's thrown into the way of events well above his paygrade.
Most of the puzzles are simple 'collect-and-use' inventory puzzles familiar to all puzzle adventure gamers. What gives The Silent Age its own little spin is the shifting back and forth in time you have to do to navigate areas and find those items necessary to progress. Clicking on your Time Machine will hop you between the present (1972) and a point somewhere in the future - your actions in the present of course being able to affect how the world appears in the future. The game's not long, but with its intriguing storyline you'll find it a diverting way to spend an afternoon.

The natural evolution of Asteroid, and so, so much more!
Pros:
_Looks amazing: The game's asthetics is just hmmm, just excellent in everyway. They aimed for a 70s-80s look and hit it dead on. Great style, great animation, attention to details oozing out of its pores.
_Sounds good: Voice acting is pretty alright, with a nice, clever-at-times-cheesy-otherwise script that is endearing. Sound effect and music are great all around though.
_Great Gameplay: It's an update to the good ol' Asteroid formula, instead of using the the left and right button to turn, you can just use the whole analog stick to aim at the direction you want to face. The results is a game that controls great but retains the sense of weight in a weightless space. The ship is fast and maneuverable, the lasers are accurate and punchy, locking on and releasing a swarm of several missiles onto multiple enemies feels sublime. Great. Tenanaten. Awesome.
_Survival/Rogue-lite Design: The game follows a Rouge-lite design, with procedural generation of level and a tough difficulty. It feels like a survival game at times, since your health doesn't recover between missions, so you have to scrap together enough resources to repair and rearm your ship while being able to affort upgrades as well.
Cons:
_Texture looks murky upclose, but this is fine, since you won't be up close that often.
_Can be a bit talkative: It doesn't interupt gameplay at all actually. But the characters are in an almost constant conversation with one another. Again, it doesn't interupt gameplay, but does make doing commentary on it rather difficult at times.
Overall, is it worth the $20? Yes! They could've sold this at 30 bucks and I'd still buy it. It's an amazing game all around. Worth a buy in every respect.

-Pleasant voice-overs of the plot, as the transitions from act to act is voiced by an extremely pleasant voice.
-The game runs unbelievably smoothly.
-Enormous levels to partake in, although it is 99% empty space.
-The game is extremely good at giving you terrible situations but giving you just enough weaponry to steal the day, making it a game that will give you plenty of satisfaction.
Cons:
-The camera is rather clunky, as it will lock to a certain axis and not move unless you make very specific camera movements.
-Some levels are unfair without lots of trial and error, meaning certain levels can be utterly repetitive.
-The game never directly tells you about the ship customization option, and some missions can be nigh impossible without a proper loadout.
-You do not choose which ships to go into battle with. The only ship you are certain to go with is A) for the early bit, the Stiletto, or B) The Angelwing. All others are strictly variables, which can make the experience a bit depressing when you kit a certain destroyer out only to have it removed for two missions in a row.
-Some voices are pretty bad, but others are acceptable, while Marcus himself has a Morgan Freeman tier voice during transitions.
Neutral:
-Missions can take a very long time depending on your play style, so people with strict scheduals might be daunted.
-The soundtrack isn't bad, but isn't good either, as it can feel a bit repetitive when it repeats multiple times, but certain tracks are epic and enjoyable.
Story:
Set in the near distant future, Nexus - The Jupiter Incident places you into the role of Captain Marcus Cromwell, the son of one of the most influential men of the era, as you work your way through the ranks. You take up when Marcus arrives on an outer moon of Jupiter, and slowly begin to unravel a plot of epic proportion.
Plot: (SPOILERS)
After the discovery of the Angelwing - an advanced alien spacecraft - and an Artificial Intelligence known as Angel, Marcus and the crew flee through a wormhole away from a mechanoid - an extremely powerful device that is invulnerable to traditional weaponry. The plot expands outward to galactic empires warring against each other and the systematic capturing of earth by these mechanoids. It is down to Marcus and the crew of the Angelwing to rescue earth and defeat the mechanoids, and perhaps save a few space empires in the process.
(SPOILERS END HERE)
All in all, I give the game a solid 8/10, an extremely impressive game for something that has come out so long ago. My recommendation for a game similar to this is Homeworld Remastered Edition.
