Warning, this review is based on my several years old experience, haven't played that since, only for a few minutes. YOu can skip to bottom for TL;DR part.
Brilliant! I've spent approx 100 with this game (only in campaign!) and it is incredibly tactical. Maybe Homeworld seems to you too much arcadish? Well, this one is more like hardcore tactical RTS :) You can assign orders even to last single battery on your corvette, but don't forget yourself! Too much micromanagement can kill you very quickly. Solution can be a lot of pausing, or simply giving orders in such manner, your ships will perform well even without your intervention, so you can take care of top priorities. Protect your ships, bring them from mission to mission throughout whole campaign and be sure your crew gathers experience, because experience can be more valuable than guns and armor itself.
And atmosphere is still "realistic". As realistic as it can be in space opera RTS :)) Thanks to music, graphics (right now I mean long trails behind ships, design of Earth ships and other details, not beauty of textures, lights or shadows, more on that in next paragraph...) storrytelling and proportional grow of your forces you get first grade experience. First you start with a single ship that travel from Earth to Jupiter for eight months. That seems to be kinda fast for today's technology, isn't it? Well, wait for your first alien ship that carries you from system to system in no time, compared to Stilleto (your first ship). It takes like ages of ingame time, to get Angelo (if I remember the name correctly), but that makes it even more rewarding. Later you will get another ship to your current one, so you will be able to use two of them. When your fleet grows to number of like 5 ships, you will feel invincible.
Today they released patch (first one after years of inactivity) that brings the game to full HD. I realized how much time passed since I started Nexus for last time. Graphics looks really old, but playability seems to be still very high.
I really hope in more updates, possibly in remastered edition or even brand new game? (ehm, inspirated by not named studio, right?)
TL;DR
If you are fan of space opera where you take care of your ships and where you can really enjoy tactical decisions and story, definitely buy this game while in discount like today's one. For current price 2,49 Euro, it's a must. Even when it's priced on it's full 10 euro, it can be a good buy.

This game might look like it's inspired by "Flashback" or "Another World" but that's not the case. It's an inventory-based point & click adventure and a great one at that!
The story is really captivating – up to the point where it's actually really hard *not* to finish the game in one sitting. It has 10 short chapters which are all exciting and convey a great mood. I've completed the whole thing in about 4 hours, with 6 achievements still missing. The visual style reminiscent of web-based Flash games might look bad at first glance – however it's not detrimental to the atmosphere at all! On the contrary: it feels like some sort of 70's art style which fits perfectly to our protagonist.
What's especially brilliant is the time travelling. Changing between two time periods, the game creates some exciting puzzles and solutions to them. Another thing that's a *HUGE* plus is the ingenious soundtrack, which sometimes reminded me of Vangelis' soundtrack for "Blade Runner".
I bought this game while it was on sale, but I'd even recommend it at full price.
Go for it, adventure fans! It's worth every penny.

A tactics RPG with persistent fleet and detailed micromanagement? In theory, I should love the hell out of this game. But I don't.
Pros:
- RPG aspects, level of ship customization - your captains are persistent, and so are your ships. You upgrade both of these, which is costly, and customize them for various roles and against various enemies. You lose a ship, you lose everything you put into them - which is costly. Customization includes a multitude of weapon types (for different roles), different strike craft and various, various equipment.
- level of control over ships - you can control the ships down to singlar guns targetting different targets, engine throttle, subsystem management, repairs, etc etc etc.... best set of options I've ever seen. If you could only control individual shield quadrants, this game would take unit control to a whole another level never seen in any game. You can blow crap up, you can just disable, or you can board. It's up to you.
- scale - the battles and scenarios are just the right scale, and just the right escalation.
- ship design and details - all the different engines (including some on the front), moving parts, turrets... also very utilitarian ship design. I like it.
Unfortunetly, that's it for pros.
Cons:
- relatively boring cliche storyline - good twist around 1/4th in, but that'd be all
- clunky camera - think Homeworld 1. Unacceptable
- you can't issue move orders on empty space - yes, that's right. You can only head towards/away from a specified target. As a result, your battle plans are very limited, flanking is difficult, and on more than one occasion I got stuck and had to restart a mission because I didn't have any targets in sight
- unreliable controls - that's right. The level of control is incredible, but very often ships don't do what you tell them to. They stumble, they pick the wrong direction, randomly stop firing, or decide they won't target X. "Derpy" is a diplomatic way to say it. It happens all the goddamn time, especially if you have more and bigger ships. Very often you're stuck manually reloading ships' weapons because they stop firing for no reason.
- random outcomes - very often if you do a mission and do the same thing let's say three times, you'll get 3 different outcomes. Good on paper, not so much in a tactics game.
- difficulty - the unfair, random kind. Sometimes you just have everything stacked against you. Enemies roll good dice, your units decide to disobey orders, which happens infuriatingly often, and you just are left screaming at the screen "why didn't you follow my orders". It doesn't help that missions on their own are pretty difficult,
While the cons aren't very numerous, the camera, move orders and unreliable behavior of your ships make the game incredibly frustrating at times.

The Silent Age is fun. It's a side-scrolling point-and-click style adventure that tells a grim story about time traveling to save humanity from being wiped about by a virus. It reminds me of the recent game The Fall in the side-scrolling p&c format and presentation of grim science fiction. There are many locations and the art style makes even mundane ones look vibrant. The Silent Age is a sharp looking game. The main central mechanic of the game is jumping between the past and future to solve puzzles. This mechanic is introduced in a really effective, interesting way. The first time travelling to the future really gets the story into high gear. For the most part there's only two different times you can jump between. So, the initial thrill of time jumping gives way to the mindless familiarity of using it to solve every puzzle. Sometimes I'd forget which place I was in was the 'past' or the 'future' because it really didn't much matter which was which. If the solution can't be found, switch to the other time and find a new item to bring back to the other time. The Silent Age still told a good story and solving the puzzles was fun, and most were reasonably easy with a few tough ones thrown into the mix. This game takes about 4 hours to finish. I do recommend The Silent Age. This is good science fiction to go with fun game play.

I bought this just to write a review, but that isnt a bad thing. I played the original on android and eagerly awaited the second part. When it came out i was more than pleased. They then announced it was coming out on steam. Time for another play through i thought. I also wanted to support the company as (spoiler) this is an incredible game.
I find it a bit odd for the characters to have voices, as i had given them voices in my head, but i understand it and think they have done a very good job. I have tried point and click games before and this is the only one that has really grabbed me. I cant really say how good it is as a point and click game though, the puzzles arent particualy hard but still provide a challenge. They all make sense but arent always obvious, which seems to be a good mix. This is aided by being able to switch between 1972 and 2012 (it makes sense in the story) which adds a second layer to just hunting for hidden objects.
The story is just so clever and you really connect with Joe (the main character) as you only ever really know as much as he does. The writing is really good, with Joe giving funny little quips when you try to do something that isnt possible or even just when he is reacting to whats happening. The atmosphere the game creates is really cool as it provides it with small glimpses of whatever is off in the horizon and sound effects that gives off a really haunting feeling.
This brings me on to the music. Ahh. The music. It all fits so well with the game and only adds to the atmosphere. Why they havnt released an official OST I dont know. As i have mentioned already, the sound design and OST add a really haunting feeling, which fits with the whole game so well.
My one main problem with the game is the length. I have two hours game time on steam and I have played the whole game through and gone back and got all the achievements that i missed. Although I suspect house on fire's answer would be 'what would you expect for £6'.
I'm not very good at writing reviews (which should be quite obvious) but what im trying to say is that its a very good game and for only £6.99 (or your regional equivelent) you should definitely get it, if that doesn't sell it then consider that ive played it through at least 5 times on android and intend to play it many more times on steam.

Don't get me wrong this is an excellent step in the right direction for something other than Madden regardless of platform but I just can't get passed zone not working and forced to only run man during the game to even have a chance of having someone down field. I really want to give this game a thumbs up because I want to have something other than the console crap which is so ridden with bugs it detracts from the experiance but this game has a ways to go before I personally can enjoy it.
Pros
-Not Madden
I list this as a pro because I know me and the rest of the sim community are at a point where Madden just isn't the answer and hasn't been for a long long time. Danny i'll give it to you that this game has the right direction but there are just little things that just ruin the whole experiance. I am excited for 2018 for the sim franchise mode and will def pick it up and test that.
-Pass and Run blocking
One of the biggest qualms I have with Madden and Ncaa 14 would have to be the pass blocking and run blocking AI especially when trying to make it where the AI can actually beat you. Axis has it right with the AI actually making blocks and seeking people out to block. This system reminds me of NCAA 11 where presnap your linemen chose who to block and you had a good time in the run game.
-Run Game
The run game is pretty good, personally the best part about this game seeing as I really detest the passing mechanics in this game either the spot passing or the controller with button passing. It just needs to get more fluid with how the mechanics are and im hoping by 18 that will be figured out. This is something that needs to be worked on some more and it will be perfect, maybe look at the ncaa 11 feature and implement it in game so we know who is getting blocked to make a decision on edge pressure and things.
-Franchise Mode
You guys have the right path for franchise mode and I feel thats the direction you need to take to get an up on madden, mostly because madden has literally 0 interest in the CFM and SIM community. If Axis were to get a more CFM/SIM vibe many more would jump ship over and start playing axis.
Cons
-Not Madden
The reason I am listing this twice is because this is a double edged sword. One of the pluses of Madden would be their budget and time that they have to make the game. Plus with all their time Madden is a pretty fluid game, you can make reads in Madden in this game you kinda just throw it up and hope someone catches the ball which to me isnt a good experiance.
-Passing Mechanics
To me it feels like you are just picking routes and throwing up the ball and hoping your receiver catches the ball, one of my main issues would have to be the deep ball coverage which is just lacking. 80 yard bombs left and right.
-Playbooks
This isnt really much a con seeing as I know you have a lack of time to develop such a big game like NCAA 14 and Madden 17 but a good feature at least for me would be tons of plays and the ability to make your own playbook.
-Little things
Once again I am only listing this as a general con not so much a game breaking purchase deciding thing. Just really the little things bother me, Which would be just animations and the arms DBs have when breaking up passes which is just whack imo.
-Zones and defense in general
The fact of the matter is Zones do not work, at least the didnt for me. Running zone on 3rd and 21 with a 3-4-4 look usually ends with a wide open dude where a purple zone is which makes no sense to me. That aspect is one of the reasons I just gave up and in the end am writing this review with only 1.4 hrs into the game. Also like I said with the passing mechanics even with a perfect defense one can still easily be beaten deep even in like quad coverage. I do not know a good fix for this probably something to do with game speed and making it feel like a real game.
Score - 6.3/10
Overall if you are wanting an experiance now this is a good buy for PC enthusiasts not looking to get a console. But for me I am just going to load up NCAA 06 on emulator and wait for Axis 2018 and see what improvments have been made. Its not a bad game but for someone who takes sim and realism over gameplay I can see the route you are taking but will hold off on buying.
Ill be back testing here and there I hope something from this will be taken and worked on. Overall I love where its headed and hope it continues. Good luck with development.

SOME GENERAL SPOILERS:
Purchased and re-playing this on PC after originally owning it for PC.
As somebody that played the original Wolfenstein as a kid in the 90s, I originally recoiled at this re-imagining of the series considering it's past disappointments. The 2009 game had some great ideas but it was overall bland and couldn't set itself apart from every other shooter that came out that year. A half baked game is what I come to expect from Wolfenstein by the time The New Order arrived. I expected another bland FPS with some mystical occult elements that essentially clashed with your initial gameplay.
I'm so glad I was proven wrong.
Pros
- Fully realized world building.
- Fleshed out characters. BJ isn't just some square jawed Nazi killer. He has his own motivations beyond stabbing Jerrys in the throat.
- Sophisticated storytelling. It didn't try to be sophomoric or self-referential. It didn't insult the players intelligence.
- Wonderful level and character design.
- Fun action balanced out by some great stealth elements that don't get too old.
- NAZI PRISON ESCAPE. SPACE NAZI BASE. ROBOT DOGS
Cons
- The controls feel loose in some ways. It takes a bit to get used to.
- The cover system [is it a cover system?] doesn't really work that well.
- With how gorgeous the game looks, I couldn't help but notice that there could have been some improvement on the graphical options front.

A fun detective game, you might think? Well, definitions of 'fun' might vary, but this certainly isn't 'fun'.
I first saw this game the day it was released on steam, and bought it, hoping I could play it and post a review before others could. I tried to like it. I really did. But I just couldn't. Half an hour of frustration led up to the moment where I just shut down the game and left it to rot in my library. The following review is based upon these 30 minutes, and believe me, I couldn't find more problems with this game in this amount of time.
The game is a port of the 1985 original. (I thought) I knew what I was expecting; pixelated graphics and cheesy sound effects. I was right on the first part. The same goes for the second part, though I was only able to find one sound effect; you punching items and people (and yourself).
The inventory system the game has is very frustrating. You have to drag items you find to a little window which is labeled "inventory". You've got your inventory. You can move a jacket into your inventory. In your jacket is a wallet. In your wallet is your money and other junk. In order to get to your money, you have to open every inventory window separately. If you want all your items in your "first" inventory, you'll have to spend a lot of time just moving all your items, and when you're finally done doing that, your inventory will be a mess. Some items look alike, which makes it even harder to figure out what's what.
There are eight operations you can perform on items during the entire game, some of which just imply each other (operate->open/close/consume). The game is horribly unforgiving. There are multiple events, even at the beginning of the game, in which you have no idea what's happening and end up getting shot. You've got little to no time to open your inventory, open an inventory in the inventory, take out your gun and shoot. When you're dead, you wished that you saved at some point in the game. This game has no autosave whatsoever (well, it's 1985. What did you expect?).
I see no reason why I should continue playing this game. There are no achievements. The story can be found in many other games/movies/comics. Not even the fact that it features trading cards would make me play it again. Avoid this game at all costs; even when it's on sale, it's not worth it. Even if you invent a time machine and go back to 1985, don't get this game.

I absolutely love this game. I've played both the original, and this game, and will try to break it down a into sections.
I will be assuming you've played multiple RTS games before, and have read my original review about Ashes of the Singularity (Vanilla), so I'll jump right in.
Campaign
Fun, challenging, and definitely has some unique scenarios. Some can be frustrating at times, but overall I enjoyed the storyline despite it being a bit tropey at times, but I don't mind that stuff. Overall campaign length for me was around 8-12 hours, but that's because I tend to turtle. Playing aggressively will probably shorten this.
Multiplayer
Really fun, but expect to have your butt handed to you your first few matches if you've only fought the AI thus far. The AI is challenging to newer players, but once you can take on the Challenging AI, you can probably graduate to a human player. Even better, is if you can take on the 2nd most difficult AI (or 2 of them!) by performing a successful turtle strategy. That said, once you can do these things, you can graduate to multiplayer. People will use much different (and more deadly) strategies than the AI that puts their difficulty just below the Painful AI setting, which is an overkill cheating AI. In this, you'll need to learn to expand fast while playing defense. Unlike playing against the AI, a human can become demoralized, but so can you. Play aggressively, try out strategies, but also ask the community for help in getting better.
- Community is very friendly
- Community is small, but growing. There is a discord channel as well, so get in on that!
-Multiplayer is much more difficult than the AI, so don't get demoralized after just a few games.
- 1v1 Games tend to last around 20-35 minutes
-2v2 games tend to last closer to 45 minutes
- Support for up to 14 player games, up from 6 players in the original Ashes of the Singularity
- Does not currently take long to get into a 1v1 ranked game...about 3 minutes on average for me.
- Custom/skirmish games take much longer right now, but the games do happen, and when they do, it's a blast. We just need more people to host games and join them than is happening at the moment
- Stardock has announced plans to help bolster the multiplayer community, such as the possibilty of giving all AotS a few multiplayer only keys to give out to friends...so basically they can only play multiplayer games, but could not play single player skirmish or the campaign, but certainly helps everyone.
- lag is minimal, I cannot recall experiencing much at all.
- Crashes...it does happen on occasion, but for me, it doesn't happen often at all. I think I've only had maybe 1 or 2 crashes from a multiplayer game of AotS: Escalation. That said, I was having router problems around that time which are now fixed, so I cannot rule out it was possibly that.
- Fridays! The game devs host multiplayer games on Friday's, I want to say at around 6 PM EST.
Single Player Skirmish
Where do I begin? You can play against up to 13 other players (14 player game support!). I love the chaos, but need to upgrade my computer from my lowly 7 year old Phenom II 955 processor to something more modern, but that's my fault, not the game's. The game definitely slows down on my CPU, though frankly, my cpu just isn't cut out for most games from the past 2 years XD.
- Supports enormous army sizes of thousands of units
New units
-The new units are definitely fun for both sides. Tier 2 air units were added as well, allowing you to puncture enemy defenses more easiliy, clean up groups of enemies, and help end the game if both sides are turtling with strategic bombers.  While there's still some balance issues, they're working on getting it right. They just released an opt-in update for those that want to try out the new balance (1/13/2017).
- Economy: The substrate economy is completely unhinged, so they don't need to worry about storage. That said, their units are weaker and more mobile, rely on shields instead of hp/armor regeneration, and on drones more than stuff like long range artillery. The Substrate economy has a unit called the harvester, which has low health, but you can build as many as you want and have them all stack the same region to boost a certain resource type, then if you run low, you can move all of them to a different region (or split them up however you want) to boost resources in different regions. They're very vulnerable though, so if an enemy air unit gets to them, they're all dead...fast. But they're mobile, so just like their units being more mobile than the PHC, their resource structure is more mobile as well.
-The biggest thing for me are the new defensive structures and the upgrade paths for them. Long story short, turtling is now feasible as a strategy to an extent, unlike vanilla AotS, which requires you to maintain a standing defensive army.
- Substrate defenses are a bit shorter range, but much more deadly than PHC's defenses
- PHC defenses includes a heavy artillary cannon that is very long range...so take these out fast, or your Substrate defensive line that can seemingly crush everything else will become rubble.
- Orbital nullification units now help move your army along instead of losing much of your army from an orbital bombardment ability.
Ongoing Development & Support
-Stardock has continued to meet their publically stated goals, or when there are things stalling them (such as when the lead developer got sick for a couple weeks), they disclose the issues and keep to their commitments.
-They are currently working on adding new units, to include about 3 new dreadnaughts for each faction, 3 new Juggernaughts (a T4 unit, so basically an end game unit, or a super experimental like from Supreme Commander), new orbitals, and new maps.
-Modding support: They're working on it right now, as stated on the roadmap. Delay caused by lead dev getting sick.
-Vulcan support: Working on it, as stated on the roadmap. Linux support should follow sometime after that, but is contingent on Vulcan being finished of course.
- 2 additional factions mentioned to be added in later expansions
- water units/maps planned for the future in roadmap
- Tier 4 units (Juggernaughts) are on their way. Please reference roadmap.
- I believe I heard viewing replays will be added at some point, which will be great for learning new strategies (or learning from your mistakes).
Overall impressions of current state of game
- Game is very polished
- Game is fun. Lots of explosions, colors, upgradable defenses, orbital abilities, streaming economy, thousands of units, 14 player games, decent AI, decent and still enlarging unit variety (See Ongoing Development & Support Section) army systems, strategic zoom, and multiple strategies available.
- Graphics look quite nice
- Full multi-core support for more than 4 cores (and for using more than 1 core, for that matter)
- Developers communicate openly with the community in both the Steam and Stardock forums
- Developers have met many stated goals to date from their roadmap, so I have strong belief in their ability to provide continued support.
- Community is very helpful and friendly, and Ticktoc is something of a forum anomaly (very helpful player, and always answering questions), so if the devs don't answer your questions right away, he probably will jump in.
- Music is just as great as the previous game (it's mostly the same, but has I think 4 new tracks, which I really enjoy)
- Units could be more distinctive from one to the next, but it's better than the original, and am sure it will improve
- Is the game worth full price? I believe so.
Should you get it on sale? Absolutely!
Should you get this over AotS: Vanilla? YES!

Okay, so here it goes... While my review here will sound like a lot of whining and complaining I can assure you that I am happy to have been able to get in on the ground level here with the "early release" of EmergeNYC. I'm glad there are people out there that are taking the time to make this game correctly rather than the German sim engines out there that often are infected with bugs. As a career firefighter myself I see this not only being a fun time waster but an excellent training tool to teach younger members in the fire service who do not have much, if any, experience. We are always looking for new, realistic ways to train that will also reduce the risk of injury and this may just be the way that is done, so props to the dev team are in order. I've seen this game come from grey buildings abound to a map that shows great potential with the features we have all been promised SLOWLY coming to life. Please devs, note slowly is in caps.
My biggest problem after roughly 30 hours of game play and a few months of updates is the seemingly empty promises. We seem to hear once a week of a new update, new patch, new fire academy release date, or the idea that makes pants a bit tighter… Multiplayer. I get the idea, I really do, but in the other pre-release games I have dabbled in the production is much, and I mean MUCH, farther along. Now I’m not saying that the rumored Patch 3.0 won’t resolve much of what we are having our monthlies over but I do think it will be a start. I do still doubt that we should be putting our time and energy in to an advanced multiplayer setting when the foundation still is not fully or even partially operational. The issues that HAVE to be addressed are as follows; decreased FPS, lag, Houdini police and EMS vehicles, lag, lag, traffic that seems to have no rhyme or reason, and the lighting issues that seem to blind you while driving in the first person. Not all were present prior to the most recent patch updates but it isn’t totally uncommon for a game to take two steps back before a bigger release. Let’s all hope for the best and trust the new, well new additions, to the dev team and trust they do have a plan.
Alright, now I’m going to sound grumpy. I swear I’m not, promise. So with anything in life its best to not make blind promises. I personally feel like the work on multiplayer and fire academy could have been way better spent making a worthwhile map and a function city with a decent traffic engine/ AI. Hell I’d even take a first person view over the, my opinion, preemptive release of multiplayer. Even if the route that we are going is to release multiplayer, don’t tell me March and on April 4th have nothing for me. The same is true with fire academy. A once very vocal and receptive team now seems to not have much to say other that the typical weekly patch update. One can only hope that they are hard at work and don’t have time for our simpleton complaints. Cannot argue there, in fact if that’s what you’re up to I’ll even buy you a beer. I guess my point is why are we worrying about multiplayer when I can’t even take a tool off the truck or advance a hose line?
This game as all the potential in the world, and that’s the problem. So much to do in so little time. A true fire/ EMS and police simulation. Right now I’d advise anyone who is looking for a battle ready game to keep on looking. This just isn’t going to get you going. I think an investment in EmergeNYC is money well spent and a gift that will keep on giving. While its not much to look at now it is certainly the diamond in the rough. As a personal note to the dev team, please just keep us in the loop. Maybe even a quick update on youtube? Either way, two thumbs up and I will be patiently (ish) waiting for the next update of this next big thing!

The "buy this game if/ don't buy this game if" thing is at the end of the review, if you want the TLDR.
First of all, what is AoE II? It is a real time strategy game (like Warcraft, StarCraft and Command and Conquer, for example) set in medieval times that features a very big selection of civilizations each sharing pretty much the same basic structures and units, but with different perks and unique units that differentiate one from another. If you ever played StarCraft or Warcraft, you'll notice that AoE II is definitely not as fast paced as those games, but it has a much more complex economy, and the very interesting element of randomly generated maps. Unlike Warcraft where you know exactly what the map layout will be, where your expansions are, and so on, in AoE II you can choose a certain type of map, but the exact location of your spawn, your enemies, and the resources, is initially unknown to you. You must scout to find resources, learn your terrain so you can wall yourself efficiently, and decide what kind of troops you are going to make and based on that, what resources will your focus your economy in.
What is Age of Empires II HD? If you buy it without any DLC, it is exactly the same game we all have been playing since the early 2000's with the AoC expansion, proper widescreen support, mods downloadable from the Workshop, and integrated steam multiplayer. With DLCs however, you obtain 3 pretty cool expansions that add not only a lot of new well crafted campaigns but also some pretty interesting civs with new mechanics.
I don't quite play this version as much as I play the original version using Voobly to manage my mods and for multiplayer, because Voobly still has a better environment for a more competitive play, as well as better features when it comes to spectating matches. However, AoE II HD does have an active community and it is getting better everyday. Lately I have been playing it way more specially after the African Kingdoms and Rise of the Rajas DLCs came along.
Buy this game if:
- You are a fan of RTS games, never played AoE II and want to experience this well-known classic
- You are interesting in a well-aged RTS with solid mechanics for an enjoyable single-player campaign
- You like castles, knights, catapults, trebruchets and want to enjoy a game about epic battles in medieval times
- You are an AoE II veteran and want to try out the new DLCs or play online on Steam, or you do not own a retail copy of the oldschool AoE II.
Don't buy this game if:
- You absolutely hate real time strategy games
- You love Starcraft because of how fast paced it is and how insane APM you need to have to play that game: AoE II is not even comparable in that regard.
- You love Warcraft 3 because of the hero mechanics that allowed for custom maps like Dota to appear: AoE II does have great custom maps, but it does not feature the RPG elements War 3 had
- You don't like Age of Empires. Duh
- You don't like games set in medieval ages
- You want to play a game like Civ, for example. This isn't quite that.
- You already own the old retail version of AoE II, play online actively on Voobly, and have no interest on trying the new DLCs

This game is quite simply... awesome.  It's unlike any other space rts ive ever played. It's graphics are almost cinematic and like watching a movie, it's level of control is something rarely seen in games now a days. I was particularly amazed with how even my crappy windows xp laptop (as opposed to my more modern desktop) could run the game at full graphics and still play  very smoothly.
There were 2 negatives to this game that you only really notice later on.
The first is the "independentness" of your space ships. i actually believe that the manual explained this was on purpose, and if done correctly, this function could make the game tons more fun and one of a kind. But they kind of failed. The idea is that your ships aren't under your command as much as following your orders and figuring out things for their own. This could have been a highly unique and interesting feature if they had taken it a bit further (for example, having different personalities of captains on your ships. so one could charge right in guns blazing when when u say attack while the other would naturally  bombard the target from a distance and disable its key systems before going in for the kill). they also could have just not implemented this idea and had the ships follow your orders exactly (like manual almost but as an ai) instead the game has an awkward middle ground that is sometimes extremely annoying. I often go manual on my ships and still have problems. I will send my flagship away from, say, the battle base titan or something similar and send it towards an enemy cruiser to keep it safer. then i will come back to find that my flagship has turned arond and is charging straight into the battle bases guns..... and only a single laser beam is firing from my ship as it charges  . This obviouslycan be frustrating. (sorry didnt mean to rant but in the late game where everything relies on timing, this can be annoying and almost game wrecking if you try to micromanage)

I recieved this game as a gift from a friend. It doesn't affect my opinion in any way, I just thought I'd mention it.
is a rouge-lite action game with a procedurally generated dungeon. It follows the tradition of games such as
and most prominantly
by allowing the player to collect and purchase upgrades throughout the adventure in order to make their character stronger.
To the game's credit, the controls are tight and responsive, and the characters move with a satisfying sense of speed and agility. It is also very well optimised and could easily run on a microwave. Unfortunately, that is where the good points end.
This game suffers from a desperate lack of balance. On some runs I got all the upgrades (figuratively), and on others I got nothing (almost literally). No matter how many defense upgrades I collected, enemies did the same amount of damage to me. Most baffling of all, there are several large rooms and sprawling corridors throughout the stages with nothing in them at all. No traps, no enemies, nothing. There is also no permanence to speak of, which makes attampted runs feel pointless in the end.
While a lot of rouge-lite games are deliberately vague with their item descriptions to encourage experimentaion and discovery,
has descriptions that make no sense and tell you nothing about what certain items or powers do. There is not even a glossary that explains the properties of these elements. As a result, I still don't know what the Paladin's special move does. Is it a shield? A retaliation attack? I couldn't tell you, because the game sure as hell doesn't.
Speaking of which,
has a selection of classes that runs the gamut of standard fantasy archetypes, with classics such as the warrior, the rogue and the wizard all accounted for. However, out of all the classes, only the archer is really worth playing, with the wizard coming a tentative second. This is because the reach on melee weapons in this game is so small that it is extremely difficult not to take damage, especially against bosses or enemies that have ranged attacks. The archer is overpowered in this case because he can shoot enemies on the other side of the screen, he has a stupidly high critical hit ratio and his poison arrow special does too much damage for a starting ability. The fact that many of the new abilities found throughout the game are weaker than his poison arrows smacks of the lack of balance mentioned earlier.
On that note, the second boss in this game is totally unfair. The way in which it attacks means that it is extremely difficult to not take damage, at least as far as I could tell. You might say "but it's a rouge-lite, it's supposed to be hard", but just remember;
had a sense of balance with its boss encounters.
has a very bland and utilitarian pixel art style that is devoid of life and vibrancy. I can respect creators wanting to pay homage to the 8-bit and 16-bit eras of gaming but, to paraphrase the lovely Totalbiscuit, developers of that era were dealing with a lack of technology, not a lack of talent, when it came to videogame graphics. There are some nice lighting and mist effects present in this game, however; I can appreciate that.
The soundtrack of this game ranges from listenable to downright obnoxious. I enjoyed a couple of the tracks on offer, but others (one of which appears to be ripped off from
) were like having hot screwdrivers driven into my ears, even with the volume turned down.
On another note, dubstep in a fantasy game?
Really?
Sorry, but
is not very good, which is a shame. A lot of love and effort has clearly gone into making this game, but in a world where genre-defining experiences like
,
and
exist, new rogue-lites must do something different in order to stand out, or at least be extremely good at what they do. As it stands,
brings nothing new or interesting to the table. It feels like it is still in Early Access, which is an issue for any new game, not just this one.
Overall,
is a hollow shell of a rogue-lite that is best given a miss, especially when there are so many better, more fulfilling titles on the market.
And another thing, referencing things that exist is not humour. You are not
, which isn't funny anyway.

I'm conflicted about this review. It's a nifty indy game with an interesting story line. As it stands now though the game is closer to an EA state than something I'd expect in a release.
Missing Features/Bugs:
Mouse support - Control is keyboard only (arrow key style), no mouse even in menus.
Mutiple resolution support - Windowed mode at a small resolution only. Cannot modify resolution or play full screen.
Display bug - When playing sometimes assets, like an enemy will not be displayed. Once this happens additional assets seem to go black. Currently I'm fighting a battle with only my party on a black screen.
It's also a bit pointelessly grindy, you can replay any mission you want as many times as you want to earn points. Those points can be used to increase the stats of any character. You end up grinding the same levels over and over to pump stats to keep getting 3-stars on missions. Go overboard and gameplay is pretty much broken.
I'd hope the developer addresses at least the glaring bugs. The story line is nifty enough to make me ignore the grindy bits.

This review is coming in two parts as this game needs to be looked at. First, is the standalone view of the game and what the devs are doing. And secondly, I will campare, like all games in a select genre there is a style that is looked at that all games try to emulate, and in this case would be madden.
So first off. I have a low-mid end pc and on similar graphic settings, the game runs very smooth, and looks pretty darn good for the settings, and on videos I have seen of people playing on high end pcs with top settings, the game looks gorgeous and plays just as smooth. Fantastic optismazation by the devs. The controls feel pretty fluid with a controller, and kind of iffy with keyboard and mouse. The aiming passing with the mouse completely shattered the standard button passing, I love it, but I have a hard time getting used to the jagged 8 direction movement of the keyboard with a personal opinion wonky key commands, but that is just me. When playing at speed, everything looks and plays as I would expect a 3 year old football game series to play when they have an amazingly devoted team behind it with constant updates and crowd sourced ideas. When slowed down, everything that should be in a football game, gameplay wise, is getting there year after year. The pocket, the running lanes, decent tackle animation. The point where the game is at with how it looks and plays, is a really nice balance as it does, what you would expect it to do. Be a little choppy, but solid. Very fun in creating a whole universe one afternoon, then the next be able to simulate years down the road just the see everything play out. The franchise is like a Betty Crocker recipe, it is good as a standalone if you take it without experience or expectations being it is a fantastic base that is solid and would not let you down ever. That being said, it is a good base, and like a lot of Betty Crocker recipes, it is good, but sometimes you just need to add a little cinnamon here, some sugar there, and now you have a fantasic football game. And after following these guys for awhile, they are bringing the whole spice rack into the dev cycle. Absolutely buy just for the fact that I don't think that I have ever seen a game progress as much in 3 years as this series. This game is fun to play and has a good base.
Now my second point. Comparing to madden. This game is not madden. Is it as pretty? No. Will it be? Very easily could be in a few years. Does this game have fancy presentation? No. WIll it? Absolutely in a few years. Is it a game series that is 25+ years old and have the money that comes along with it? No. Will it? Time, possibly, money? Personally I think that by 2020, NFL continues license with madden, yet Axis is right next to it in sales. Does this game not care about it fans and only cares about money with cash scam card building modes? No. Will it. Never. This game strives to be what madden used to be about, and what used to make it fun, and instead of taking good ideas that didn't work the first year and toss them in the trash like the vision cone, it will keep them and refine them and make them better because thats what good game teams do. Everything is trial, error, correct and repeat. Not trial, error, keep the same or trial, error, and toss out and bring back the errored way 3 years later and claim it is a new thing altogether.
Should you buy this game for its standalone gameplay and what it offers? 7/10 being some people live and die by graphics and the shiny new thing. For those people, don't. But for the people who care about decent gameplay for the price and a constant striving for simulation football, absoletly buy.
Should you buy this game to compete with Madden? 9/10. The only thing that would make somebody not want what these people are doing, is they like the NFL. They like playing with NFL teams. There is absoletly nothing wrong with that. But if you want to see a game do what it says it will, and do what other games say they do but dont, then absoletly buy this game.

UnEpic is a great game that I've been having fun with since it appeared in one of the IndieRoyale bundles last year. I've been waiting for it to come to Steam, because, frankly, it deserved to be on here. It's an amazing (Metroidvania-like) platformer with RPG elements, and it has some funny (but also annoying/childish) dialogs in it.
The world of UnEpic looks equally amazing thanks to the fantastic lighting in it. Along the way you'll find or earn gear that makes your character stronger, just like any other RPG basically. There are sidequests and bossfights, secrets to find, torches to light, you name it. It's a big world and completing the game will take you probably somewhere between 15-20 hours. That's long, if you ask me, especially for a price this low.
Only thing that truly annoyed me was the fact that it saves randomly, and it never shows an indication on when it's exactly saving. Not a big problem, but there's one boss fight that requires you to drop quite a few items. It was during that moment that I had to quit and the game saved my location, but not the items on the ground. So when I resumed I lost all of those items. 'Frustrating' is the word I'm looking for here. I hope it gets fixed before the official release, or that it allows you to manually save your game, instead of the game doing this for you. Ok, ok, enough rambling about something no one cares about.
Verdict: UnEpic is an epic game that needs to be experienced by all gamers out there.

I need to make a correction. Ashes DOES now run.
After several days of research I found that one of my Sapphire Nitro+ RX 480's IS defective. It runs everything fine by itself (so I thought) but I found the VRM was not correctly supplying voltage to the GPU and causing issues with all DX12 games under workload and more. Running my single 'good' GPU everything works beautifully. I do not reccommend this game at all, unless it goes on sale for less then $4. The so-called "twin-stick, gauntlet style/diablo/binding of isaac/etc" gameplay is not at all relateable, and the game turns into a hold an attack direction and wait for either an ability to go off cooldown (every 15 or so seconds) or have an ability proc an additional effect when you hit an enemy with a basic attack.
When you level up in this game, you get a tiny bit of health, and a tiny bit of damage. The game jokingly gives you the option of increasing Health, Attack Speed, Defense, and Damage. You can dump every point into damage, defense or attack speed, and you will notice zero difference. What kind of damage increment is a FRACTION of one point of damage, when monsters have increasingly high scaling health in the thousands and tens of thousands within a few hours of gameplay? What is 0.01% damage protection and attack speed?? Why would they have increments so damn minor they don't even matter?? At least with the health upgrade, you can maybe survive another hit with enough points... but therein lies the next problem.
This game has no difficulty curve, especially on one player. Eventually, you will be put in a situation where an attack is unnavoidable, because a projectile/enemy ability will FLASH across the screen (or off-screen) and hit you, which causes immediate death . Worse yet, enemies are capable of stunning and freezing you, even some common enemies, and they may continue to keep you locked in place permanantly until death.
Virtually every boss in the game has an ability that kills you in one hit from what I've found in my three hours of gameplay. It's so horribly painful to spend so much time grinding, just to be one-shot by something you couldn't avoid. Bosses are not fun to fight.
...With all that being said, the reason why I -do- like this game, is because it can be fun if you are looking for some silly mindless gameplay, especially if you are the sort that likes to grind for items. Don't get me wrong, the game is still horrible through-and-through, but random luck streaks are always exciting. But the time and price investment simply do not outweigh the issues
On a final note, multiplayer is still broken. So I guess it's permanantly single-player for a lot of folks in any case.

A fun experience with problems.
The Good:
Large scale conflict that runs on my potato with few issues.
Fairly decent campaign with fairly interesting characters and missions.
Hover armies have grown on me.
Decent selection of maps.
Good selection of units between the factions, even if their roles are unclear in the text box.
Army system where units are organised into armies and will micro themselves accordingly (I never use the queue for brining in certain troops to an army however, I prefer to be using my factories at all times making a collection of units and counters.)
PHC macross missile massacre supported by the big rail guns.
Substrate laser and plasma fun times with drones galore.
The Bad: (I like the game enough to complain about it constantly)
Orbital abilities that cost little to nothing, as you'll want the 'quanta' resource for upgrades anyway.
No ability to switch the orbital abilities to support only, it's either all, no nukes or nothing.
No warning when an opponent uses an ability near you, even when in strategic view mode. (Like a warning sign and stuff might be nice!)
Orbital abilities divided into several structures and have no clear icon in strategic view when you spot these important enemy structures.
Strategic view is mostly unhelpful at picking out dangerous forces or targets for the player, so everything can kinda blur together if you have inexperience.
The AI has a tendency of throwing it's game away by overspending on advanced defences and 'quanta' generators rather then fighting for map control.
Advanced defences have no clear counter as they beat the traditional artillery counter, often beat dreadnoughts and utterly slaughter frigates and cruisers.
Some maps are unbalanced in regards to territory lines.
Territory lines are hard to see, making territories very hard to find in the fog of war. (It's possible to finish a 2 hour mission only to find an extra metal territory right next door!)
Many campaign missions, if not all, are set upon skirmish maps. (They did a good job in spite of that however, loved the highland static defenders with the fifty billion turrets and no AA!)
Upgrades feel arbitrary, show no indication on units that they have been upgraded for the player or their opponent to see, but feel damn near essential to beating enemy advanced defences.
Audio bugs are present giving a disturbing 'underwater' sound or static when playing.
Other audio bugs often give a loud beep noise that sounds like a windows error, and can be terrifying when engrossed in the game.
There are no audio settings for turning ambient sounds down other then the master sound control. Leaving the game with the sound of wind or random birds in the background.
Unit balance feels a bit off (Could just be me), with frigates being utterly worthless past the first few minutes of a game, multiple units on a side being geared to fighting the same unit type (Like 3-4 different units that counter frigates.)
Substrate forces being generally better then their PHC counterparts (That could just be me.)
Substrate getting army annihilating defences, when PHC has nothing remotely as effective. (In my opinion.)
Strategic bombers that have a HUGE amount of HP that, in a twist of irony, most AA static defences struggle to kill. (Guess only fighters are good against them?)
Unit bugs where many forces seem to sit around and not fire at enemy targets they are clearly engaged with. (Even when fully charged by medics and power charging frigates.)
UI bugs where pressing A to attack move can often deselect the current army and then stay trying to order an attack move to units that don't exist.
UI where selecting units and buildings to place can often not go through.
Sometimes orders aren't given. It's often unclear what building you have selected when placing structures. Placing buildings does not feel very nice and is often sluggish to move across the screen (Could be a problem with my frame rate?) The inability to drag out a line of structures to queue them up (Like wanting to drag down a line of turrets or 'quanta' generators.)
Managing your macro can often be a pain, as there is only one structure you can build at a metal/radioactive deposit, and only one above a power point yet you must select the structure type from the menu to build these structures. A simple click on the deposit with an engineer could be more efficient. (Not that big of an issue.)
There are likely many more issues that I have told myself over the past week of playing this game, but I can't remember them right now and haven't struck with me quite like these.
But as I said above, I do genuinely like this game, so much that I want to complain even more! This game is more of a continuation of the evolution of the large scale RTS and I really like the Army system.
It's has it's share of problems, and I'm personally not a fan of the current direction of the game with a planned tier 4 and possibly even tier 5 of units, nor am I a fan of the turtle style of play as I see it as a boring way to lose/win the game in either case.
This is a fun game however, with most of the games management in the macro side of setting up resources, static defences for your outposts and to prevent bomber shenanigans, lining up your factories to produce the mix of forces you think you are going to need and finally sending off a fully managed group of hover boats to get stuck in the conflict. It's great and I recommend it if you love games like Total Annihilation, Supreme Commander 1 and 2 or even Planetary Annihilation!

Princess.Loot.Pixel.Again is an addicting rogue-lite platformer, with randomly generated dungeons. The game has different classes that you can go through the dungeon as, and artifacts that can sharpely change the game fast. I was just reviewing this game when the developer randomly posted an update titled "FULL RELEASE!" This update changed almost nothing, and gives me mixed feelings on the game as it stands. So keeping that in mind, lets go through the gameplay.
You start your dungeon run by selecting one of 7 classes. Each class has a unique playstyle, with certain skills the others lack (speed, strength, crits) are quite balanced, and lead to strong replayability. Any character you choose will start you off with 3 bombs and 3 keys, with bombs you can blow up walls, and with keys you can open any locks on any doors or chests. After you spawn in you'll be running room to room, slaying monsters, blowing up crumbling walls, hoping for green chests, entering shops, picking up items, unlocking doors, solving jump puzzles, defeating bosses, making dark deals, upgrading your weapon and hopefully having lots of fun :)
+Unique class system
+Randomly generated levels
+Unique artifacts that alter gameplay
+The game tests your reaction and patience
+Great soundtrack
+Steam cards and achievements
-In need of more enemies and artifacts
-Bosses need to be balanced
-Rng plays too heavy of a role in succeeding
I highly recommend to any player that enjoys rogue-lite games. The game is all about how you react, you can go hacking n' slashing through rooms, but you could fall in acid, be too timid and you could get hit with a fireball, the result of someones run is a reflection of balancing strategies and having the scale tip in thier favor. The different classes and game changing artifacts strongly give the ability to play the game more and more, and even though the game cut out most of the story elements, and it would be nice to have more enemies, the game accomplishes a fun 10+ hours of mastering each class, and the weakness and strengths to items and powerups in the game. Despite having a number of flaws, I continue to come back to the game and is now one of my favorite games in my library, and I dont say that lightly. The game could have been the platformer successor of Binding of Isacc, it could have been the next new, great, rogue-like game out there, development has ceased, but trust me, NO ONE will be happier than me, if this project is picked back up again.

There are few games that I would ever give the title of "Epic". Mostly because that terms is sadly applied to every mediocre title or franchise that comes down the pike, that it's really lost all clout. However, Borderlands is a title, if not a franchise, that deserves such a monicker.
Right from the opening movie, the game immerses you into the world of Pandora as seen through the eyes of four "Vault Hunters" seeking a legend told to them in youth. But Pandora isn't your usual Sci Fi planet filled with green skinned women and chest bursting aliens. Rather, it's the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child of a massive scrap yard and the movie 'Deliverance', as mountains of discarded trash make up the scenery and most of the inhabitance would rather fornicate with your corpse rather than talk to you. Laden with the blackest of humor, characters that are both hilarious and creepy, Borderlands is an experience that should be a part of every game collection.
Mechanical speaking, you will find few titles as sound as this. Playable on both high power PCs and even strip down models, the FPS mechanics are impeccably done, merging gun and run with special abilities and traits that make each hunter an experience in themselves to play. This title is a must for co-op players who are looking for a game that they will play over and over again. DLC is solid, and gives a great in between for players that still want to experience Borderlands without playing the main title, or sinking to play the horribly sub-par sequel.
This game will give you it's worth, even at full price. I've owned it for a few years now, and I still go back with my friends and play it through again, still finding new guns and items not found in previous playthroughs.

A rollicking good 25 hour space opera. The tactical battles are difficult but fun and upgrading your ships with new goodies is gratifying. It's even fun to hate Admiral Norbank, who has got to be one of the biggest asses ever put into a video game. The gameplay is unique in that you have a relatively small fleet of large, powerful capital ships that do not maneuver quickly and have multiple weapon systems. They have a weight to them that feels awesome.
There are a lot of tools available for modding the game but precious little has been done with them... not sure why. I got the game for $2.49, figuring for that price I could hardly go wrong. I was completely stunned at what I got and I can't figure out how I managed to miss this gem. Even if it isn't on sale it's worth every penny. If you like Sins of a Solar Empire or Homeworld then I can't imagine how you wouldn't like Nexus: The Jupiter Incident. Oh... and the Angelwing is simply an awesome craft that you can hardly help getting attached to.
I've seen a lot of bad reviews that complained that the game wouldn't run or that it crashed a lot. I'm not sure what their issue is but I can say that Nexus ran fine on my system (Windows 7, Intel CPU, Nvidia GPU) and I never crashed once while playing. On my original playthrough, the game lost some key bindings when I alt-tabbed out and it didn't have any Steam Integration, so I couldn't use shift-tab to access messages and whatnot. I also had to create my own desktop shortcut, as the game wouldn't run via the Steam generated desktop shortcut. The in-game videos also ran choppy from time to time, which was odd. ALL of this has been fixed with a recent update. Current generation resolutions are supported, it has Steam Integration, and the videos now run smooth as silk, though they are somewhat low res when compared to gameplay resolutions of 1920x1080 or higher. The game always looked good but now it looks better than ever! I'm finding myself just as captivated with the story, visuals, and gameplay on my second playthrough as when I first played it. Simply astonishing! If you have been on the fence about getting Nexus, don't wait another moment.
Hint: Read the manual. It won't take long, as the information is very concise, but there are some nuances to successful navigation (how to create your own navigation points), using all your weapons (how to attack multiple targets at once), and managing systems that you won't get from the in-game advice popups.  :)

On the "plus" side, The Silent Age is a nice old school point and clic game, with some good elements (time travel, manipulating puzzles in two eras and the paradoxes that come with it), easy navigation, friendly gameplay, fine graphics for this kind of game and interesting plot twists. I felt in immersion in the story and cared about what happened to the main character.
On the improvement points, there could be more difficulty in puzzles. Use of the objects is sometimes too obvious and linear and you only have a few rooms to clean of objects per level to figure what to do; few useless//weird items to make you go around, trying and failing; those who played Indiana Jones, The Secret Of Monkey Island or Day Of The Tentacle series might understand what I mean.
Life extending elements could be good too, as I felt it finished kickly, but I think it goes well with the pace of the game. You don't loose interest, you end the game wanting to learn more but feeling you had what you came for.
To conclude, a great game for the price, a "feel good" game for the nostalgics and the newcomers as well and a really thrilling story. Good job, developpers!

This is my favorite racing game so far.  It is better than all of the fancier-looking ("serious") racing games I've tried.  My biggest complaints about racing games are usually around controls (either too sensitive and you drift all over, or not sensitive enough, and you can't even make a turn) and/or that the game is just boring.  This game has neither of those issues.  As far as controls go, they feel very responsive and fair, and each character's car handles a little differently, so you can experiement and find one that works best for you.  As for boring, the races all have parts of the course with air/water or other environments to keep you on your toes.  Your vehicle will automatically morph (to a boat or aircraft) and will handle a little differently during these portions.  You also have weapons you can deploy and defend against, sort of like Mario Kart.  Non-competitor enemies will also popup and try to slow your progress, but not in a way that is impossible to avoid.  I definitely recommend this game if you are looking for a good racing game and not too concerned about super-realistic graphics or any sort of pseudo-narrative/campaign mode.

A+ for effort.  Sports video games are the only thing I truly miss about console gaming.  While I can spend a fair amount of time with FIFA and NBA 2k, they aren't what I want to be honest.  I want the NHL, I want the NFL, MLB, and NCAA football and basketball.  Axis 2017 brings us one step closer to having a great PC american football game.
Do not buy Axis Football if you want a perfect, Madden EA quality game.  The playbooks are basic and quite limited, the passing game is a bit wonky, franchise mode is nothing compared to an EA or 2k game, I really could go on for a while here.
That being said, I definitely recommend Axis Football 2017, and am quite happy with my purchase.  (on sale for 17.99$. )  While far from perfect, Axis has released a fun football game for PC gamers.  This years game is a marked improvement over last years offering.  The developers really seem like they want to make the best football game possible, and I'm excited about what the next version will look like.  And if you don't like the non NFL teams in the base game, there are mods that give you lots of options.
TL;DR?
It's far from perfect, but it beats a modded Madden 08.  Mods in development, game constantly improving.  If you want a american foodball game on the PC, I suggest supporting these developers and their effort.

This is the first game I've bought in spite of "mixed" or lower reviews. I just wanted to weigh in and say -- like some others have said -- this isn't Madden, but it's football on the PC, it works, and it's fun.
I'm three games deep, but based on the reviews I thought it was quite possible I'd be quitting & refund requesting midway through the first one. The graphics are admittedly not flashy, the physics can be a bit weird, and the controls have been tricky but not in a way that's hurt the game for me. I bought Mutant Football before this one based on one review, and while MFL is fun, it's not really football. You can't kill other players and refs in real football, you can't become huge on one play and crush all defenders under your feet, etc. This game IS football. The strategy is there, the plays are numerous and they work.
This is clearly not made by a big studio with a ton of money, which is why the negative reviews here are a shame. This company should be making some money and seeing that there's a demand for a great football game on PC. That will either convince EA to finally put Madden on PC or allow Axis to continue to improve their game. What's here is playable and fun, and while it has its issues, if you're a football fan it's absolutely worth the $20.

Well, what do I say about this game? It's a shame that some people negatively view this game and compare it to Madden. First of all, you can't expect actual NFL teams due to licensing issues. Second, of course this game is not going to be as beautiful as Madden or deep with depth. It's a small team with a noticeably smaller budget than EA (By a few million...). With that being said there are things that I do enjoy about this game. 1. The physics in the game are interesting to say the least. I enjoy the tackling and the different ways thay players are tackeld or fall over. (P.S. Scrambling as a quarterback and launching yourself into a defender is hilarious). 2. The passing game (With the aiming rather than just pressing on an icon) is great. I love being able to decide where the football will go rather than just tapping a button. 3. The defender chasing is better than Madden (Yes, I said it). The defenders will actually run towards the area where the ball holder is running rather than making boneheaded mistakes such as running straight into an offensive lineman who can throw them to the ground or running in fifty different directions before finally running after the ball carrier. Those are three of the biggest positives that I take from this game. Now, there is obvious work to be done, but the dev team is responsive and looking to build up from this game. I knew what to expect (Unlike some negatative reviewers) and I took a chance on this game because I miss playing simulation football. I hope that Axis Football only continues to trend upward from here and I am already looking forward to Axis Football 2018 without having even finished my first season in this game. Understand what you're paying for and why you're paying for it before you go and write a review about how you expected this game  to be like Madden. (Seriously, can people not read reviews or do some research on a game before buying it?)

It's pretty fun. But the controls are really really bad. SC2 makes everything really easy. You just can put stuff in control groups. And you can select parts of your army to move them. In this, everything always gets stuck together. Then bundled up. It shouldn't be automatic. It should be manual. If I want to take a unit or a portion of units away from the army, it selects the entire army as soon as I click a unit. Automating it doesn't make things more convenient. It makes it much more difficult.
The game is supposed to be more macro oriented than SC2, but you still need to be able to control units properly so you're not a-moving your army mindlessly. You still need to be able to separate units back if they take damage. Especially the heroes. As well as be able to harass with some squads. I was able to pull of some of it in playing practice with somebody. But the controls is a really big problem with this game. There should at least be options on how you want the controls and bundling to work.
I wouldn't necessarily recommend this game to anybody until it gets more polished. It can be a waste of money if you end up playing it just to get tired of the controls. If you do get this game, the tutorial is terrible. However, the campaign is a tutorial as well. It does much better at teaching you everything. I'm referring to the base campaign. As stunned as I was that Stardock releasd Escalation as a standalone DLC when it just delivers on my original expectation of the unfinished steaming pile of Beta that was AotS vanilla, I still ponied up for the 50% off version of escalation. Worth it. For $60, ashes scratches a unique itch that forged alliance has left untended for years.
Units and structures are constructed using engineers and credits over time a la Forged Alliance.
Bases can actually be built up and defended in a meaningful way.
Some structures can be upgraded, units unlock with the right pre-reqs rather than a clear tier 1-2-3 system.
Dreadnaughts, while limited to Rock, Paper, Scissors feel like Experimentals, leveling and earning abilities.
Unfortunately if you are looking for online multiplayer action, AotS is completely dead. After bending over every longtime fan of the genre who supported the early access AotS Vanilla, the animosity was bound to have repercussions. Just look at the reviews on the original. That said, I paid for both, $60 total, and I received 20 hours of fun so far and counting. Half the price and twice the entertainment of a trip to a theme park.

I've had this game on my wishlist for a while but the price tag (£26.99) was just way to high, however I had some money in my steam account so decided to use it on this and finally take a leap of faith and buy it.
Just for information this game is currently at a tech demo stage and therefore VERY early stages of development.
As you would expect there are so many bugs and issues however due to the early stage I wasn't really looking at that. To start off with positives :
I think in a few years this game "could" (I’ve supported many EA games that have stopped production before) be something great. I love the idea that you get to control all the emergency services and can customise the police and EMS vehicles on the fly.  Imagine joining your friends and creating scenarios and responding to calls and working together as a team. The idea of a whole city to put out fires, respond to crimes and medical situations is really the game I have always wanted. However, this game is SO far away from this at the moment and is at its very core a grand idea at the moment.
Visually the fire engines look pretty impressive as well as the blue and red lights on the buildings as you pass.  The sirens sound very realistic and traffic actually gets out of your way as you go behind them. Inside the engines looks amazing too very highly detailed.
Overall they have so much to implement and that includes first person, fires to respond too, multiplayer, scene command (what will the EMS and police do) iron out all the bugs, model the city, better UI, better controls, physics .... I could go on and well this will take a very long time to impliment all this.  The last update they talk about a multiplayer option, I just don’t understand this line of devlopment . Get the rest sorted, work on the game add some content and then once you have that then maybe bring the multiplayer in.
So in summing up maybe this game will be great, maybe this game will fall flat on its face and I personally don't think the money they are asking for at this point in time is justifiable or worth it. If it was £10 I would maybe take the risk but for £26.99 for and don't forget the term DEMO I’ll refund and invest in something else.

Updated 7/22/2017 - Alright, so first off I've upgraded to an EVGA GTX 1060 6GB from an EVGA GTX 960 4GB ftw edition. Played for almost two hours straight and the game is comletely stable for me now using both DX 11 & 12. Now I'm not sure myself, but assuming since it's a new better GPU, I imagine this is the biggest difference unless there have been updates I'm unaware of which heavily addressed stabiliy issues. But, as said, the game appears to be %100 stable for me now using this new GPU.
Updated 4/30/2017 - Stability seems a bit better, though about as intermittent. Killing any third party programs still seems to help, but in the end, killing every process I can, lowering graphics, underclocking and et cetera, I still experience fairly consistant CTD's on both DX11/12. I suppose I may be in a unique set of circumstances, but seeing as things are still improving on Stardock's end and that I really do like this game in spite of technical difficulties, I'm changing my recommendation from a "no" to something of a "soft yes." Just keep up the work and get this game a bit more stable!
This is still something of an early impression review, as I'm not done with the campaign yet and haven't played multi-player.
Now I do like the feel of this game, a streaming economy which feels a bit like how the Dawn of War games and Rise of Nations works. Combat feels fairly smooth with the 'army' function, which allows you to conform multiple units to act and behave as a single unit which increases the armies effectiveness. It's actually a pretty nifty and the AI acts well, that said the enemy AI is compotent and doesn't behave weird or plain dumb like a lot of RTS games which suffer from dumb AI. So kudo's on that.
Now for instability. I'm to understand the game was designed for DirectX 12 and Windows 10. Both of which I'm using and the game is pretty unstable, or at least was. I still experience crash to desktop every so often, but when it will happen is totally unpredictable. Though typically I'm able to get a good hour in before the game cleanly drops to desktop, sometimes with an error stating my video driver has failed and recovered. I've lowered my graphics down and disabled an overlays, such as the Steam and Nvidia GeForce experience overlays. Now I can't say whether or not this problem is unique to me, but from searching I can see a lot of people have problems with this game and instability.
So where the game is kind of fun, it fails on it's technical side on a subjective level. Though I imagine better rigs with superior gpu/cpu's may perform better with stronger stability, I can't recommend this game until these issues are addressed by the developer. But this game is worth keeping an eye on if you're really into real time strategy games.
Pros:
-On higher graphics, this game looks fantastic
-Strong AI
-Unique gameplay mechanics, though very subtle
-Decent tutorial and introductions
Cons:
-Game is very unstable
-Game is very taxing on gpu, pushing high temps and bottlenecks very quickly
I really don't have much bad to say, though ten years down the road this could be looked at as a run of the mill real time strategy which failed in the shadow of it's better bigger brother Sins of a Solar Empire (a much much better game, same developer, Stardock games) which is much more worth checking out.

The game is super fun and reminscient of Rogue Legacy in the satisfaction department when it comes to opening chests, getting relics (Hero Siege-style, which can be annoying at first because you don't always know what they do), and doesn't make you feel like you need to save expendable items like the bombs and keys.  The combat leaves a lot to be desired, it's just simply too easy.  Nothing poses a challenge to a player who knows NES-era dodge tactics (...move left and right).  Even the last boss is so incredibly easy that I sat there expecting a "this isn't even my final form" type of encounter.
But, I still recommend the game because it does have some replay value and for $5, that can't be beat.  If you're decent at games, expect about 2 hours to beat it the first time with less than 1 hr required for subsequent completions.  The achievements add some incentive to keep playing for a few run throughs, but you'll be burnt out if you try to complete it consecutively with each class in an effort to 100% the game.
If expanded upon with some content that adds more depth via levels, monsters, and bosses could really shine.

This is a fantastic game, mainly because of it's realism factor. But I want to tell you one key thing: If you buy this game, don't give up on it after the first few sessions! Even after watching the tutorial videos and playing on the tutorial server, I found the first few games to be frustrating. I was getting killed multiple times (by enemies who were smartly utilizing cover) and I didn't know what I was doing. HOWEVER* once I got the hang of the controls and communication, this game became a blast. I eventually learned to use cover to my advantage. I used communication with my squad to stay on top of what was happening in the game. I frequently looked at the map to gather intel on the surrounding area. I stuck with my squad mates and supported them. I asked them questions about enemy locations and fostered communication. I realized that when I first started playing the game, I wasn't using these key strategies. As a result, I have spent a few sessions playing hour long games with really amazing groups of people, in conflicts where I genuinely feel like we have worked as a cohesive team.
This is NOT your standard FPS - when you kill an enemy, there is no "+50 score!" notification that would be reinforcing to some players who are used to standard games. There is no "Kill Death Ratio" score either. It's all about team work, suppressing the enemy, defending and attacking objectives. I love this game and it has fast become my favorite, and I only have 8 hours of gameplay in.
UPDATE: 28 hours in and I am still going. A couple of notable experiences: Mortar rounds falling down around our squad and hearing the tiny bits of concrete/rubble hit the ground in the aftermath; Moving through tall grass with our squad and hearing the buzzing of flies in the grass around us; As a marksman doing overwatch for our squad while they were inside a compound and spotting enemy infantry and vehicles moving toward compound thus resulting in successful defense of the position. These are just a few of many awesome experiences. Just remember to assume the role you have in that game - if you're a medic, expect not to get too many kills, if you're anti tank, be johnny on the spot with the LAW/RPG, if you are the squad AR then put down some suppressive fire and cover your teammates. This game is all about team work.
