Wondering what it feels like to play squad? Here is a true story.
You get orders from Squad 1 to make your way to a town 500m north... Your squad leader sets a rally point for a valley and you all gather around it and talk about what your roles are and how to attack the town. A moving object catches your attention and you see an enemy squad walking on the ridge... You break the conversation by yelling " CONTACT TO THE LEFT!"
You're SL tells everyone to hold fire and wait for line of sight... Then an rpg goes off.... You hear a man screaming medic!!! and others yelling "bearing 260, 100 meters!" rifle fire exploads everywhere! You can't distinquish your gun from the man next to you.... Bullets are raining down, and you hope that since you can't see them anymore they can't see you... You fire to where you think the enemy is. But that does not stop the earth from errupting around you under small arms fire.... Someone screams "MEDIC DOWN!" but you have no chance to react. Your SL throws down smoke and tells you to advance, by the time you make it to the enemy you find 6 dead bodies and see another man running away... Did you shoot someone? Did you manage to kill them all, or were you the only one who couldn't see them? You decide not to ask questions as it might take away the flavor of the small victory.
Your tired and injured group rallies around, deploying a spawn point for the fallen... Only half of you are left standing.
You hear a faint rumbling... (what is that sound you think to yourself) "GET DOWN!" your SL yells just as a BTR opens fire on what's left of your squad...
Your eyes blocked by the grass you pray that the shots will not find you... Hoping the btr will think he whiped your squad and go somewhere else to hunt. But the shots keep coming your vision is fading. You pull out a medic kit to patch yourself, as you think, what's the point, we are all dead anyways...
BANG!!! the sky above the grass fills with explosion and smoke... BAM! A second explosion and shrpanel flying all around. The sound of the btr's guns tearing through the air is gone... The only sounds left are rocks finding their way back down to earth... Then there is a still silence around your location now as smoke rises into the clouds a hundred meters away...
Not being able to keep from the curiosity you look up.
Squad 5 made its way to your location and thier Heavy AT has saved you.... Alone you stand with your SL wondering, will the rest of your mission be even harder.... You lost 7 men in under 2 minutes... a heavy price to pay when you are still 300 meters from the town. But you must carry on, you must continue.... You are a soilder and your mission is not done.
Absolute amazing game, you can play it for hours.

So after 150 hours I've decided to finally do a review.
I've had experience in many different fps games over the years but recently my interest in them dwindled. From arma to csgo to battlefield, I played them a fair bit, but only played them casually and didn't see them as rewarding enough to fully sink some hours into end on end - something was missing for me.
Then squad rolled in.
I spent my first match running around as many do trying to kill anything that didn't have that green name tag. I died repeatedly. Confused and frustrated I tried different approaches but ultimately kept on drifting off into that typical fps mentality and tried soloing it. The struggle was real until a voice came down my headset. "Crow, meet me at this marker on foot, I've got a plan. Open your map with the M key to take a look" I hadn't been paying attention to the comms chatter and shrugged my shoulders and thought right ok, the squad leader must have been able to tell I was new.
I walked along to the marker taking cover where I could, being cautious because I had been getting picked off all game. I waited at the marker prone next to a bush for a solid 3-5 minutes.
The SLs voice came over in proximity, "me and you are going to get a rally set up behind enemy lines so our team can outflank and secure the objective" I can't remember the guys name to save the life of me, but what followed was the most bad♥♥♥♥♥teamwork I have ever experienced in any game. I was hooked, this game shined like no other fps, what was really missing in the rest of the fps games.
Me and the SL proceeded onto a town, clearing rooms as we moved along, leap frogging and providing each other cover as we progressed, he called out enemies and so did I and we dropped them in sync. We were deep in enemy turf now. He told me not to fire. I held fire. A habit I found hard to break. But I did. We ended up at a point where he placed the rally. Squad members spawned in. Anti tanks and lmgs in hand. We began our assault on the enemy flag. Explosions galore and bullets whizzing everywhere. We secured it after 10 minutes of very intense fighting. We lost by 7 tickets.  He thanked me and the rest of the squad and acknowledged our teamwork.
I played the game all night and now I squad lead regularly. Something I initially thought would not be my thing.  This game is for a niche market. And It's hard to break them old fps habits.  But when you do - it's worth every ♥♥♥♥ing penny.
Get this masterpiece.  Thankyou devs.

There's some really good points to this game. It presents interesting moral dilemmas and branching story lines, which, combined with limited resource availability, forces you to make choices (often choices between the lesser of two evils). The core gameplay mechanics are simple but entertaining. There is a fairly large element of trial and error here, though this is balanced by a fairly generous autosave system, enabling you to try out different options without starting again.
The difficulty can be fairly unforgiving. This isn't a bad thing in itself, but I think it can detract from the narrative elements of the game. Additionally sometimes the game becomes difficult simply because the game fails to communicate to the player effectivley. For example in one instance I was tasked with removing propaganda banners and, despite having several cutting tools in my inventory, the game insisted that I couldn't remove them with my bare hands. I also came across a few glitches in my playthrough, nothing gamebreaking, but overall the game felt a little unpolished.
For the price, I'd probably recommend it.

If you can stand cheesy humour and gamurr references galore, this is actually a really good metroidvania. The UI is the first of its kind in the genre, boasting interesting and really PC-spesific features (hotkeys, customizable windows, etc.). The weapons also adds extra layers of meta game, because the various weapon types don't just vary in speed, damage and other common stats. You will have to build your character wisely, because putting all your points in a singular weapon type is sure to fail as soon as you go up against an enemy with strong defenses against it. You also have pets and spells and armour and potions and scrolls, and all that good stuff.
The RPG levelling system is deep and allows for much experimentation. The visuals are decent, the music is good and the story is pretty uninteresting.
A coop multiplayer mode recently appeared in the main menu, which I'm looking forward to trying out.

Great game with an awesome competitive community. Thanks to the developers for continuing to update this! I play this on Ubuntu (Linux), it also works on Mac, instructions below:
Install PlayOnMac/PlayOnLinux (POM/POL; ensure that you click to install XQuartz when it asks you to). Install Age of Empires II HD from that (you may need to check the Testing checkbox when searching for the installer in the program). On the Age of Empires II HD entry in POM/POL, hit Configure, then the Miscellaneous tab, then Open program's directory, then rename Launcher.exe to Launcher.exe.bak and rename AoK HD.exe to Launcher.exe. Then you should be able to launch AoE II HD from POM/POL.
Every time AoE is patched, you'll need to reinstall AoE to install the patch properly and get multiplayer to work. Going back to Configure for AoE, click 'Make a new shortcut from this virtual drive', then click Steam.exe or whatever Steam's launcher is, then Next, then 'I don't want to make another shortcut', then Next. Launch Steam from that new POM/POL entry, right-click on AoE in your library and click Uninstall. Then install it again. You'll probably need to rename the AoK HD.exe launcher as I described every time you reinstall too.
The process to install AoE on Mac/Linux will change when POM/POL 5 aka Phoenicis is released.

Day 1 - Wick, Adam, & Amber are flung onto the unknown grasslands of a strange planet. Adam & Amber, being lovers, clutch on to one another for safety. Immediately all three, under the influence of a cursor, carve their way into a mountain that has only one entry point and make some beds from the poplar trees they found nearby. A stale survival meal gives them nourishment for the night.
Day 3 - The food supply cannot sustain with the eight survival meals remaining. Adam becomes the farmer for the group and begins planting potatoes, wheat, and rice. Amber begins hunting nearby game and making a freezer for the meat. Wick is still digging into the mountain. Wick is found to be the rival of Adam. No wonder he looks at him with disdain!
Day 7 - A week has passed. Wick has recovered steel, components, and other materials from mining. He begins researching a new form of crafting for the group. It seems like Wick is doing all of the work. Adam and Amber are happy that they are still together. A caravan from another group comes by. They exchange an assault rifle for some of the group's rice and potatoes. Wait, was that all of the food? Wick is furious.
Day 12 - Amber has killed nearly every animal (or things that even move) in the area. The freezer is full of meat and potatoes now. There are enough meals to last the group through the winter for sure. The group decides to name the town "Myro". They also decide to call their group "The Black Sun Empire". Pretty lofty for three space dweebs, but it has a nice ring to it. Defences are made. A vistor, Sheckly, decides to stay with the group. He takes the place of Wick. Wick is now in charge of defences (and planting flowers).
Day 26 - The settlement has grown into a small village. Pigs and boars have been tamed. A Llama wanted to stay in Myro. An entire farmhouse/pigpen has been created for the new domesticated animals. Life is well in Myro. Everyone smokes Smokeleaf and is at ease. When raids come, the settlers close the main gate and send out the three guards, with Wick at the helm of the town's defence. The town has an election. Adam is chosen as the leader, as most people connect with him since he is a farmer and populist candidate. Wick becomes jealous.
Day 31 - It is a quiet day in Myro. The total population of the town is now 19 citizens. The farmers are out in the fields harvesting and planting. The tailors and smiths are crafting away. The lone artist, Zeko, is sculpting another wacky statue. However, Wick and Adam get into an argument outside of the gates. Adam lands a punch on Wick, but Wick draws his pistol and puts a bullet straight through his head. The town guard come out and see Adam's head blown open with Wick standing over him. They do not arrest Wick. He buries Adam in a shallow grave outside of town. Everyone asks where Adam has gone when he isn't back in town by nightfall. Wick says he has no idea, but that he knew Adam was becoming very stressed by leading the entire town. The citizens want to wait a few days before they have another election. Amber knows what really happened, but is too afraid of Wick to say anything.
Day 38 - A week has passed since Adam went missing. The town decides to move forward with the election. Wick is the new leader of the town. He immediately has Amber framed for the murder of Adam, since she thought he was seeing another woman. Probably Elise, the nurse who always takes care of his wounds. Wick throws her into the town's jail, which is located out of town for some reason. There is to be a trial, but no one comes in defence of Amber. The town needed a scapegoat, and Wick knew just who it should be.
Day 43 - Amber has been found guilty. She is to be executed. Wick is waiting in the center of town with the rest of the citizens while Amber is dragged by the guards. Wick proclaims that Amber needs to confess her crimes, but all she does is spit on his face. Wick smiles, wipes it off, and pulls out his pistol. Wick looks Amber in the eyes and pulls the trigger. Now the true era of The Black Sun Empire has begun...

An absolutely brilliant game, and one of the best single player first person shooters I've ever played.
Smooth, responsive, and satisfying gunplay, a wonderfully diverse pantheon of weapons (many of which have secondary modes of fire that essentially turn them into new weapons), and delightfully gory deaths and animations make the gameplay an absolute blast, whether you decide to play as a stealthy assasin, a dual-wielding berserker, or anything in between. A mix of old-school design sensibilities and modern polish makes for a refreshing and unique combo that more games could learn to model.
What really suprised me about this game, however, was the story. It's good. Really good. At least, compared to the majority of first person shooters out there. It's powerful. It's dramatic. It's got touches of levity where it's needed.
And most importantly, it gives the game a soul. Something warm, and distinct, that keeps it from being generic and forgettable. It's half the reason I like the game so much, honestly. It's got a soul. You don't see that all that often in AAA productions nowadays.
All in all, this is one I highly recommend. If you like intense shooting, tense stealth, old-school game elements, captivating stories, alternate history fiction, or just slaughtering hordes of Nazi scum, try it. It's good.

Escalation is a stand alone expansion to Ashes of the Singularity. Includes all the same campaigns as vanilla Ashes as well as extra content. Dont buy vanilla Ashes just go straight for Escalation, you are seriously missing out on nothing by buying Escalation without getting vanilla Ashes.
Great strategic focused game, more emphasis on the greater strategic plan compared to more tactical intensive games like Starcraft, although there is still a lot of tactical options.
Territories with resources must be linked to generate resources, so that opens up nice options for attacking an enemy behind their front lines, and cutting off their supply lines, using a wide variety of orbital abilities.
Wide variety of units and buildings between the two factions, means both factions play differently to one another but are still easy to learn to use.
Compared to Supreme Commander Ashes plays very similar to but at a faster pace but not so much that it becomes an issue of actions per minute means victory.
Multiplayer is alive and kicking. I play 2-3 matches per day (lasting ~30 minutes each) and the most i have to wait in ranked queue is 4 min on a bad day.
Continuous development from the devs means only more good things to come. So even now, we have a entirely new tier of super heavy units coming out soon, as well as additional units for each tier currently available, from Frigates to Dreadnaughts and even naval units in the near future.
As of June, we now have two massive new units (one for each side). They are called Juggernauts, were added to the game for free, add yet another dimension to the game and apparently another few are on the way. So the game just keeps getting better and better..

Very much a spiritual successor to Supreme Commander.  Ashes of the singularity: Escalation is a huge improvement from the base game that came out earlier this year.
If you enjoy battles with lots of units, getting dizzying arrays of resources/powers at your command, you will enjoy Ashes.  The one major difference if you haven't played the base game between this and most RTS's (Namely Supcom), is that resources are driven by capturable nodes, that are improveable by your engineers in order to generate additional resources.  Having to expand yourself very thin in order to capture enough nodes to keep your war machine running can be very challenging at first, but is a very rewarding style of gameplay that forces both the AI and players to look at other options rather than simply seizing one point and holding.
Overall, I greatly enjoy this game, and am very excited to see what comes next.

Hero Siege is a fun little game to waste your time on, it has a very large amount of playtime in it, as every run that you do through the game is completely randomized, and you will almost never get the same run as you had before.
Pros
+Hundred of hours of playtime
+Little fun references
+Relic system is very similar of The Binding of Issac
+Many classes to choose from
+Many skills and attributes to level
+can have 10 different characters
+Full gamepad support
Cons
-Can be aggravating when you first start
-Only local coop for people without The Karp of Doom
-Hard to keep track of projectiles and the player on the later waves, such as wave 40+
-Cannot shoot diagonally
-Some classes are much more powerful than the others
-Some projectiles do too much damage (enough to three shot the strongest classes at their lower levels)
I would give this game a 9/10 because of the playtime and rpg aspects, while also having all of the relics that you can get, which reminds me of binding of issac a lot. The multiplayer is in alpha, which is why it is exclusive to the DLC, as they are not prepared for everyone who has the game get on multiplayer, as their servers cannot handle it, even now, they have a very large amount of server issues and bugs in multiplayer, but the local coop is still fun and enjoyable. Yeah, review. There you go. My impressions on this game.

So this was the first HP style tank game I'vre really ever played. I hated the idea of gold ammo and this game fit the arcade bill nicely while War Thunder hits the more sim aspect. There was no gold ammo, tanks had a decent amount of upgrades and there was tons of potential and a good player base to build on in the US. I absolutely loved the game and couldn't get enough.
Then all of a sudden things just started to go downhill. PVE is a GREAT thing to offer and this games PVE is very passable and can be enjoyable but has had a lot of problems with how AI bots spawned (and still does). It was however a nice thing to have and to offer as a practice mode before going to PVP.
/ Obsidian decided to normalize the rewards (both XP & credits) between the two modes the game had (at the time). Wihle PVP was still more, PVE was not that far behind. This basically pushed all players who were tired of some of the more 'toxic' player attitudes in PVP right to PVE. The player base started to drop some.
Then, and my memory is a little fuzzy here, however i have have not seen it happen in years, they decided to REMOVE ammo racking from the game and in some ways 'dumb it down' in terms of aiming complexity. In some ways that was a good thing as pixel hunting can be incredibly annoying at times. However, this was viewed as a more 'casualization' of the game and the player base dropped even more.
With the normalization of rewards, the removal of ammo racking / casualization, the extremely slow to seemingly non-existent release of new tanks / content, the inability to run events (as they never started or seemed to work as intended), the release of premium tanks that were nothing more than reskins of existing premium tanks, forcing players to split progress between two possibly three servers (EU / NA maybe even RU)
Global Ops, while a fantastic mode was too little too late. Combining some of the best of PVE & PVP this would have been the best mode to start the closed beta with several years ago (hindsight) but adding it about a year ago with an already sparsely populated game (on the NA server) and trying to split that small population between three modes did nothing to help anything.
Lastly,
refusal to merge the main servers along with the decision to have players play through steam on a separate launcher aka not merging the accounts (prior to steam release) while the game is dying further pushed players away as an obvious 'cash grab' to capitalize on WoT's disenfranchised.
It's a shame really. There was tremendous potential here and there still is, but unless a flood of players join this, this game is worth a little PVE now and then but not much more. in the end this game pushed me to World of Tanks and to get more into War Thunder.

Beholder is a very interesting game. So far the story is intriguing, the aesthetics are great, the gameplay is functional - some of it even good - and the user interface is horrible.
The game reminds me of the sneaking around from "This War of Mine" and the paperwork from "Papers, please" with a unique spin on the whole thing. The game have a fixed story, although with mulitple outcomes, solutions and choices that gives it quiet a bit of replayability. I find the game challenging, even in "easy" mode, and there are many ways to lose.
The basic gameplay is somewhere between resource management, 2d "stealth" and time mangement. You always have a bunch of objectives and most of them are timed, which gives an appropriate feeling of being under pressure. The stealth mechanics are very simple, but the inherit push-your-luck setup makes for decent tension. The paperwork part of the game is also very basic - nowhere near "Papers, please" - and a bit weak, although fitting for the theme. Getting enough money seems to be the biggest challenge, with many different solutions and the ressource management is pretty decent and forces you into some hard choices.
However, where the game shines for me is the story. While I find the painfully banale good/evil morality choices boring and overused, and the simplistic portrayal of a totalitarian state to be a bit cartoony, there are also many more ambigious and authetic moments. Not all victims are innocent and sometimes you just have to blackmail that criminal sailor in order to buy medicine for your daugther. You get to know your tennants and love or hate them, and I am exploring the various different storylines with great joy. Enough joy that I reccomend this game, although you might wanna read the cons down below before buying.
In my eyes, the worst part about the game are definatly the lack of a save game feature. Because the game requires a restart every time you loose the game (and that have happend to me 4 times in 6 hours of gameplay, 2 of the games played on "easy"-mode), you're going to play the same content alot, and especially the first 15 minutes or so are becoming a real pain. Which is why I recommend playing on easy.
I also find the UI obnoxious. The 2.5D hides various features and you have to zoom in and move the camera around or you might miss something. The mouseclicking is sometimes unresponsive, which is very frustrating when your trying to get your♥♥♥♥♥out of your tennats apartment before they find you with your hands in their underware drawers - at least it creates tension, but it's kinda the wrong kind. And in general the UI is way to big, ugly and unwieldy.
Be aware that although I find the game have some replayability, it is not a procedural, there are no endless mode and there's very little randomization (so far), as opposed to some of the other games in this... "Dystopian job simulator" genre? I personally see this as a strength, but reading other reviews not everyone does :).
Oh, and by the time of this review, I'm 6 hours in with restarts, and still havn't finished the game - I get the feeling there's still quiet a bit to get through.

The game Beholder is centered on ludonarrative, (where the idea of the game is the what the player feels, not what's happening in the game) not unsimilar to Papers, Please, which this game seems to take a minor bit of inspiration of. That's good and all, but it can lead to a game that's more fun to WATCH than to play
This could *possibly* be more circumvented by having the ENTIRE point of the game being centered on said ludonarrative, or having more freedom with choices.
While the game does make a big deal out of choices being meaningful, it has a lot of sitting and waiting, where "not giving this character a gun in 48 hours," doesn't feel like it has weight, or is meaningful. It doesn't make sense for a time limit to happen, and I personally think that if it were entirely removed. I understand why it's there, an anti-frustration feature, but it takes away from the theme of the game. For the specific moment I mention, a character asks you to get a gun for them. If you don't get it for them, they die. But how do they die, exactly? Well, it goes like follows:
1) HUGE exclamation point over the character
2) Asks for gun
3) Don't give her the gun
4) Another exclamation point comes over the character
5) Upon talking to the character, they move out then die
The problem with that, though, is that it feels like the world happens because of the player, not around the player. The game would be a lot more atmospheric is that the character approaches you, asks for help, and has 48 hours before dying, but the timer is hidden. Upon the time limit being over, she dies in her appartment; you get to see her die, not just get a newspaper about it.
If you do give her the gun, however, the character's EX comes in and she murders them in cold blood. You get a telegram a little bit later, thanking you. I, again, personally think that it should've happened randomly. Like, you give her the gun, and several days later, the EX comes-- not just a couple minutes after you give her the gun.
Outside of that, however, the art style/artistic direction/music compliment the games atmosphere. However, the atmosphere feels more like a joke-- a parody of a 1984 at times, but it's played completely seriously. All in all, this game has an good theme, artistic direction and overall style, but the game itself falls short even for what it's trying to accomplish with its gameplay. I can't reccomend it to an average player.
However, I still walked out of playing this game enjoying it. I love it! But, it definitely needs some improvement in some minor- but important- places. Thank you for the devs being so awesome!

This game is built around an incredibly interesting concept, and executed quite well.  I do, however, feel there are a handful of glaring shortcomings that  hold this game back from being a 10/10.  I will do my best to summarize these without spoiling anything, but if you like to go into a game fairly blind, please read at your own risk.
1) This game is incredibly short
- You will likely find your first few playthroughs of Beholder quite difficult, and will have to restart or replay the game to experience all of the different story variations.  While that in itself is great, I've managed to get through most of them in my twelve hours played.  This game eventually comes to an abrupt stop, disallowing any continued play on that file (other than the few things you can do leading up to your ending).  Ultimately, this means that this game is basically on a timer from start to finish, which brings me to my next point...
2) This game is incredibly linear
- As you'll likely find in your first couple playthroughs, the first bit of the story is quite linear and allows for little deviation.  While you can manipulate the means to which you do things, the end is still the same.  Even once the game opens up, and allows more choices, you are still on a timed track through the game, with the main objective(s).  Personally, I find this to be a drawback, as I enjoy drastic differences based on the decisions I've made.  Not to say that there aren't ANY, but they are few and far between.
3) The English version is riddled with mistakes
- I realize some may find this petty, but it REALLY interferes with my ability to immerse myself in a video game.  While a lot of the dialogue 'fits', it's set to very poor grammar and unrealistic responses, which are likely due to a loss in translation.  The few times you hear any actual speaking in the game, after the initial cutscene, it is done by a heavily accented voice that makes a plethora of mistakes in it's pronounciation of words.  While this isn't a deal-breaker on it's own for me, it's definitely something to note.
In conclusion:  This game is incredibly fun, and is great if you're looking for a shorter game you can blow through multiple times quickly, in order to see how your decisions impact the characters and finale.  This is a fantastic concept, and I hope to see the developers expand upon it to see it reach it's full potential.

TL:DR Far from ready.  Get Madden 08 for the PC instead.
I love football.  I particularly love coach-mode franchise football.
It is great that someone is making a football game for the PC.  The problem is that this is just a terrible game.
This game would be acceptable (if very flawed) if there were no other options and this was somewhere in the 90's.  But even in the 90's there were better options (front page sports pro football 98,  for example).
This part here is the deal breaker for me:
I have not seen such a limited sports game UI since the 90s.
The ability to customize things or even see the most basic of info is very limited.  You can't even view depth charts.  You can't view your roster.  You can't view your playbook (except for in game).  You can't change your playbook.  You can edit players, but the values are very limited.  You can not edit players in franchise mode.
The play calling UI is ok.  Although many of the plays stink and most of the ones I have grown used to in other games are missing.
The player subsitution model is bad, but acceptable.
The ability to sim a week is missing.  You own the team?  You must play every game.
The graphics are very very bad:
I could live with bad graphics if the game were otherwise worth a darn.  The ball bounces like it is made of flubber.  The player animations are very crude and often make no sense.  For example, a player is considered to be blocking another player if they are touching.  Most of the time one of my defenders would stand with his butt to the quater back  hold hands with an offensive player.  Player models are far too large for the field.  They bounce around, sometimes flying away like a bad skyrim glitch.
If you want a PC football game, which is much much better, get Madden 08.  It is available DR free as a DL purchase from amazon.

After the crash, we decided to tunnel into the mountain and create a shelter underground, which at the time seemed like a great idea. Sadly, our fortress turned out to be our tomb. The decision to forgoe planting and sowing crops was also a foolish one. The densely wooded area was teeming with wildlife, and our regular hunting trips always provided ample sustinence. In a pinch we could always depend on the myriad of berry bushes as well. After much expansion and growth, things seemed to be turning around, but then winter came. Our food supplies had dwindled away, due to frivilous use on prisoners from our obsessive need to expand. When we went out to forage and hunt, the reality of it hit. All the berry bushes were withered and dead, and the animals had all embarked on their winter exodus.
Realizing our fatal error we quickly constructed large structures to house crops. The cold and sparse sunlight would make it impossible to sow crops any other way. Starvation set in, and the hunger pangs were crippling. There were so many corpses outside from past raids, but we refused to become cannibals. Somehow we made it long enough for our potato crops to sprout, and in desperation we harvested them early while they were still adolescent. Somehow the whole damn harvest only provided us with 10 meals, mainly due to Steve, who possessed the winning combination of both the greedy and jealous trait. He must have eaten a quarter of the raw crop before our cook could prepare it all.
It wasnt long before our supply was spent and starvation set in yet again. Before we could go out to prematurely harvest the next batch, a man hunting Warg pack entered out lands, and rushed our fortress. We all quickly ran inside, and forbid the door. They started ramming against the walls and door, and then they retreated to sprint in circles out front, howling, taunting us. We were now effectively trapped. We were already beaten and weak from the harsh winter, there was no way we could take on a pack of five wargs. Of course our wood supply also was spent and the inside of our fort dropped to 10 degrees. We chopped up the chess tables we just built to make fire, but we still had no food. The choice was simple, either wait until starvation and cabin fever overtook everyone and die slowly, or to face the beasts outside and eat their corpses.
It didnt go too well, the Wargs finished us off easily, and the story was over. Farthest Ive made it so far, next time Ill try a desert area instead of the Boreal Forest.

An absolutely brilliant game, and one of the best single player first person shooters I've ever played.
Smooth, responsive, and satisfying gunplay, a wonderfully diverse pantheon of weapons (many of which have secondary modes of fire that essentially turn them into new weapons), and delightfully gory deaths and animations make the gameplay an absolute blast, whether you decide to play as a stealthy assasin, a dual-wielding berserker, or anything in between. A mix of old-school design sensibilities and modern polish makes for a refreshing and unique combo that more games could learn to model.
What really suprised me about this game, however, was the story. It's good. Really good. At least, compared to the majority of first person shooters out there. It's powerful. It's dramatic. It's got touches of levity where it's needed.
And most importantly, it gives the game a soul. Something warm, and distinct, that keeps it from being generic and forgettable. It's half the reason I like the game so much, honestly. It's got a soul. You don't see that all that often in AAA productions nowadays.
All in all, this is one I highly recommend. If you like intense shooting, tense stealth, old-school game elements, captivating stories, alternate history fiction, or just slaughtering hordes of Nazi scum, try it. It's good.

NOTE: This review is for the latest version, currently v.0.81.
Very fun game, a plataformer with some rogue-like elements. It chooses to follow the old school 8-bit look and does that very well. In game you can see references to other games, like Binding of Isaac and Mario.
I see much potential and recommend this game. All the current problems can be justified by the fact that the game is still in development.
The controls are very responsive, which is essential to have fun on a game like this. The difficulty level can be challenging for a casual player, took me a few attempts to finish the game. I wouldn't call this game hard, but it will kill you quite a few times until you learn the patterns and traps.
The game flows nicely and you can jump right back to action after each death. Even though this is early access, it's very polished and I found no bugs or crashes.
The current trailer reflects very well the gameplay.
Right now the main thing lacking is content, but that is expected since it's a game on early access.
We only have 4 bosses and 8 stages, that can get boring after some hours. Some items appear to have no function or no clear explanation (sadly, many roguelikes follow this "trend"). Steam achievements are still not implemented. The story is incomplete, there is no ending and no reward for finishing the game, I would like to see some element of progression, like new perks or characters.
You can find some spelling errors here and there and the game could use more balancing. Some items are too powerful, the guitar can kill the last boss in 3 hits. Again, remember this game is IN DEVELOPMENT, so all those issues could be fixed soon.

As an RTS veteran from back to the original C+C, I reviewed this game on the Vanilla version and recommended it because of its superior A.I in the genre (really adapts and challenges you and is very scalable) and its solid resource/unit mechanics and visuals.
Its faults back then were a slight lack of unit variety, a couple of U.I issues and its lack of complex tactical options like stealth or naval units.
I'm back to say Escalation is a solid step in the right direction and well worth the purchase for new or returning players (only 20 dollars for returning).
It did a great job fixing the slight wonkiness of army management and the strategic zoom really helps considering the games huge map scale that only keeps getting bigger (I will say my computer is not a fan at all of the ever-increasing on-screen army sizes lol)
More importantly, though, Escalation adds new defense options with upgradable turrets, and new ways to break that defense with strategic aircraft. Both were sorely neeed to give some variety to unit choices and strategies, and with the 3+ additional ground units added per faction as well, there is now a very solid tactical foundation for the game with several strategies one could decide on and change on the fly. I am really pleased by how much they added without flooding the game with units. I have completed all but the last mission of the campaign and its well balanced this time around. The devs have certainly learned from their early hiccups and that is a very good sign!
That being said, on to the downsides. Though the Global Abilities (like C+C Generals commander skills) have been given a once over and several new and cool things added to your arsenal there, I can't really say that a new tactical "layer" was added. Warping in units and defenses on the fly was always in Vanilla. Its just better and more thought out here.
There are still not any stealth mechanics, naval units or burrowing units in the game, and it slightly suffers because of this. That does give the sense that there is plenty of places to go from here, but be prepared to invest in that development too, as the devs have shown that paid DLC is their drive for continuing to enhance the game. The stand-alone part was just to get another shot a review scores after those enhancements go live.
I, for one, am completely willing to invest in the game. Its the shot in the arm RTS needs with Starcraft II's bar of entry so high and, so far, the paid content has been well worth it.

While space opera has enjoyed a literary resurgence, the genre is not particularly well-represented in gaming. Ten years since its release, Nexus: The Jupiter Incident remains the best of the genre, and its longevity can be attributed to three main things: 1) The gameplay, story and setting are top-notch, 2) The graphics stand the test of time, even a decade later, and 3) The game's loyal fanbase has produced some truly spectacular mods, including a Battlestar Galactica mod that is far superior to any of the officially-licensed games released for that franchise. Nexus features space combat on a grand scale -- battles stretch across systems and light minutes, weaponry is extremely varied and has real strategic value, and tactics matter much more than in other space combat games. The decisions you make during engagements can produce wildly varying outcomes, and the game's missions require you to think about how you approach targets, which weapons you deploy, which ships you place in the line of fire, how you prioritize targets, and how you utilize the variety of equipment and ship modifications available to your flagship and fleet.
Nexus: The Jupiter Incident isn't a game for people who want dogfighting in space, and it's not the type of game that can be mastered with a five-minute tutorial. While some people find the learning curve off-putting, for those of us who are fans of the game, its depth is part of what makes it special. When Nexus was released, there wasn't anything like it. A decade later, that statement still holds true.

OVERAL OPINION: Not worth the effort (at least not yet)
This game having a 90%+ approval rating is not accurate. That is the main reason I'm submitting this review. This is my opionion, yours may differ and that's fine. I'm not trying to pick a fight here but I honestly believe that even for the asking price this game does not yet offer a good enough value proposition to warrant a purchase.
I bought this is part of a bundle for under $2. I love indie games of this genre (e.g. Rogue legacy) but I still don't want to play this since there are free games that are better. I believe this should not yet be on early access since it's too unpolished and does not offer anything novel to set it apart (it's painfully generic). The animations are close to static for sprite character movement (shifting a few pixels when walking an "floating" up ladders). I am also not given a reason to care for the game or the unnamed characters in it and I have no idea what is actually happening in the story. At least there could be some dialog or a "note from the developer" at the beginning that lays out the direction of the game and its goals.
In light of this, consider the write up for the game by the developer:
"The story is about an enamoured Young Man who dared to go and ask the King for his Daughter's hand in marriage . But he is just a roturier and an Executioner is commanded to behead the young man. That very moment, a Evil Mage bursts into the castle and kidnaps the King. Our fearless hero rushes to the beast's lair to outfiht[sic] it and prove that he is worthy of blessing. There are several game's endings which depend on quantity of attempts and chosen routes (there is some branching in the structure of the castle so a gamer should to make a choice)."
Why is that not in the game?
If the animations are improved and some sort of dialog is added to the story section (or at least a a more elaborate set piece) that would already help immensely. To the developers: Please get a domain name so your support email isn't
it evokes the feeling that you either A) Don't care enough about the game to register a domain or B) Don't have the money to maintain a basic hosting (which is very worrisome and does not bode well for the game).
The different characters play differently and does give some variety but ultimately this game still needs an incredible amount of work (even for a greenlight project). I'll be happy to see this game reach it's potential. In a sea of incredible indie game, ambitious greenlight projects and deep digital special this one just does not measure up.

Enjoy kart racing games? Buy this game right now.
One of the most addictive, funstrating kart racers I've ever played. I would normally describe it as a Mario Kart clone, but it's so well-done and polished that that description just wouldn't do it justice. There's something about S&ASRT that I find really satisfying, but I don't quite know how to describe it. Maybe I'm just a sucker for kart racers.
As far as gameplay goes, it's pretty standard. There's a number of playable Sega (and a few non-Sega) characters to choose from, each with their own stats (speed, acceleration, handling, etc.). There are item boxes on the track that contain weapons and traps. Boosts are placed around the track that you can drive over, and you can do a number of flips and rolls while in midair to gain a boost when you land.
What sets Sonic Racing apart from Mario Kart are the bits of track that cause your vehicle to transform (although I haven't yet tried Mario Kart 8 at the time of writing). Sometimes you'll be driving on land, sometimes you'll be flying in the air, and sometimes you'll be driving a boat. Each of the vehicles handles differently, so adjusting on the fly gives the game a little extra challenge.
Both local multiplayer and online multiplayer are options, and you can even play online with your local friends. For singleplayer, there are Time Trials, Grand Prix, and Career Mode, where you face sets of races and other driving challenges.
Good:
+ Handful of callbacks to older Sega titles like NiGHTS and Golden Axe.
+ Every character has different stats, and the more you play a certain character, the more 'mods' you unlock which slightly change their stats. So, say you really like Shadow but you wish that he handled better. Then you can pick Shadow with the Handling Mod. This allows you to pick the character you like with the set of stats you like. This is especially important in multiplayer when players aren't allowed to pick the same character, but they can at least play with similar stats.
+ There are some tracks that have forks, and each path is favorable for different karts. Sometimes there will be one path that transforms you to a boat while the other transforms you to a plane. This gives players even more choice to pick which path is best suited for the kart they picked.
+ I always play with a controller, and the controls feel great. I don't know how well they translate to keyboard, though; I haven't tried.
Bad:
- Playing online has been a generally positive experience for me (aside from frustration and cussing at players who hit me with an item right before the finish line. In fact, I do that in singleplayer too.). My only gripe is that I've seen other players warp all over the place due to network lag, and that causes the physics engine to throw its hands up in confusion. I also feel like I've played with a few hackers a couple times, but I could be wrong.
- The AI drivers on Expert have ridiculously perfect aim. Okay, I don't necessarily see that as a fault in the game, but I just felt the need to complain about it.

Obviously a lot of us have been wanting a football game available via Steam for the PC for a long time.  Finally one has arrived.  Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game.  It's a nice try but falls way short of expectations.  And I wasn't expecting a Madden experience just some decent fun gameplay.
What ruined it for me....
---Computer player does not do what you expect from a real game experience.  For example, my computer opponent was on their 1 yard line on 4th down in a tied game with all 3 timeouts remaining with 2 minutes to go.  In real life that team would punt the ball, try and stop the other team to get the ball back and try to win or get to overtime.  Therefore I did what anyone would do...select a play for a punt return.  But the computer faked a punt and gained 50 yards (by running up the middle!) and ultimately won the game.  This is so unrealistic and laughable that it ruined all the fun I had up to that point.  The gameplay should be reality based.
---The graphics are substandard.  Too many players run around in circles or all over the field like they don't know what they are doing...chasing ghosts.
---The announcers are repetitive and make comments not relevant to what is happening on the field.
---Not enough customization available for creating your own league.  You can't limit the number of teams, create your own divisions, etc.  You can't change names of cities or teams or players.  Editing uniforms is very limited unless you open up files and hex editors and try to edit funky looking graphics on the screen instead of pointing and clicking on a part of the uniform and just selecting a color...very cumbersome!  I want total control of how I want to play...as advertised but not fulfilled.
Anyway, I'm requesting a refund but am open to buying a future version if things improve.

Having so much fun with this game... as far as non-NFL, non-Madden games go, this is top notch.  I've been turned off of Madden for a long time, so this game has been awesome to see progress to the point it is at now.
It's not perfect, but it's fun and that's all that really matters.  Gameplay is fast and smooth - it reminds me a bit of Tecmo Bowl back in the day.  The aimed passing is a lot of fun, I still have to get around to setting up my controller with joy2key so I can combine controller movement with mouse aimed passing... then I think I will have the perfect set up.
From all I've heard about the devs, they do a really nice job supporting and improving the game after it has been released, so I think the game will continue to get better from here on out.  I do have a few "cons" with this game, but they are not game breaking, and they definitely do not outwiegh the positives.  For one, the game is a little easy - playing on Hall of Fame, I still whip the computer by a couple of tds on 90% of the occasions.  2nd - kick and punt returning is too easy as well - a 40-50 yard return is almost assured, and KO return tds are commonplace.  WR's drop the ball a bit too often, and the CPU tends to throw a few too many picks (I picked off 9 passes in one 5 min qtr game, but that was an outlier thus far).
However, the pros destroy the cons in this game.  First off, it's a fun game of football - fast and smooth (missing an animation here or there, but all in all it plays quite well).  Secondly, the team creation mode is the best creation mode in any sports game that I have ever played in my life.  As long as you have photoshop or the Gimp, the only limit is your imagination.  It really is fantastic.
As I said, other than a few hiccups here and there, this game is worth far more than it's price tag... the uniform creator is worth that alone - sometimes I call this game "Football Player Dress-up Simulator 2017", as you can have so much fun with that aspect of the game.
All in all, it may not be Madden (yet) in terms of graphics, bells and whistles, but it's a ton of fun and I would play this over Madden 18 any day of the week.

This game is like a hamburger from McDonald's...it has bad composition but it tastes good as hell so you just keep eating it...even when you know its a crap...
But...to be honest...I like this game a lot...its a crap in a good way...there are many things why I like this game but I wont write those...I want to write something that could improve the game a little...
Firstly I want to write something about balance of classes...there are some classes you can dominate the game with closed eyes and there are classes where you have to go over and over just to find out its almost impossible for you to finish this game...and thats only on the Normal difficulty...
Balance of classes leads me to the balance of the mobs/bosses...when you start a new character boss fights are very hard and you can only hope for some easy boss to spawn...when you are level 1 (or Act 1 Normal) and there is boss with 5K hp (and you are dealing like 50 dmg) there is almost no way defeating him when he can kill you in one hit...on the other hand...when you are (lets say) level 60 (or Act 5 Nightmare) and there is boss with 14K hp (and you are dealing like 2000 dmg) you can kill him just as he spawns...I would recomend you to balance those bosses with the actual Difficulty and Act...this is making classic mobs stronger then bosses as the game goes on...esspecialy on higher dificulty than Normal...
The other thing I wont to point out is the Damage of mobs as the game scales...its easier for ranged classes to dodge traps/projectiles but for melee classes its almost impossible to dodge some attacks...you have no choice then but running through the map trying to separate mobs and kill them in fewer numbers...only hoping they drop healing orb so you can restore 10% of your hp...its really frustrating...
Now lets talk about Stats...one of the most useless/unbalanced thing in this game...there is no point investing points in damage/attack speed/damage reduction...the only stat worth maxing is Health...and its kinda useless anyway...sure you can double your HP and allow you to recieve more damage...but in the end you are going down in 2-3 hits from mobs anyway...HP is the only stat that is making you a little more sustainable...
Drop. What to say about drop...there are some epics items and some very...very useless items...i suggest to bind items to the Acts...lets say...for example: there are items giving you +10 strength and there are items giving you +200 strength...i suggest to bind those weak items to early game and put superior items to the end...it really annoys me a lot when i run through the dungeon or i kill the final boss just to find out that i have dropped only some coins or a superuseless item...while at the same time making me superstrong earlygame when i drop superior item early...this is another thing that makes this game unbalanced...
Items. this is just an addition. When i drop something i would like to know what a certain items does..everytime i drop something i dont know i have to google it...its annoying as hell...when you pres ESC you should have an acces to show you what your items do...
Grass. I reccomend to destroy the grass just by walking on it...
Boxes. I reccomend to destroy boxes in 1-2 hits...bigger boxes in more hits maybe...but it is annoying to hit multiple boxes without spells...
Potions. I reccomend that toxic potion wont kill you when you are low on HP but instead leave yout with at least 1 HP...would be great...and...i dont know how speed up potions really work...how many of can you stack? there should be some character info...
Talents. Some spells in talents dont show their damage...you should work on this...how am i supposed to know...
Bugs. One of the bugs that really grind my gears is the bug where mobs get stucked in walls...i cant run from them i have to come to them...
Info. Multiplayer. I understand that multiplayer is still in beta but would be great to work on it...i bought this game with my friends because we wanted to play the game together...now i can only play singleplayer...
Anyway...i really like this game even when it has many things that could be better in my opinion...i hope devs. would look at this and concider some of my recomendations...

Fantastic game with excellent gunplay and story. It does what very few WWII games do and put you through the terrors the Nazis inflcted on the world. Then it gives you several guns and you blow through them.
The gunplay is fantastic and everything handles with weight. Weapon variety is fairly solid, nothing too mind boggling and is good enough to make blowing through enemies feel very satisfying. The laser cutter you acquire adds really cool environmental puzzles, which helps break the pace and the occasional platforming is not too aggressive.
The graphics look meh, and I think it could've done a lot better. I own an Nvidia graphics card, so I don't run into many problems that some AMD card owners will run into, but for me, performance is fairly solid. I wish there wasn't a 60 FPS cap, but hopefully, for the sequel, this will be removed.
The health mechanics are really good and even though you have to pop in and out of cover, because your health only regenerates by 20 points, it really adds a sense of tension that just doesn't exist in other shooters. Only major complaint is that the stealth sections kind of suck and there's not a whole lot of options. Enemy detection is either too aggressive or mind bogglingly stupid.
Otherwise, this game is fantastic and is definitely worth a buy.

Difficulty: 8 Out of 10 (This game can be extremely difficult at times and should be known to be) (You will die)
Now I want to say that this game is fun but soley to people that can firstly handle it. And secondly those who already enjoy the genre. If you have never played an 8bit adventure/dungeon crawl/Rougelike game this may not be for you.
So to start I must say I got the base hero siege game as a gift the DLC however I chose to buy partially since it was on sale and partially because I enjoyed the base version of the game enough to do so.
The base game: Now as far as the game goes it's good borderline great! But there are so many issues with it bug-wise  that it's hard to get truly involved in the game and to back it up. It seems like the creator's  instead of fixing major issues with the original release of the game decided to work on extra content Making the first dlc almost unappeiling or unattractive after dealing with the inital release's  bug's. The games "Online"-Multiplayer is unavailable and is currently "in the works" however there should really be a notification that the whole game is "In progress" or should be under the "early access" catagory  because at least then people would more intimately know what they were buying into and would not feel the dampening that I and some players have felt when playing this game. One m,major issue i have with the game though is that you can get to the point where nearly no monster will phase you bosses or otherwise this can be truly annoying having no challenge it may take a long time and effort to get to that point but once you are there it may make the game rather manotonous. However as I said this game is good, It is fun Entertaining and a great installment to the 8bit top down zelda-esque dungeon crawler Or Rouge-like that the fanbase has come to love. Me and my friend's that are able to be in the same room love to play Co-Operatively grinding through dungeons and gaining new abilities for our varied character's, There are many great options in customization with character looks and skills that set you apart and a great feeling when you tactically kill a stronger boss then you should be able to kill. In all this game offers allot for not being a truly "complete work" at least it doesn't quite feel like one yet. But the amount of fun ive had with just the vannila game outweighs the care (The fact I got it free didn't hurt XD)  The true thing to note here is that the game can only get better as it goes on into production and i truly cannot wait till it's more fleshed out, It is honestly so much fun to play to me!
In closing, I whole heartedly reccomend grabing this game at least on a sale if you think you may like it.

Positives:
- Well optimized
- A few memorable characters (Klaus and Max are an interesting duo)
- Overhealing and armor is nice, and goes along way towards respecting the heritage of the game.
- Getting armor for headshots is a nice way to incentivize skillful play
- You kill nazis
Neutral:
- While the shooter foundation is solid, it doesn't really bring any new ideas to the genre. The laser cutter could have been the gravity gun of this game, but its potential is vastly underused, and merely becomes another generic weapon in your arsenal as well as a tool used for advancing plot and occasionally opening boxes.
- While the story was quite grand in its scope, i often found it difficult to suspend disbelief in its favor.
- Stealth is an option in many of the missions, but lacks options. You rarely have time to kill more than 2-3 guards before getting spotted, so stealth usually boils down to sneaking up as far as you can, killing a commander and whoever is nearest to him and hoping that there aren't more commanders in the area. This is all fine, but as a stealth purist, i would have loved to be able to complete the game using nothing but the knife (and maybe the silenced pistol?).
- I feel like the cutscenes would have been better from a 1st person perspective.
Cons:
- A lot of enemies sucked. Giant bullet sponges with automatic weapons are not really fun when your only option for fighting them is to just spam as much damage at them as you can and hope you don't get hit in the process.
- The combat is bland. Aggression is punished by the large number of hitscan wielding enemies, so what you're left with is picking off enemies one at a time from behind cover. The beforementioned bullet sponge enemies make hit and run tactics risky, as you could find yourself running into a shotgun wielding dude that takes an entire magazine of headshots to take down.
- The game was quite unbalanced. A lot of the campaign was♥♥♥♥♥♥easy (playing on Über) only broken up by a few super difficult fights involving several bullet sponge enemies
Overall it's a decent game that runs great, but is dragged down by being generally unremarkable mechanically and, to a lesser degree, story wise.

In the end, its really hard to find a match, but you should be able to get into one at least on starting tank tiers. And to make it worse, all the matches i've played have been 3v3s which is really underwhelming and not that exciting, the first team to lose a tank, has a great disadvantage.
Game is mostly focused on newer tanks, and has pretty similar unlock tree like the World of Tanks. Each tank uses its own experience points. You can buy tanks from 3 "dealers", and each dealer represents a nation, American, Russian and Korean/Chinese. They are unlocked by leveling up previous tank the tree. There are no garage slots, which is a really good thing, and you can buy as many tanks as you like. The progression seems very fast at start, i dont know how it gets later on though. There are 5 types of tanks Main Battle Tank, Tank Destroyer, Armored Fighting Vehicle, Self Propelled Gun and Light Tank
You can customize your tank with upgrades (which you unlock with exp points and some are bought for very small amount of ingame money), use different ammo types (ammo is bought with ingame money), also upgrade your armor (which offers rather good boosts like cannon rotation speed). There is also tank crew, where each member levels individually and has their own skilltree.
Sadly there isn't any cosmetic customization as far as i can see. Instead, some donator tanks have unique looks and camouflage.
Game looks pretty and combat felt okay, but you will need some practice because some parts of tank are well defended and certain types of ammo cant pierce it. You can also you use smoke grenades to hide yourself from enemies. The issue i had so far was with driving, even with 60ms it feels like there is delay when im trying to steer.
Out of few maps i've played, they look pretty, most of them are industrial zones with few buildings around and hills for hiding.
Donator currency can be used for buying few premium tanks and exp boost/skip, some tanks are sold as DLCs. There are also daily quests that reward you with lootboxes, but so far i only got exp and money from them.
It doesn't seem p2w, which is really weird for
. I kind of want to vote the yes for it, but i didnt enjoy it that much, and i dont think it will be able to gain decent playerbase.
Pros:
- Solid tank game, it is very similar to World of Tanks
- Around 100 different tanks, 5 types, and 10 tiers
- Detailed account statistics
- PvE mode
- Doesnt seem to be p2w (i didnt research premium tanks though, game says they only offer extra experience..and faster matchmaking? either way, there is no cash shop besides those tanks, only extra thing you can buy is experience skip)
- Tank animations look well polished, there are some nice looking maps too
- No garage slots
Cons:
- Very small playerbase
- Needs better tutorial for armor piercing rounds (hints during the game would be even better)
- Noticeable steering delay even with good connection and ping (maybe its crew dependent)
- Because of its small playerbase, you will usually get matched up versus people of higher tier and the matches are usually 3v3s
- So far i've played only 3 different maps, the map pool is either very small or some maps are unlocked at higher levels, maybe some maps are available only for bigger battles.
- No cosmetic customization

I'll keep it short for those of you on the fence and just tell you I've been into hardcore military sim shooters for over two decades.
This is one of the best teamwork/squad based first person shooters I've ever played. A true and worthy successor to Project Reality (realistic mod for BF2) and something every FPS player with a love for realism should own. Developers are constantly updating and refining the game too, eventually we will have attack choppers and CAS jets.
It takes all the "realism" a videogame can reasonably muster and channels it through a game that's easy to pick up, hard to master. Everything feels significantly "smoother" than anything you do in Arma III, from movement to shooting and netcode. This was built from the ground up for Multiplayer.
It goes on sale all the time, buy it and let me know if you need some introductory help, the community is great for newbies, just listen to your team and be willing to learn!
Final note:
A microphone is all but mandatory for the full Squad experience. This game is about true teamwork and the side that lacks it will almost certainly lose regardless of individual player skill.
Hope to see you on the battlefield!

First off, his game has many ups and downs. From personal experience I've had a decent amount of playtime to conclude that it is a fairly decent game. The game is very much a milsim style game, however can't compare to ARMAIII, the reason for that being is that Squad isn't as "open world", what I mean by that is that unlike ARMAIII, where you could explore the land mass, it has borders, but does give A LOT MORE space than Counter Strike, Insurgency, Day of Infamy, etc. Squad also doesn't offer weapon customizations. As many players that I've personally played with dislikes the idea, it still is a good option to have. Lastly Squad doesn't have a billion controls, as it's just borderline simple.
The best part about this game is that it runs on "Unreal Engine". What this mean is that the game runs, in some cases, more realistic than your standard point and shoot games, in other words bullet drops, distance, explosions and sounds, along with my favorite part of all milsim games is the smoke, it's not a little cloud of puff you would see in GTA or Counter Strike, its an actual trail of smoke that does something in your advantage.
This game focuses on leadership, teamwork, and partially your driving skills... Yea you read that right, driving skills. It's hard if you have never played driving sims in first person.
NOW EARLIER YOUR SAW ME TYPE "...in some cases," I mean this to some discression as I've never seen a truck catch on fire while it is submerged in deep, cold waters... In lieu of writing a detailed review where I pick apart what makes this game a work of pure genius, I'll get right to the key points that I feel make playing this game such a special experience.
Rimworld is a game of imagination. Everthing in this game lends to painting a picture in your mind's eye of what your colony is experiencing. The graphics are minimalistic, with characters/animals/mechanoids represented with simple, vector "pawns" that move on a 2d grid. Most of the depth Rimworld provides is through text in menus and alerts. The true brilliance in this representational model is that you are free to visualize with your IMAGINATION what each scene of desperate survival looks like. Its almost like reading a book, and more akin to P&P D&D, or those old text based adventure games like Zork.
In an age of hyper-realistic. AAA video games that leave nothing to the imagination. Rimworld seeks to cultivate the long lost art of creative thinking. It does so in a way that is both compelling, and (in many cases) emotional. You become attached to your pawns, colonist and animal, as well as the wellbeing of the colony itself. You are sad (or at the VERY least perturbed) when a Scyther takes your favorite colonist's head off in one shot, or your dog gets eaten by a wandering couger. The stories of Rimworld write themselves, and come to life in your mind.
Pros:
Simple aesthetic lends to imaginative interpretation of gameplay.
Highly in depth-gameplay with micromanagement that is (largely) optional until you need it.
Music is great and reminds me of Firefly (even though there are only a few tracks, I don't get tired of hearing them).
Updates about the time you finish a few runs with lots of new content and bug fixes (thank you Tynan).
TONS of replayability, custom modes, settings, mods, etc.
Mod support through the workshop that adds to and fixes base content.
Variation in difficulty with the storytellers, permadeath mode, and tradition difficulty as well as custom scenarios.
Cons:
Bigger maps aren't (yet?) optimized well, and can lead to lag on higher playspeeds and long load times.
Some bugs and oddities affect gameplay adversely.
Medical operation success rates and (inevitable) failures.
Your game does eventually end, and you are always sad to see the pawns lauch off, and the colony abandoned...

Summary: definitely my kind of game, and a non-compromising improvement on the original Ashes of the Singularity, though in catering to hardcore PC RTS enthusiasts, it might put off more casual players or those with older hardware
Technical: The Nitrous engine is fantastic, it does justice to its claim of 'first ground-up DX12 game engine' and kudos to the devs at Oxide for putting in the work to do it right.  Especially for a game of this scale it makes a noticable performance difference, which means you are fighting another player or the AI, not fighting glitches and lag. That said, this game is DEMANDING, it scales all the way from 'quite demanding' up to 'requires a supercomputer' ... take note of the hardware requirements before buying, it will slam both your GPU and CPU, a Core i7 does not go to waste.
Gameplay: it will feel familiar to hardcore RTS fans (and maybe not the most accessible title to RTS newbies), especially those who have played other Oxide-developed titles, but what sets Ashes apart is the impact of scale on strategy. Micro-management is simply not feasible in every situation, and there are plenty of tools and and AI development to minimize the required actions-per-minute. Seriously, the AI is good as an opponent, and for managing units within your armies. If you enjoy the macro aspects, this might be the game you were waiting for.
Story/theme: In the first installment, there wasn't so much to back up the sci-fi dystopian theme and brief story campaign, which is understandable for a smaller developer, and the above points were enough to win me over. Still, I was pleasantly surprised to find far more effort paid to world-building lore in the new expansion's missions. The campaign is still more like an advanced tutorial than the main course for gameplay, but it doesn't feel like *just* a tutorial any more.
Misc: Devs are super active with patches and balance tweaks (Escalation seems much improved in terms of balance), and really transparent with taking feedback from the community and their intentions, commendable practices in the software business. The community of players is understandably small for a niche game like this, but generally quite friendly and fun to play with.

Positives:
- Well optimized
- A few memorable characters (Klaus and Max are an interesting duo)
- Overhealing and armor is nice, and goes along way towards respecting the heritage of the game.
- Getting armor for headshots is a nice way to incentivize skillful play
- You kill nazis
Neutral:
- While the shooter foundation is solid, it doesn't really bring any new ideas to the genre. The laser cutter could have been the gravity gun of this game, but its potential is vastly underused, and merely becomes another generic weapon in your arsenal as well as a tool used for advancing plot and occasionally opening boxes.
- While the story was quite grand in its scope, i often found it difficult to suspend disbelief in its favor.
- Stealth is an option in many of the missions, but lacks options. You rarely have time to kill more than 2-3 guards before getting spotted, so stealth usually boils down to sneaking up as far as you can, killing a commander and whoever is nearest to him and hoping that there aren't more commanders in the area. This is all fine, but as a stealth purist, i would have loved to be able to complete the game using nothing but the knife (and maybe the silenced pistol?).
- I feel like the cutscenes would have been better from a 1st person perspective.
Cons:
- A lot of enemies sucked. Giant bullet sponges with automatic weapons are not really fun when your only option for fighting them is to just spam as much damage at them as you can and hope you don't get hit in the process.
- The combat is bland. Aggression is punished by the large number of hitscan wielding enemies, so what you're left with is picking off enemies one at a time from behind cover. The beforementioned bullet sponge enemies make hit and run tactics risky, as you could find yourself running into a shotgun wielding dude that takes an entire magazine of headshots to take down.
- The game was quite unbalanced. A lot of the campaign was♥♥♥♥♥♥easy (playing on Über) only broken up by a few super difficult fights involving several bullet sponge enemies
Overall it's a decent game that runs great, but is dragged down by being generally unremarkable mechanically and, to a lesser degree, story wise.

Hero Seige is an isometric rougelike shooter with RPG elements and a fantasy theme with severl different classes to play and very addictive gameplay. You fight off enemies in increasingly dificult waves and try to collect "relics" that give you improvements to your stats or new abilities; like a familiar that shoots when enemies get in range.
For those of you who dont care about the pros and cons, I give the game a 7.5/10 and you should buy it if you're into rougelikes and their difficulty. If not, you should probably stay away.
Pros:
-The game has an interesting art style, blending a cute-ish retro pixel-built look with some creepy enemies to make a game that is very colorful and pleasing to look at.
-The gameplay pace and style varies depending on your class, making the game very replayable and fun each time you start up a run.
-Online and Local Co-Op
-Very well coded, with only one bug sighting throughout 10 hours of playing.
-RPG system makes it less upsetting when you die (which you will, alot)
-Different heads for your characters allow for slight customisation of what you look like in game
Cons:
-Lots of projectiles can get lost behind scenery or mixed in with entities in the game causing you to die from something you didn't notice very frequently.
-Visual/Audial conveyance of damage is almost non-exsitant, with a slight flash and a small sound clip of your characer going "ugh"
-Characters like to spout one-liners EXTREMELY frequently, and the voice acting is mediocre at best.
-Bosses spawn and immediately after a few seconds of a large red spiral showing up at spawn, attack, leaving you no time to react to what the boss is. This can be catastrophic to your run, as some characters will die instantly upon the bosses spawn attack.
-Some enemies can one hit you all the way up to level 40, which is really sucky if youre a melee class
Overall, the game could use some fine-tuning and balancing, but it is extremely fun. The DLC is also a great addition, and should be bought as well as the game, as it gives you a new Act and a new Class. Definately one of the stronger rougelikes, and you'll enjoy it if you're a fan of other roguelikes (i.e: The Binding of Isaac, Rogue Legacy, Risk of Rain, ect.)
